report.summary: This release rebuilds the way log messages are written and displayed in the terminal, with no intended change to what testers see, so console output needs regression checks.
keyChanges: Log-line assembly (timestamp, type label, tag, message, extra data) moved into per-reporter processing steps backed by new shared helpers for date formatting, placeholder compilation, and color resolution with caching; formatted log output is not intended to change, so any visible difference in log lines is a regression.

The output writer now takes an options object (an error flag plus a write mode of default, sync, or async) instead of a raw stream, so error entries are routed to the error output inside the writer and asynchronous writes resolve only after the stream drains; the logging entry point's second argument changed meaning from an async flag to this mode selector.

The styled reporter's console-clear action now goes through the redesigned writer without the options object the writer expects, so logging with the clear-console option enabled is the most likely regression in this group and may abort the log entirely.

Custom options passed to the default console reporter are now actually merged over the defaults; previously they were collected but never applied, so custom streams, time formats, and line formats silently had no effect, while the built-in defaults (stdout for logs, stderr for errors, HH:mm:ss timestamps) stay the same when no options are given.

Five synchronous/asynchronous write variants, the internal routine that picked between them, and the tag/message preparation step were removed in favor of one write path through a shared stream utility; normal logs must still reach stdout and error logs stderr in both modes, noting that in synchronous mode error output previously went to the default stdout handle regardless of the configured stream.

Log-line rendering moved from positional printf placeholders to named placeholders handled by new formatting and date helpers (dropping the dayjs and printj dependencies) while keeping the HH:mm:ss default timestamp, and the old code's rewriting of colons in tags into ' - ' separators now lives inside those new helpers.
The logger core now imports the same helper from a restructured module location, which is behaviorally neutral unless the path is wrong, in which case the library fails to load at all.

Log writing now goes through one output routine with three modes: plain writes, asynchronous writes that wait until the destination stream is ready before finishing, and synchronous writes direct to the stream's file descriptor; the plain reporter's output path and the styled reporter's clear and log-processing path all route through it, so all console output depends on it.

Background colors are now resolved by name or hex value and cached; the second and later lookups of the same background color name return the whole cache table instead of the single color formatter, making repeated styling with the same background color the most likely regression, and unrecognized background color names now print an error to the console.

The three built-in log layouts (a one-line layout with icon, tag, message and extra detail; a boxed layout with the type on a colored background; and a bracketed [date][type] tag message detail layout) are now served from a precompiled template table, so field order, spacing, and colors should look unchanged, and any wrong mapping would show as garbled or reordered log lines.

Text and background colors are now resolved through shared helpers that cache results for the whole process instead of per reporter instance, so named colors, hex values, and keyword fallbacks should render exactly as before, and the same color can now be reused consistently across every entry in a run.

Icon selection no longer forces an empty icon for plain log entries, so a message logged at the ordinary log level now falls back to the default ❯ marker and its spacing where the line previously began directly with the message text.

Built-in reporter settings, including the default output templates, moved into shared defaults that caller-provided options still override, so a consumer customizing only some settings keeps the built-in behavior for the rest.

The built-in templates were rewritten from numbered placeholders to named ones while keeping the same layout, and badge-style entries still highlight the level name on a colored background that previously forced the text on it to be black.
qaChecks: Verify that a log created with the clear-console option enabled still wipes the terminal screen and then prints the full log message; if the screen does not clear, an error appears, or the message is missing entirely, this is a failure.

Verify an ordinary info log still prints one line with the formatted timestamp, the uppercase type label, and the message, and that no literal placeholder fragments such as %date or %tag leak into the output.
Check a log with a namespaced tag such as server:db still renders its segments separated by the styled ' › ' separator, and a log with an empty tag still prints cleanly.
Ensure timestamps still follow the configured time format exactly as before the change.

Verify logging an Error object still shows the error message, the ERROR type label, and the indented stack lines ending with the return-arrow marker, and that this output lands on the error output channel (stderr) while a normal info log still goes to standard output.

Verify styled logs still show the correct icon per log type and apply configured text colors, testing both a hex color such as #ff0000 and a named color, and that extra detail lines render in the additional color (grey by default); a badge log should still show its highlighted colored type label.
Confirm a styled log with no custom color set still renders normally without errors.
Ensure a rapid burst of many consecutive log lines all appear completely and in order, with no missing or truncated lines, confirming asynchronous writes still flush fully.

Verify the library loads without module-resolution errors and a plain log prints to stdout in the layout [HH:mm:ss][type] message, with the type right-padded inside its brackets and the timestamp in HH:mm:ss.

Verify, with the two streams captured separately, that normal logs land on stdout and error logs (pass an Error as the argument) land on stderr in both synchronous and asynchronous logging modes; in the old code a synchronous error write went to the default stdout handle, making this the key regression check.

Verify a log issued in asynchronous mode immediately before the process exits still appears complete in the captured output, since the previous implementation explicitly waited for the stream to drain before considering the write finished.
Verify a log with a tag containing a colon, for example app:db, still renders its segments joined with ' - ' rather than showing raw colons or placeholder artifacts.
Verify the custom options now take effect: output goes to the custom stream and uses the custom time format, because before this change such options were ignored and defaults were always used.

Verify a log emitted in synchronous mode to a custom stream lands on that stream and not on stdout, since synchronous writes previously went to the default stdout handle even when another stream was configured.
Verify the two loggers keep their own settings for the whole process run with the default logger unaffected by the custom one, because the defaults are now a single shared configuration object.

Verify every mode (default, synchronous, asynchronous, and the deferred asynchronous case) completes for all sample inputs (plain string, extra string argument, array, object, Error) without crashes and with a printed line for each.
Verify log entries written with each write mode (plain, asynchronous, synchronous) all appear completely and in the right order in the output.
Check that a rapid burst of many long log lines is not truncated or dropped, since asynchronous writes must wait until the stream is ready before finishing.
Ensure error-level entries, which are routed to the error stream, are written just as reliably as normal entries.
Confirm that repeated output, including the styled reporter's screen-clear or refresh step between entries, keeps producing output without hanging or losing lines.

Verify two consecutive entries styled with the same named background color both render with that exact background color and neither fails or falls back to unstyled text, because later lookups of the same color currently return the wrong value.
Check that a background color given as a hex value starting with # renders with that exact color.
Ensure an unrecognized background color name prints a clear error message and the log line itself still appears rather than the output crashing.

Verify the built-in layouts still print every field in order: the one-line layout with icon, tag, message and extra detail, the boxed layout with the type on a colored background, and the bracketed [date][type] tag message detail layout.
Check that the same layout used repeatedly renders identically each time, since built-in layouts are now reused from a precompiled table.
Ensure a custom layout keeps its fields, colors, and spacing in the intended places.

Verify that a message logged at the plain log level with no custom icon now begins with the default ❯ marker followed by the message, where before this change such a line began directly with the message text, and confirm the new marker keeps the line readable and aligned with other entries.

Verify that info, success, error, warn, debug, and start entries still show their usual symbols (ℹ, ✔, ✖, ⚠, …, ●) and that an entry carrying a custom icon still shows that icon instead of the built-in one.

Verify that each entry still renders in the established order of icon, tag, message, and additional details on the following line, with no raw placeholder tokens, stray escape characters, or missing colors, including when output is redirected to a file where colors are disabled.
Verify that named, keyword, and hex colors still render with the intended text color on normal entries now that color resolution runs through the shared cached helpers.

Check that badge-style entries still draw a colored background block behind the level name and that the text on that block stays readable in both light and dark terminals, since the block previously forced black text.

Verify that a consumer overriding only its icons still gets the built-in output templates and level labels, and that one overriding only the templates still gets the built-in icons, since defaults are merged underneath caller options.
Verify that fully custom templates still render correct lines for both normal and badge-style entries.

Verify that with logging set to asynchronous, writing a burst far larger than the output buffer, such as ten thousand lines piped into a slow reader, still holds each log call open until the buffer has drained - before this release the dedicated asynchronous writer waited for the drain signal before finishing; confirm the new writer still waits and the timing is intended.

Check that logging the single word hello still prints one line with the time in square brackets and the level name, and that the stray 4$s text which used to appear in the middle of every line before this release is now gone - confirm the cleaned-up line layout is intended.

Confirm that logging a normal message and an error message, each once with logging set to synchronous and once with asynchronous, still sends normal lines to the normal output and error lines to the error output in all four combinations - before this release a small internal chooser picked a dedicated writer for each combination and that chooser is now gone; confirm the single consolidated writer handles all four as intended.

Check that with the logger's output pointed at a custom file in its settings and logging set to synchronous, a normal log line now lands in that custom file - before this release the line was always written to standard output no matter what the setting said; confirm the custom file is now used as intended.

Verify that a message logged with a namespaced tag such as server:api shows the tag the new way - before this release the colons were rewritten into dash separators with an extra dangling separator left at the end, so the tag printed as server - api - ; confirm the new tag formatting is intended.

Check that with logging set to synchronous and both outputs redirected into the same file, an error line logged first and a normal line logged second now appear in that order when you open the file - before this release the error line went through a buffered writer and the normal line was written straight in, so the normal line could land above the error line; confirm the corrected ordering is intended.

Verify that when the logger is started with a custom time format setting, for example hours and minutes only, the timestamps on printed lines now follow that setting - before this release custom settings were silently ignored and lines always showed the default hours-minutes-seconds time; confirm honoring the setting is intended.

Confirm that with asynchronous logging and the error output piped to a slow reader, a flood of error lines such as a loop of a thousand still holds each log call open until the error buffer drains - before this release a dedicated asynchronous error writer waited for that drain before finishing; confirm the consolidated writer behaves the same on purpose.

Verify that with the normal output redirected into a file, the error output left on the terminal and logging set to synchronous, an error message now shows up on the terminal's error output - before this release the error line was written into the redirected file because the error destination was overlooked in this mode; confirm the corrected destination is intended.
uncertainty: The screen-clear action in the styled reporter calls the redesigned output writer without the options object the writer now requires, so any log created with the clear-console option may throw an error and print nothing at all (screen not cleared, message lost); treat a failure of the first check as the release's most likely regression.

Exact log-line rendering cannot be fully confirmed from the evidence: the previous default template appears to have contained a malformed fourth placeholder, and the old tag handling (colons rewritten into ' - ' separators) now lives in new formatting helpers whose behavior is not in the evidence, so the deciding test is a side-by-side capture of the same log calls, including a colon-containing tag, against the previous release.

No previous version of any changed function was supplied (all diffs are additions), so old-versus-new inputs could not be derived and the checks target the new behavior itself; the repeated-background-color anomaly is evident in the new code, but no direct callers of that helper appear in the supplied dependency evidence, so its user-visible reach depends on which reporters style entries with named background colors.
No application context was generated for this repository, so no pages, routes, or navigation steps could be supplied and all guidance is framed around console output.

report.summary: This release reworks how drawings are rendered on the canvas, so the main risk is drawings that look or restore incorrectly after everyday viewing and editing actions.
keyChanges: Shapes, lines, arrows, and text on the editor canvas are now drawn from a per-element cached image with 20 pixels of padding, regenerated only when the zoom level changes; the editor turns this optimization on while scene exports keep the previous exact path, which the change itself notes is not pixel-perfect under the fast path.

The scene renderer's options changed: per-call scroll offset overrides were removed and a render-optimizations flag was added (on in the editor, off for exports), and zoom handling was consolidated into paired apply-and-restore helpers that now wrap element, selection-outline, and resize-handle drawing.

The cached image is keyed only by zoom, so an element edited after it was first drawn at the same zoom can keep showing pre-edit pixels; text edits are the case this rendering change alone cannot invalidate, because a text element's cache is only regenerated on a zoom change.
When selection rendering is on (the editor default), the scene render now returns before painting scrollbars, so scrollbars no longer appear on the editor canvas; confirm this removal is intended.
Arrows and lines are cached using their full bounding box with corner offsets, so arrows drawn in any direction must land exactly where drawn, arrowhead included.

A new whole-number (floored) scroll rule now applies everywhere view coordinates are computed: mouse-wheel panning, scrollbar dragging, scroll-to-content centering when a scene loads, and export positioning, so positions can differ from before by at most about one pixel.

The interactive canvas now renders with render optimizations enabled, which the renderer itself flags as not guaranteeing pixel-perfect output, and resizing the browser window now clears cached per-element render shapes so all elements redraw after a resize.

Autosave to the browser no longer removes temporary selection elements before saving (previously they were filtered out), so a selection rectangle could now be persisted to local storage and come back on reload.

Canvas-based exports (PNG and copy-to-clipboard, plus the export preview) now position the drawing using floored scroll values instead of a raw fractional offset, so drawings with half-pixel element coordinates can shift by up to one pixel in the exported image.

Loading scenes from files, share links, or saved browser drafts now clears cached render shapes/canvases and defaults missing canvas offsets to 0, forcing every restored element to be freshly rendered.

Elements copied or cut inside the app, undone/redone, or saved to browser storage are now serialized without an internal per-element canvas cache: the in-app clipboard payload excludes it, undo/redo snapshots now store it as null instead of keeping whatever the element held, and browser autosave strips it too, so restored content must come back fully rendered with no stale-cache artifacts.

The canvas renderer's separate zoom-scale and zoom-translate helper steps were removed and folded into a single apply/reset zoom routine used by both the live canvas and image exports; this is expected to be behavior-neutral, but every render now passes through the reworked path.

Scroll offsets are now standardized as whole (floored) numbers across app state and scene definitions, and the image export path normalizes its offsets the same way; verify exports and panned canvases show no sub-pixel shift, blur, or clipped edges.

All three ways of moving the view — mouse wheel, panning by dragging, and dragging the on-canvas scrollbars — now round the scroll position down to a whole number where fractional positions were previously kept; because each update is rounded and sub-pixel leftovers are discarded, a very small scroll tick can now jump a full pixel in one direction while producing no movement in the other.

Since stored scroll positions are now whole numbers, the pointer-to-canvas coordinate mapping can differ by up to about one pixel from before, which matters when clicking precisely on element edges at high zoom.

Every newly created element, including the text element made when pasting clipboard text, now initializes canvas-cache placeholders (empty cache, cache zoom fixed at 1, zero offsets), and text elements explicitly reset their cached shape; this prepares per-element cached rendering and runs on all element-creation and paste paths.
Scrollbar and coordinate-conversion code now formally expects whole-number scroll values; no behavior change is expected there, and the image-export pipeline shares this code path.

Verify that editing an existing multiline text element in place, without changing zoom, updates the on-canvas text immediately, including text pasted with Windows-style line breaks still shown as separate lines.
Check that changing an existing shape's stroke color or opacity shows on the canvas immediately without a zoom change.
Verify elements stay sharp and correctly positioned while zooming in and out across several levels (for example 50% to 200%) and back, with no blur or offset from where they were drawn.
Test arrows and lines drawn in every direction, including from bottom-right to top-left, and confirm the full stroke and arrowhead render without clipping or a slight positional shift.

Check that the dashed outline and corner resize handles around a selected element align exactly with the element at a non-default zoom such as 200%, and that dragging a selection rectangle highlights exactly the area dragged.
Ensure elements render crisply on a high-DPI (retina) display, since the cached path scales by the device pixel ratio.
Verify an exported PNG or JPEG matches the on-screen drawing: complete elements with padding around the content, multiline text on separate lines, and the arrow fully drawn with its head.
Check that an SVG export contains the shapes and text with correct colors and opacity.
Test copying the drawing to the clipboard produces the same complete image.

Verify whether scrollbars still appear on the editor canvas when the drawing extends beyond the visible area; they are no longer painted after this change, so confirm this is the intended new behavior.
Ensure the indication shown when every element has been scrolled out of view still appears, since the renderer's visible-elements result drives it.

Verify that drawing, dragging, resizing, and zooming elements still renders everything correctly on the main canvas with no elements disappearing, flickering, or drawing misaligned, since live rendering now uses optimizations that do not guarantee pixel-perfect output.
Test resizing the browser window while elements are on the canvas; every element should redraw cleanly afterwards with no stale, doubled, or distorted strokes.

Test dragging a selection box over elements and then immediately closing or reloading the tab; after reopening, confirm the drawing restores normally with no stray empty rectangle or leftover selection artifact saved as an element.
Verify that normal edits persist across a page reload: edit, wait a moment, reload, and confirm all elements and the view come back as left.
Verify opening a previously saved drawing file renders every element (shapes, lines/arrows, text) correctly, including elements lacking stored canvas offset data.
Confirm opening a share link loads the complete scene centered on its content with nothing missing or misdrawn.

Test exporting the drawing as PNG and copying it to the clipboard with half-pixel element coordinates; the exported image should contain the complete drawing with padding intact and nothing clipped at the edges, allowing for up to a one-pixel shift versus previous output.
Check that the preview image shown in the export dialog matches the drawing on the canvas.

Verify mouse-wheel scrolling and scrollbar dragging pan the view in the correct direction at different zoom levels without jumping or content misalignment, now that view positions snap to whole pixels.
Confirm newly loaded scenes center on the drawing content as before, within about one pixel.
Verify copy and paste: select previously drawn elements, copy, then paste; each duplicate appears fully rendered with the same strokes, fill, and size, and can be moved, edited, and copied again.
Verify cut: cut the selection so the elements disappear, then paste; they return fully rendered with nothing blank, ghosted, or duplicated.

Verify copy right after zooming or panning: copy an element while the canvas is zoomed or scrolled, then paste; the duplicate must still render identically, since stale internal cache data would show as blank or misdrawn shapes.

Verify the undo/redo round trip: draw several elements, undo back to an empty canvas, then redo forward; every restored element looks exactly as it did before the undo, with no blank, doubled, or distorted shapes.
Verify repeated undo and redo on an element that was just moved or zoomed; it redraws correctly at every step.
Verify auto-save and reload: draw elements, wait a few seconds for the delayed save, then reload the page; the drawing and its view position restore and all elements render and remain editable.
Verify save on tab close: make a change and close the tab immediately, then reopen; the latest change is present.
Verify that a drawing saved by the previous version still loads and renders correctly after this update.

Verify zoom rendering: at roughly 50%, 100%, and 200% zoom, draw and select elements; shapes, selection handles, and scrollbars stay aligned with the content with no shift, blur, or leftover artifacts.
Verify panning while zoomed: pan the canvas at high zoom; content tracks the pointer correctly and stays crisp.
Verify export content: export the drawing as PNG and SVG; the output contains every element in place with the chosen background and even padding on all sides.
Verify edge placement: after zooming and panning so the drawing sits at odd offsets, export again; nothing is clipped or shifted by about a pixel at the borders.

Test scrolling with several small trackpad ticks at 200% zoom in both directions: the view must move in both directions and settle on whole-pixel offsets, because tiny fractional movements no longer accumulate between ticks and one direction may fail to move at all.
Check panning by dragging across empty canvas and then clicking exactly on an element's edge: the element visually under the cursor should be the one that becomes selected.
Ensure dragging the horizontal and then the vertical scrollbar moves the view smoothly in step with the pointer and the view stays where it was left when the drag ends.
Verify drawing shapes with each tool plus a text item, then zooming between 50% and 200%: every element should re-render crisply and keep its exact position.
Check drawing a rectangle starting exactly at a visible reference point at 150% zoom after panning: the shape should begin directly under the cursor, not offset by about a pixel.
Test copying text from another application and pasting onto the canvas while zoomed and panned: a text element should appear at the cursor, be selected, render correctly, and stay editable.
Confirm copying several existing elements and pasting: duplicates should appear centered under the cursor with their relative spacing preserved.
Validate exporting a drawing that extends beyond the visible area as PNG: the exported image should match the on-canvas content without scrollbar artifacts or shifted layout.
Check that drawing an arrow going up and to the left from where you start shows the entire arrow including its head with nothing clipped, just as before this release, and confirm that is intended.
Verify that typing text on the canvas and pressing Enter to start a second line still shows every line on its own row exactly as it did before this release, and confirm that is intended.

Check that dragging a shape in very small steps still moves it smoothly across the canvas: before this release it moved in fractions of a pixel, and it now snaps to whole pixels, so confirm that slight stepping is intended.

Verify that making the window smaller or scrolling so part of the drawing sits outside the canvas no longer shows the scrollbars that used to appear along the edges before this release, and confirm that removal is intended.

Verify that dragging a selection rectangle across the canvas makes the light-blue highlight start and end exactly where you press and release the mouse, matching how it looked before this release, and confirm that is intended.

Confirm that opening and using the editor normally still renders the drawing exactly as before this release, since the module-level change only adds constants and imports that feed the new rendering routines.

Check that zooming in and out with the mouse wheel on a drawing containing text and shapes redraws everything sharp at the new zoom rather than leaving it blurry or misplaced, and confirm that is intended.
Confirm dragging an element or scrollbar still tracks the mouse accurately and does not introduce visual offset or lag.
Confirm panning by dragging the canvas still feels responsive and the drawing does not jitter or blur during the drag.

Verify that zooming the canvas in and out with the mouse wheel still scales the whole drawing correctly and keeps it lined up with its selection outlines and resize handles, exactly as before this release.

Check that opening a drawing file saved by an older version of the app still shows every shape in the right place with the usual hand-drawn look — loading now clears each element's stored rendering and assumes a zero offset whenever none was saved, where before whatever the file contained was reused untouched.

Verify that exporting a drawing to a PNG image still frames every shape with an even margin of empty space — the export now positions the content using a rounded-down scroll offset instead of a separate raw offset, so a drawing at fractional coordinates can end up to one pixel off inside the saved image compared with the previous release.
Confirm a newly drawn shape can still be moved, resized and deleted normally and its appearance on the canvas is unchanged.

Confirm that panning the canvas with the mouse wheel or a trackpad still moves the drawing smoothly — each scroll step is now rounded down to whole pixels, so tiny trackpad nudges that used to creep the view along bit by bit can now be swallowed entirely or jump a full pixel at once.

Verify that selecting a shape while the canvas is zoomed to twice its normal size still draws its dashed outline and corner handles at their normal on-screen size and position, as before this release, and confirm that is intended.
uncertainty: Whether something outside this group clears the new per-element cached image when an element is edited at an unchanged zoom is not shown here; shapes reset their cache whenever their geometry is regenerated, but a text element's cache is keyed only to zoom, so if nothing else resets it, edited text keeps showing pre-edit pixels until the zoom changes - the edit-after-draw checks above settle this.

The renderer's own documentation states optimized rendering does not guarantee pixel-perfect output, and the exact cases where the optimized on-screen canvas differs from the previous rendering are unknown; compare thin strokes, text, and small zoom levels carefully while editing.

The zoom helper consolidation appears to be a straight refactor and the type/import-only edits (whole-number scroll offsets, new imports) have no runtime effect by themselves; no specific input was identified that the old and new renderer treat differently, so the zoom and export checks are smoke tests guarding the shared rendering path rather than probes of a known behavioral difference.

New elements now carry canvas-cache placeholders whose cache zoom is fixed at 1, but the rendering code that consumes this cache is not part of this group's evidence; if cache reuse ignores the current zoom, elements could appear stale or blurry after zooming — the zoomed-rendering checks above cover the visible symptom.

report.summary: This release adds the ability to rotate elements in the drawing editor, with rotation now consistently respected when selecting, resizing, editing, viewing, and exporting, while unchanged, unrotated behavior stays the same.
keyChanges: Selecting a single element now shows a circular rotation handle above it; the corner and side resize handles and the dashed selection outline rotate to match the element's angle, and selected text now shows the rotation handle while still offering no resize handles.

Handle hit-testing changed to check the rotation handle first and then the resize handles, so on a rotated element the grab points sit at the visually rotated corners instead of the old unrotated positions; the resulting rotation drag is picked up by the canvas pointer logic.
Element drawing now applies the element's angle on both the fast cached path and the detailed redraw path, so elements with a rotation angle render rotated on the canvas instead of axis-aligned.

Content bounds now enclose rotated corners instead of the raw rectangle, so image and SVG exports are sized to fit rotated shapes, pasted rotated elements center on the cursor, and scroll-to-content centering and scrollbar indicators reflect the full rotated extent.

Selected elements now have a rotation handle: dragging it rotates the element around its center, holding Shift snaps rotation to 22.5-degree steps, the angle wraps cleanly through a full turn, and the cursor over that handle is the horizontal double-arrow instead of the default arrow.

Resizing is now rotation-aware: on a rotated element, each corner and edge handle keeps the opposite side anchored instead of letting the shape drift, and Shift still forces the height to equal the width; for elements that were never rotated the new math reduces exactly to the old behavior, so existing resizing should feel unchanged.

A transient rotation flag was added to editor state: it defaults to false, resets the moment the pointer is released, and is stripped from browser-stored state, so a reloaded session never resumes mid-rotation; drawings saved to files or the backend now also carry this flag as false.

Restored content is angle-safe: elements loaded from files, browser autosave, shared links, and live collaboration updates now default to 0 degrees when no angle is stored, so drawings made before this release load upright and editable.

The text editing overlay now tilts to match a rotated element's angle while editing existing text, and text drawn fresh on the canvas is explicitly unrotated; this new overlay input is flagged as a contract risk if any editing entry point omits it.

Selecting an element now also shows a rotation handle above it, about 16 pixels away, and dragging it rotates the element around its center; while rotating with a mouse, a new rotate tip appears in the editor's hint area.

Clicking now reverses an element's rotation before hit testing, so tilted elements are selected where they visually sit instead of anywhere inside their upright bounding box; previously the pointer was compared against the unrotated bounds.

Text editing follows rotation: double-clicking a tilted text element, or pressing Enter with one selected, opens the editing box rotated to match the element, where it was previously always horizontal.
The resize tip and the new rotate tip appear only when the last pointer press came from a mouse; with pen or touch, resizing no longer shows the resize tip as it did before.
Every newly created element (shapes, lines, text) now stores an angle value defaulting to 0, so drawings created from now on carry an angle field in their saved data.

SVG-based drawing export now writes each element's rotation into the output: shapes, lines and arrows, and text elements get a rotate transform around their own center in addition to the existing position offset, so an element rotated on the canvas (for example 45 degrees) now exports rotated instead of flat as before.

Zero-angle elements now also carry a no-op rotation in the SVG, which should look identical to previous exports; the risk is a position shift if the rotation center is computed wrong, so unrotated exports must be compared against the canvas.

The same render pipeline serves the editor's export dialog (SVG output prepared by the scene export helper) and the copy-drawing-as-PNG clipboard action, so both outputs must show rotated elements correctly.

The other changes in this group are non-runtime edits — an empty line in the math helpers, a type alias in the scene renderer, and a new rotation-in-progress flag in the editor's internal state type — and need no functional testing beyond a general smoke check.

Confirm that resizing a shape you have first tilted, by dragging a corner handle of for example a rectangle rotated partway, keeps the opposite corner fixed in place while the shape grows or shrinks, instead of the shape drifting sideways as happened before this release when the tilt was ignored during resizing.

Check that with a text element selected, dragging the round handle above it now tilts the text, where before this release selected text showed no handles and could not be tilted or resized at all.

Verify that when you rotate a shape on the canvas (for example turn a rectangle about 30 degrees with its rotation handle) and then export the drawing as an SVG file, the shape in the saved file comes out tilted by that same angle, where the previous release saved it upright as if it had never been rotated, and confirm this new behaviour is intended.

Check that when you drag a selected shape to a new tilt, the round handle above it swings around so it stays centered over the shape's top edge, where before this release no such handle moved with the shape.

Verify that a shape you have tilted keeps its tilt on the main canvas while you drag it and scroll around, where before this release the shape was stamped back onto the screen without its tilt and shifted by its corner rather than turning about its center.

Verify that clicking a corner handle of a tilted shape exactly where it is now displayed starts a resize, while the spot where the handle appeared before this release no longer responds, so the grab area matches what you see.

Verify that selecting everything on a canvas containing a rectangle tilted 45 degrees draws one bounding box wrapped around the tilted shape's true extents, where before this release the box hugged the untilted rectangle and cut off its corners.

Confirm that saving or exporting a drawing that contains a tilted shape produces an image with the shape tilted exactly as on screen, where before this release the exported image drew the shape upright.

Verify that clicking on the visible body of a tilted rectangle, diamond or ellipse selects the shape, where the click test used to treat the shape as upright so a click on its tilted body could miss it; confirm that clicking now matches what is actually drawn.

Confirm that when you start rotating a selected shape by dragging its rotation handle with the mouse, a hint about rotating appears in the hint area at the bottom of the canvas, where before this release nothing appeared there while rotating; confirm the new hint is intended.
uncertainty: The circular handle returns a rotation action that the canvas pointer handlers must act on, and those handlers are not part of this change group; if dragging the handle does not rotate end-to-end, that wiring likely belongs to a companion change in this release rather than these selection and rendering changes.

The rotated text overlay depends on every text-editing entry point supplying the element's angle; the double-click editing flow is not part of this change set, so if it omits the angle the overlay receives an invalid rotation value and can lose its positioning and scale — the rotated-text check above is where this would appear.

Drawings saved before this release may not carry the new angle value on their elements, and clicking now depends on that value; if a loaded element has no angle it could become impossible to select by clicking. Test with an old local save or a previously shared drawing to confirm selection still works.

The supplied context gives no navigation details and no documented rule for how export should treat rotation, so the expected result is canvas appearance; any mismatch in angle or position for a rotated element, especially arrows whose rotation center comes from computed bounds, should be reported as a defect rather than a styling choice.

Verify that selecting a shape and dragging the rotation handle above it now turns the shape around its centre, following the mouse as you move it, which never happened before this release when dragging that handle left the shape completely unchanged, and confirm the turning is smooth and stops at the shape's centre rather than swinging it around some other point.
Verify that selecting a single text element now shows only the round handle above it and no square resize handles, where before this release a selected text element showed no handles at all.

Confirm that resizing a shape you have first tilted, by dragging a corner handle of for example a rectangle rotated partway, keeps the opposite corner fixed in place while the shape grows or shrinks, instead of the shape drifting sideways as happened before this release when the tilt was ignored during resizing.

Verify that the dashed outline around a selected shape tilted 45 degrees tilts along with the shape, where before this release the dashed outline stayed straight and horizontal around the untilted bounds.
Check that with a text element selected, dragging the round handle above it now tilts the text, where before this release selected text showed no handles and could not be tilted or resized at all.

Verify that when you rotate a shape on the canvas (for example turn a rectangle about 30 degrees with its rotation handle) and then export the drawing as an SVG file, the shape in the saved file comes out tilted by that same angle, where the previous release saved it upright as if it had never been rotated, and confirm this new behaviour is intended.

Check that when you drag a selected shape to a new tilt, the round handle above it swings around so it stays centered over the shape's top edge, where before this release no such handle moved with the shape.
Check that the small handle above a selected element is drawn as a filled circle with an outline, where before this release nothing was drawn in that spot above the element.

Verify that a shape you have tilted keeps its tilt on the main canvas while you drag it and scroll around, where before this release the shape was stamped back onto the screen without its tilt and shifted by its corner rather than turning about its center.

Verify that clicking a corner handle of a tilted shape exactly where it is now displayed starts a resize, while the spot where the handle appeared before this release no longer responds, so the grab area matches what you see.

Verify that selecting everything on a canvas containing a rectangle tilted 45 degrees draws one bounding box wrapped around the tilted shape's true extents, where before this release the box hugged the untilted rectangle and cut off its corners.

Confirm that saving or exporting a drawing that contains a tilted shape produces an image with the shape tilted exactly as on screen, where before this release the exported image drew the shape upright.

Verify that clicking on the visible body of a tilted rectangle, diamond or ellipse selects the shape, where the click test used to treat the shape as upright so a click on its tilted body could miss it; confirm that clicking now matches what is actually drawn.

Confirm that when you start rotating a selected shape by dragging its rotation handle with the mouse, a hint about rotating appears in the hint area at the bottom of the canvas, where before this release nothing appeared there while rotating; confirm the new hint is intended.

Confirm that selecting a shape now shows an extra rotation handle floating above its top edge in addition to the eight familiar corner and side handles, where before this release only those eight handles appeared; confirm the extra handle is intended.

Verify that double-clicking a text element after tilting it opens the editing box tilted to match the text on the canvas and that typed text appears at that same angle, whereas before this release the editing box was always horizontal because shapes could not be tilted in the first place.

Confirm that hovering the mouse over the rotation handle of a selected shape now shows the left-right resize arrows cursor, whereas before this release that spot kept the ordinary default arrow cursor.

Check that a brand-new shape you draw starts upright at a tilt of exactly zero, where a freshly created element used to carry no tilt value at all; confirm that starting every new shape at zero tilt is intended.

Check that clicking empty canvas space that only overlaps where a tilted shape would sit if it had never been rotated does not select that shape, since the click area used to be computed as if every shape were upright and such a click could grab it; confirm the click area now follows the rotated position.

Check that a freshly opened drawing starts with rotation switched off: open the app in a new session, click a shape right away, and confirm it shows its normal handles and can be resized and then rotated cleanly on the very first drag, since the app now deliberately starts every session not rotating where before it had no starting value for this.

Check that a drawing saved by an older version still opens with every shape upright, for example by reloading a page with your saved work or dropping an old saved file onto the canvas, and that one of those old shapes can then be selected and rotated cleanly, since old shapes carry no tilt value which the app now fills in as upright instead of leaving it missing.

Verify that rotating a shape and then reloading the page brings the drawing back with no rotation in progress and nothing selected, since the temporary in-progress rotation flag is no longer written into the browser's saved copy of your work, whereas before this release such an in-progress flag could be saved along with the drawing and restored on reload.

Verify that double-clicking a piece of text you have rotated with the rotation handle opens the editing box tilted to the same angle as the text, where before this release the editing box always opened horizontally no matter how the text was tilted; confirm the tilted editing box is intended.

Confirm that releasing the mouse button after turning a shape with the rotation handle ends the rotation, so the shape keeps its new angle and moving the mouse afterwards no longer turns it, since the app now tracks an in-progress rotation that previously did not exist and must switch it off the moment you let go.

Confirm that with the text tool, clicking an empty spot on the canvas still opens the new typing box centered under the click point and untilted exactly as before, at any zoom level, since the new-text editor is now given an explicit zero tilt that keeps its positioning and zoom scaling from breaking.

Check that a drawing reopened from a saved file keeps every tilted shape at its saved angle, where building an element from stored data used to carry no tilt at all; confirm the preserved tilt is intended.

Confirm that pressing the rotation handle above a selected shape and dragging turns the shape instead of resizing or moving it, where before this release there was no handle above the shape and pressing that empty spot did nothing; confirm that this spot now starts a rotation is intended.

Verify that while you type in the editing box over tilted text the box is rotated by the same angle so your typing lines up with the tilt underneath, where the box used to stay horizontal and would not line up with tilted text; confirm the matched angle is intended.

report.summary: This release adds grouping and ungrouping of whiteboard elements, so selecting, clicking, copying and pasting now treat grouped elements as a single unit.
keyChanges: Selecting elements that belong to a group now also selects the whole group: when a marquee selection ends, groups of the captured elements are selected alongside the elements themselves, and single elements that are part of a selected group are selected through that group, so selections now move and behave as whole groups.

Plain clicks on grouped content changed: a plain pointer down followed by a pointer up with no drag on an element that belongs to a selected group no longer clears the selection, because a click on a grouped element previously deselected everything, while clicking empty canvas or a different ungrouped element still clears element selection, group selection, and any active group editing.

Double-clicking an element that belongs to a selected group now enters editing of that group so that individual elements can be selected and moved inside it; during such editing, only the elements that are part of the edited group's own selection are eligible for group selection of nested groups.

Drag-to-duplicate inside a group being edited now passes the edited group's ID and a group mapping so newly created duplicates are added into that same group rather than landing outside it, and these duplicated elements are then grouped with their source.

Group selection state, element selection state, and editing state are now managed as three separate pieces of state that are cleared together when clicking away, so a stale selection of one kind is no longer left behind while another kind is cleared.

Double-clicking a member of a selected group now enters that group for editing (only the clicked element stays selected) instead of opening the text editor; double-clicking an ungrouped element or empty canvas still opens text editing as before.

While a group is being edited, clicking another member of that group selects it within the group; clicking an element outside the group or on empty canvas now exits group editing, and that outside click no longer adds the clicked element to the selection.
Switching to any drawing tool, releasing the space bar while a tool is active, and committing a newly inserted text now clear the group-editing state together with the element selection.
Pasting now carries group information, so pasted copies of grouped elements stay grouped with each other instead of arriving as loose duplicates.

Scene loading from files, shareable links, and locally stored drawings now guarantees every element has a group-membership list, and the default editor state gained the two new group fields that save, export, and clear-canvas flows rely on.

Duplicating elements now preserves grouping correctly: copies of grouped elements get fresh group memberships and form a new group together (previously a copy silently joined the original's group), and when a copy is made while a group is being edited, the copy stays inside that edited group.

The duplicate-selection command and paste now share one group-ID map per operation, so all copies taken from one group land in the same new group; the drag-duplication path uses the same changed routine, whose required inputs changed.
Select all (Ctrl/Cmd+A) now also selects the groups that contain the selected elements and exits any group-editing state, instead of only selecting individual element IDs.
Every newly created element (shapes, lines, text) now starts with empty group membership, which underpins the new group and ungroup commands this change wires into the editor.
Element creation flows also feed export (including the watermark text element), so PNG/SVG export and clipboard copy go through the changed creation code.

Elements can now be grouped and ungrouped: the canvas right-click menu gains group and ungroup entries (registered as the fourth and fifth context-menu items), Ctrl+G groups the selection and Shift+Ctrl+G ungroups it (Cmd instead of Ctrl on Mac); the group shortcut requires Shift not to be held.

Grouping is a deliberate no-op that adds no undo step when fewer than two elements are selected or when the selection is already exactly one complete group; ungrouping with no group selected is likewise a no-op with no history entry.

Selection display changed: elements selected as part of a group no longer get individual dashed outlines; one dashed rectangle is drawn around each selected group and around the group currently being edited, and that rectangle stays upright even when group members are rotated.

The drawing state now tracks which groups are selected and which group is being edited, and the changed rendering code runs on every canvas repaint as well as in the export and clipboard image pipeline.

The keyboard shortcuts dialog now lists two new rows immediately after the Redo entry: Group with the Ctrl or Cmd+G combination and Ungroup with Ctrl or Cmd+Shift+G, which render as Cmd+G and Cmd+Shift+G on Mac and Ctrl+G and Ctrl+Shift+G on other platforms.

The two new row labels are fetched through the interface translation system, which raises an error when a label is missing in both the current and the fallback language, so a missing translation could prevent the shortcuts dialog from opening at all.
Every drawing element now also carries a list of group identifiers in its data model; this is type-level groundwork for grouping and has no direct runtime behavior of its own.
qaChecks: Verify that dragging a marquee over one element of a group selects the entire group, showing one selection outline around all group members rather than a single element.
Check that after selecting a group, clicking directly on one of its members and releasing without dragging keeps the group selected instead of clearing it, which is the behavior before this change.
Ensure that clicking on empty canvas clears both element selection and group selection and ends any active group editing session, leaving no stale group highlight.
Check that double-clicking a member of a selected group enters editing of that group so individual members can be selected and moved within it, instead of starting text editing or doing nothing.
Verify that while editing a group, selecting a subset of elements and ending the editing session leaves the outer group intact and still selectable as a whole.
Ensure that dragging one member of the group with the duplicate modifier creates a copy that is also a member of the same group and is selected together with it, not a standalone ungrouped shape.
Verify that after duplicating and releasing, the duplicated element and the original are grouped and that the group selection outline covers both.
Check that grouping two or more selected shapes creates one group that is immediately selected as a whole and moves as a unit.
Verify that ungrouping a selected group separates its elements and clears the group from selection without leaving a partial group state behind.
Confirm that the select-all action selects every element together with the groups they belong to, so dragging any group member afterward moves the entire group and not just the individual element.

Verify that with a group selected, double-clicking one of its members enters group editing (that single member becomes the selection) instead of opening a text editor, while double-clicking the nearby ungrouped shape or empty canvas still opens the text editor as before.

Verify that while editing a group, clicking a different member of the group selects that member, and clicking an element outside the group exits group editing without adding the outside element to the selection on that first click.

Verify that clicking empty canvas while editing a group exits group editing, and that choosing any drawing tool via toolbar or keyboard shortcut, or releasing the space bar while a tool is active, also ends group editing so drawing a new shape works normally.
Verify on a touch device that double-tapping a member of a selected group enters group editing the same way a mouse double-click does.
Verify that pasting previously grouped elements creates copies that remain grouped with each other (dragging one copy moves its group-mates) and form a separate group from the originals.
Verify that pasting plain ungrouped elements still inserts and selects them at the cursor as before.
Verify that pasting while a group is being edited completes normally and the next click behaves consistently, with no stuck group-editing state.
Verify that a saved file or shareable link containing grouped elements opens with the groups intact and group editing works on them.
Verify that an older saved file whose elements have no group data opens without errors and its elements can still be grouped and group-edited afterward.
Verify that reloading the page restores the locally stored drawing with groups behaving the same as before the reload.
Verify that with group editing active, inserting a new text element and committing it ends group editing so selection and group state are fully cleared.
Verify that normal text creation with no group selected (double-click empty canvas, type, commit) still works exactly as before.
Verify that exporting the drawing to PNG and SVG and copying it to the clipboard as PNG and SVG still produce complete images whether or not a group is selected.
Verify that saving to a shareable link and reopening it succeeds.
Verify that the clear-canvas action resets the scene fully, including any group selection or group-editing state, so fresh grouping works right after.

Verify duplicating a selected group produces copies offset down-right as before, and the copies form their own new group: dragging one copy moves the other copies but not the originals, and the originals remain grouped as before.
Verify duplicating a single ungrouped shape still creates an independent copy offset down-right that is not part of any group.
Verify opening a drawing saved before this update and duplicating one of its elements creates a working, selectable copy without errors, since those elements may carry no grouping data.
Ensure pasting a copied grouped pair places the pasted copies at the cursor grouped together as a new group, separate from the originals' group.
Ensure pasting a single ungrouped element still pastes normally at the cursor and stays ungrouped.
Verify Ctrl/Cmd+A selects everything in the scene (both groups and the loose element), dragging the selection moves all of it together, and the groups remain intact afterwards.
Verify that after select all, duplicating produces copies that keep the same new-group behavior as direct duplication.

Verify grouping several elements makes them act as one (dragging one member moves the group and a single selection border appears), and ungrouping separates them back into individually selectable elements.
Verify exporting the scene to PNG and SVG renders all elements correctly and still includes the watermark text.
Verify copying to clipboard as PNG and SVG produces the same result, and that adding and editing text on the canvas still works.

Verify selecting two or more shapes and using the context menu's group entry or Ctrl+G (Cmd+G on Mac, without Shift) encloses them in one dashed selection rectangle, and that undo removes the grouping.
Test the boundary input of exactly one selected shape: pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G must change nothing and add no undo step.

Confirm that selecting every member of an existing group and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G again does nothing (no duplicate grouping), while adding one extra shape to that selection and pressing it again creates a single larger group.

Verify Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+G on a selected group dissolves it so the shapes are selected and movable individually again, and that the same shortcut with no group selected does nothing and adds no undo step.
Verify a standalone shape selected by itself still shows its own dashed outline exactly as before.
Verify selecting a grouped shape now shows only one dashed rectangle around the whole group with no dashed outlines around the individual members, replacing the previous per-element outlines.
Verify the group's outline rectangle remains upright even when shapes inside the group are rotated.

Confirm in a live collaboration session, if available, that another participant's selected elements still show their dashed outlines, since group outlines are currently drawn only for your own selections.
Verify exporting the scene to PNG and SVG and copying it to the clipboard produces images of the shapes only, with no dashed selection or group rectangles in the output.
Confirm the export dialog's preview of a grouped scene shows the shapes without selection outlines and matches the exported file.

Verify the shortcuts dialog opens and shows a Group row with Ctrl+G (Cmd+G on Mac) and an Ungroup row with Ctrl+Shift+G (Cmd+Shift+G on Mac) listed next to the Redo shortcut, with the rest of the dialog still laid out correctly.
Verify after switching the interface language that the two new rows show translated labels and the dialog still opens without errors in each available language.
Confirm with two shapes selected that pressing the displayed Group key makes them act as one group and pressing the displayed Ungroup key separates them again.

Confirm that clicking a single shape that belongs to a selected group no longer draws a dashed outline tightly around that shape alone, only around the whole group, whereas before this release every selected shape always received its own tight dashed outline.

Verify that selecting two separate shapes and running the group action makes them behave as one group, so that clicking either shape afterwards selects both of them, where before this release the shapes always stayed independent.

Check that while editing inside a group, clicking a shape outside that group leaves group editing and clears the selection instead of adding the outside shape to the selection as a plain click would have done before.

Verify that with a grouped pair of shapes selected, double-clicking one of them enters editing inside the group rather than starting text editing at that spot, which differs from before this release when double-clicking always opened a text editor.

Verify that dragging a selection rectangle that encloses only one shape of a grouped pair ends up selecting the whole pair, where before this release the rectangle selected only the shapes it actually enclosed.
Check that with at least two shapes selected, right-clicking the canvas now offers a Group action and an Ungroup action in the menu, neither of which appeared before this release.

Verify that running the ungroup action on a selected two-shape group splits it back into independent shapes, so that clicking one of them afterwards selects only that one, where before this release there was no way to separate grouped shapes at all.

Confirm that after double-clicking into a large group that contains smaller groups, clicking a shape belonging to one of the smaller groups selects just that smaller group's members, where before this release the same click selected only the one shape.

Check clicking a member of a group: click one shape that has been grouped with others — before this release a click selected just that single shape, and clicking should now select the entire group so its members move together, while double-clicking still lets you edit individual members inside, so confirm that is intended.
Check that after grouping two shapes together, clicking just one of them selects the whole pair, where before this release a click always selected only the single shape you clicked.

Check duplicating while editing inside nested groups: build two small groups, group them together into one big group, double-click into the big group, select one small group and duplicate it — before this release duplicating paid no attention to grouping, and the copies should now stay inside the big group while forming their own fresh small group instead of being lumped in with the original inner group, so confirm that is intended.

Check that grouping an outside shape together with a shape of the group you are currently inside creates the new group as a wrapper around the original, so clicking the newly added shape selects all three while the original pair still selects on its own, something that could not happen before this release because shapes could not be grouped.

Verify that after grouping two shapes and rotating both of them, selecting the group draws one dashed rectangle standing upright around the outside of the pair rather than tilted with the shapes, and confirm that upright framing is intended, since no group outline existed before this release.

Check select all while editing inside a group: double-click a grouped pair to edit its members and press Ctrl+A or Cmd+A — before this release select all simply ticked every element individually, and it should now cancel the group editing and treat grouped shapes as whole groups, so confirm the selection comes out group-aware as intended.

Check copy and paste on grouped shapes: select a grouped pair, copy it and paste — before this release the pasted copies kept the original group's membership so they stayed glued to the originals, and the pasted pair should now arrive still grouped as its own new group that can be moved without dragging the originals along, so confirm that is intended.
uncertainty: The supplied application context contains no named surfaces, menus, routes, or labels for the grouping and selection actions, so the exact command names and keyboard shortcuts used in the steps above were described generically and must be confirmed in the editor before testing.

Previously any double-click opened the text editor; the new code intercepts double-clicks on members of a selected group to enter group editing instead, and this evidence shows no remaining path for editing the text of an element inside a group. Confirm grouped text elements can still have their text edited through some interaction; if none exists, that is a usability regression to raise before release.

The duplication path triggered while dragging elements (the alt-drag duplicate) uses the same changed routine whose required inputs changed; the supplied context did not confirm that path was updated, and no navigation for entering group-editing mode was supplied, so duplicating while inside an edited group could not be pinned to concrete steps — spot-check both if reachable.

Navigation details were not supplied for any affected surface, and the new context-menu entries are registered under translation keys rather than confirmed wording, so locate the group and ungroup items by right-clicking a selection on the canvas; the exact on-screen labels are unconfirmed.

Because the change is purely additive, the most likely regression is a missing translation for the two new row labels, which would make the shortcuts dialog fail to open in that language; the grouping behavior behind the advertised shortcuts is implemented in other parts of this release and should be judged together with those groups.
