checks: Verify selecting two or more shapes and using the context menu's group entry or Ctrl+G (Cmd+G on Mac, without Shift) encloses them in one dashed selection rectangle, and that undo removes the grouping.
Test the boundary input of exactly one selected shape: pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G must change nothing and add no undo step.

Confirm that selecting every member of an existing group and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G again does nothing (no duplicate grouping), while adding one extra shape to that selection and pressing it again creates a single larger group.

Verify Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+G on a selected group dissolves it so the shapes are selected and movable individually again, and that the same shortcut with no group selected does nothing and adds no undo step.

testAreas.area: Selection outlines for grouped versus individual elements on the canvas
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; on the editor canvas, create a group, then select grouped and ungrouped elements to compare the outlines.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator editing a drawing.
testAreas.setup: One group of two shapes plus one standalone shape, with at least one shape rotated.
checks: Verify a standalone shape selected by itself still shows its own dashed outline exactly as before.
Verify selecting a grouped shape now shows only one dashed rectangle around the whole group with no dashed outlines around the individual members, replacing the previous per-element outlines.
Verify the group's outline rectangle remains upright even when shapes inside the group are rotated.

Confirm in a live collaboration session, if available, that another participant's selected elements still show their dashed outlines, since group outlines are currently drawn only for your own selections.

testAreas.area: Exported and clipboard images of grouped drawings
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; from the editor, open the export dialog and use the copy-to-clipboard actions reachable from the canvas context menu and their shortcuts.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator editing a drawing.
testAreas.setup: Two shapes grouped and left selected in the scene.
checks: Verify exporting the scene to PNG and SVG and copying it to the clipboard produces images of the shapes only, with no dashed selection or group rectangles in the output.
Confirm the export dialog's preview of a grouped scene shows the shapes without selection outlines and matches the exported file.

testAreas.area: Keyboard shortcuts dialog in the drawing editor
testAreas.howToReach: Open a drawing in the Excalidraw editor and open the keyboard shortcuts dialog from the editor's interface; the exact menu entry was not found in the supplied context.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator or editor.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with at least two shapes available to select; if possible test on both a Mac and a non-Mac device, or at least note which platform shortcut text is shown.
checks: Verify the shortcuts dialog opens and shows a Group row with Ctrl+G (Cmd+G on Mac) and an Ungroup row with Ctrl+Shift+G (Cmd+Shift+G on Mac) listed next to the Redo shortcut, with the rest of the dialog still laid out correctly.
Verify after switching the interface language that the two new rows show translated labels and the dialog still opens without errors in each available language.
Confirm with two shapes selected that pressing the displayed Group key makes them act as one group and pressing the displayed Ungroup key separates them again.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Confirm that clicking a single shape that belongs to a selected group no longer draws a dashed outline tightly around that shape alone, only around the whole group, whereas before this release every selected shape always received its own tight dashed outline.

Verify that selecting two separate shapes and running the group action makes them behave as one group, so that clicking either shape afterwards selects both of them, where before this release the shapes always stayed independent.

Check that while editing inside a group, clicking a shape outside that group leaves group editing and clears the selection instead of adding the outside shape to the selection as a plain click would have done before.

Verify that with a grouped pair of shapes selected, double-clicking one of them enters editing inside the group rather than starting text editing at that spot, which differs from before this release when double-clicking always opened a text editor.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Verify that dragging a selection rectangle that encloses only one shape of a grouped pair ends up selecting the whole pair, where before this release the rectangle selected only the shapes it actually enclosed.
Check that with at least two shapes selected, right-clicking the canvas now offers a Group action and an Ungroup action in the menu, neither of which appeared before this release.

Verify that running the ungroup action on a selected two-shape group splits it back into independent shapes, so that clicking one of them afterwards selects only that one, where before this release there was no way to separate grouped shapes at all.

Confirm that after double-clicking into a large group that contains smaller groups, clicking a shape belonging to one of the smaller groups selects just that smaller group's members, where before this release the same click selected only the one shape.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Check clicking a member of a group: click one shape that has been grouped with others — before this release a click selected just that single shape, and clicking should now select the entire group so its members move together, while double-clicking still lets you edit individual members inside, so confirm that is intended.
Check that after grouping two shapes together, clicking just one of them selects the whole pair, where before this release a click always selected only the single shape you clicked.

Check duplicating while editing inside nested groups: build two small groups, group them together into one big group, double-click into the big group, select one small group and duplicate it — before this release duplicating paid no attention to grouping, and the copies should now stay inside the big group while forming their own fresh small group instead of being lumped in with the original inner group, so confirm that is intended.

Check that grouping an outside shape together with a shape of the group you are currently inside creates the new group as a wrapper around the original, so clicking the newly added shape selects all three while the original pair still selects on its own, something that could not happen before this release because shapes could not be grouped.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Verify that after grouping two shapes and rotating both of them, selecting the group draws one dashed rectangle standing upright around the outside of the pair rather than tilted with the shapes, and confirm that upright framing is intended, since no group outline existed before this release.

Check select all while editing inside a group: double-click a grouped pair to edit its members and press Ctrl+A or Cmd+A — before this release select all simply ticked every element individually, and it should now cancel the group editing and treat grouped shapes as whole groups, so confirm the selection comes out group-aware as intended.

Check copy and paste on grouped shapes: select a grouped pair, copy it and paste — before this release the pasted copies kept the original group's membership so they stayed glued to the originals, and the pasted pair should now arrive still grouped as its own new group that can be moved without dragging the originals along, so confirm that is intended.

moreChecks: Confirm that after double-clicking a shape to work inside its group, clicking an empty part of the canvas now clears everything and leaves the group so a following click on one of its shapes selects the whole group again, whereas before this release an empty-canvas click simply cleared the selection.

Check duplicating a grouped selection: group two rectangles, select them and press the duplicate shortcut, then drag one of the copies — before this release duplicating produced plain ungrouped copies, and the two copies should now come out as their own new group that moves independently of the originals, so confirm that is intended.

Confirm that once you have double-clicked into a group, dragging one of its shapes moves only that shape and leaves the rest of the group where it is, matching how dragging any single ungrouped shape behaved before this release.

Check that opening the keyboard shortcuts dialog — which before this release showed no group or ungroup entries — now lists a group row and an ungroup row in the editing section, displaying Cmd on a Mac and Ctrl on Windows, and confirm adding them is intended.

Verify that with shapes selected, pressing the control or command key together with the G key and without holding Shift groups the selection immediately, while adding Shift to those same keys never groups anything, since before this release neither combination did anything and Shift is now set aside for ungrouping.
Confirm that with a grouped pair selected, holding Shift along with the modifier and G keys ungroups it, a combination that did nothing at all before this release.

Confirm that selecting every member of a group and using the group command a second time adds no extra outer layer and leaves the selection as that one group, a repeat case that could not arise before this release because grouping did not exist.
Confirm that clicking a drawing tool such as the ellipse while a group is in edit mode clears the selection and ends the group editing, so the next shape you draw is standalone.

Verify that clicking one shape of a grouped pair and then double-clicking that shape opens the group for editing so later clicks pick single shapes inside it, instead of starting a text box the way double-clicking did before this release.

Verify that when two pairs of shapes have each been grouped and then all four are grouped together into one big group, ungrouping the big group leaves each original pair still grouped so a later click on one shape still brings its partner along, an outcome that was impossible before this release.

Verify that selecting two shapes, grouping them, saving the drawing, and reopening it keeps the shapes grouped, because scenes saved before this release stored no group information for their elements and the new version records it, and confirm this behavior is intended.

Check that after clicking one shape so its whole group is selected, the ungroup command dissolves that group so a fresh click selects only the single shape clicked, since before this release there was no way to group or ungroup shapes.
Confirm that double-clicking empty canvas to insert a text label while a group is in edit mode ends the group editing right away, so the text is created outside any group editing context.

Verify that when a drawing tool such as the rectangle is selected, double-clicking into a grouped shape to edit the group and then holding and releasing the spacebar to pan ends the group editing, so the next click starts from an empty selection.
Check that while editing inside a group, clicking one of the shapes that belongs to that group keeps you in group editing instead of dropping you out.

Verify that opening a drawing file saved with an older release that had no grouping feature loads all shapes correctly and lets you select and move them without errors, since shapes without group information are now treated as ungrouped.

Verify that opening the app in a browser where a drawing was saved with the previous release still loads that drawing normally and starts with nothing selected and no group in edit mode, since the starting settings now also prepare group tracking.

Check that copying a shape, double-clicking a grouped shape to enter the group, and pasting adds the pasted shape to that group instead of leaving it ungrouped, which is new because pasting never joined groups before this release.

Confirm the new Group and Ungroup commands are available: select two shapes and press Ctrl+G or pick Group from the right-click menu — before this release there was no grouping and no such command existed, and the shapes should now act as one unit that selects, moves and deletes together, so confirm that is intended.

Check that a shape drawn fresh from the toolbar can be grouped straight away: draw a new rectangle, select it together with an existing shape and press Ctrl+G — before this release newly drawn shapes carried no group information at all, and every new shape should now start with an empty group membership so grouping it on the first try works, so confirm that is intended.

Check that on a Windows or Linux machine holding Ctrl and pressing the letter G with shapes selected triggers the grouping, and that on a Mac the command key with G does the same, since neither combination had any effect before this release.

report.summary: This release introduces a new point-editing mode for lines and arrows on the drawing canvas, letting users reshape them point by point with drag, keyboard, and undo/redo support, backed by internal changes that touch most canvas drawing behavior.
keyChanges: While a line or arrow is in point-editing mode, moving the pointer now drags the grabbed point handle, and releasing a start or end point very close to the opposite endpoint snaps the shape closed into a loop, which can then be filled with a background color.

Point editing also gains Alt-click and Alt-drag to append new points (placement compensates for element rotation, so points land under the cursor even on rotated lines), Delete to remove the selected point — where removing what would be the last remaining point deletes the whole element — and zoom-scaled point hit-testing in which overlapping point handles resolve to the rightmost one.

Element updates whose points are unchanged are now skipped entirely, with no version bump, redraw, or collaboration broadcast; scene replacement now also maintains an id-to-element lookup that the new point editor depends on, so a stale lookup would make point edits silently do nothing.
A loop-detection helper changed only its input typing, with no runtime behavior change.

Double-clicking or pressing Enter on exactly one selected arrow, line, or drawn stroke now opens a new point-editing mode instead of the old behavior (double-click used to start text editing); a round handle is drawn at every point of the element, with the active point highlighted while hovering.

While point-editing, canvas clicks and pointer moves are handled by the new point editor: resize-handle detection is skipped for the edited element, and the rectangular selection frame is no longer painted (it is also suppressed while mid-drawing a multi-point line).

Point editing ends automatically as soon as the edited element is no longer selected, for example after pressing Escape or selecting a different element, and exiting is meant to keep undo history clean.
The point-editing state is stripped from browser autosave and defaults to off for new, imported, and shared scenes, so reloading or opening a drawing never resumes point editing.

Selecting a line or arrow and double-clicking it (or pressing Enter) now enters a dedicated point-editing mode that shows a red circular handle on every point; entering the mode normalizes the element's stored geometry so the start point sits at the origin with the position compensated, meaning the line should not visibly shift.

In that mode, dragging a point now compensates for the element's rotation angle, and the handle positions themselves account for rotation, so point handles on a rotated line or arrow should sit exactly on the drawn points and follow the cursor direction correctly.

While point-editing, Alt+click adds a new point at the cursor and Alt+hover extends a trailing preview point; releasing Alt without clicking removes that uncommitted preview point, and pointer-down with Alt commits it.
On pointer release, if the first or last point was dragged so the path forms a loop, the two endpoints are snapped together so the shape reads as a closed loop.

The helpers that decide which resize/rotation handle a pointer hits changed their parameter shape from a single coordinates object to two separate scene pointer coordinates; behavior is intended to be identical, but a mismatched caller would make handle detection silently fail, breaking resizing and rotating of selected elements.

Selecting a single line, arrow, or free-drawn stroke now shows a new hint-strip message about the line editor; while editing points, the message switches between a point-selected and a no-point-selected tip, and the first point (index 0) is treated as no point selected.

Hint text is now passed through the platform shortcut formatter, so key names in hints display as Cmd/Ctrl, Option/Alt, and Delete per platform; the formatter itself now only replaces whole words, so text containing embedded words such as 'delta' or 'default' is no longer mangled.

Undo and redo now track the point editor: entering point-edit mode is recorded as a history entry and undo/redo restores it, while changing the selected point within the same line no longer creates extra undo entries.

A helper that computes a line, arrow, or freehand element's bounding box from its points now lives in the shared geometry module and is called while a point is dragged; it recomputes bounds and shifts the element so only the dragged point appears to move, which matters most for rotated lines and arrows.

The shared scene now maintains an id-to-element map and a non-deleted lookup that the point editor, the delete-selected action, and the finalize-line action use to resolve the element being edited; deleted elements return null from the non-deleted lookup.
The scene's unused constructor was removed and the remaining edits are type-only (point arrays marked readonly plus a type import), so they have no runtime behavior to test.
While in point-edit mode on a line or arrow, Delete now removes only the active point (the active point moves back one, or stays on the first point) rather than deleting the whole element as before.
When a line is down to fewer than two points, Delete removes the entire line, closes point-edit mode, and does not record that removal as its own undo step.

Escape now exits point-edit mode: the mode closes, and a line left with fewer than two points or too small to see is removed, with the result recorded in history; previously Escape did not close point-edit mode.
Escape also triggers finalize while a point drag is in progress, which the old key handling did not allow, so a drag can now be interrupted.

After a line is deleted while a group is being edited (including via last-point deletion), the first remaining member of that group becomes selected; the undo/redo writer was refactored with no intended behavior change.
qaChecks: Verify that in point-editing mode dragging the start point, a middle point, and the end point each reshapes the element to follow the cursor and that the reshaped geometry persists after release.
Test Alt-click and Alt-drag along both the straight and the rotated line: a new point should appear exactly under the cursor and the line should reroute through it.
Verify that selecting a point and pressing Delete removes only that point, and that deleting points until one would remain removes the entire line from the canvas.
Verify at a low and a high zoom level that clicking a point handle grabs the intended point, and that when two point handles overlap the rightmost one is grabbed.
Verify entering point-edit mode via double-click (and via Enter on a selected line) shows a red circular handle on every point and the line does not shift or jump position when the mode opens.

Verify on a rotated line or arrow that every red handle sits exactly on the drawn point, and dragging a point moves it in the same direction as the mouse cursor rather than mirrored, since rotation compensation is new.

Verify Alt+click adds a point at the cursor, Alt+hover extends a trailing preview point, and releasing Alt and moving without clicking deletes the preview without leaving a stray extra point on the line.

Verify that in edit mode dragging the first or last point until the path forms a loop, then releasing, snaps the endpoints together into a closed shape, and that clicking a point (rather than empty canvas) keeps the element selected instead of deselecting it.

Verify dragging the last point to within a very small distance of the first point and releasing snaps the dragged endpoint onto the opposite one so the shape becomes a closed loop, and that assigning a background color afterwards fills the closed shape.
Verify releasing the endpoint just beyond that snap distance leaves the shape open with no unintended snapping.
Verify every real point move, add, and delete made in one browser appears on the other participant's canvas, and that Ctrl+Z locally restores the previous shape after each edit.
Verify dragging the first (start) point of a line visibly moves it while the remaining points keep the shape coherent, and that this edit syncs and undoes like any other point edit.
Verify core scene operations still work end to end: paste elements, move a selection with the arrow keys, delete it, then reload the page so all remaining elements reappear and render correctly.
Verify joining an in-progress collaboration session loads the complete current drawing, including lines that were point-edited earlier.

Verify that with exactly one arrow or line selected, pressing Enter or double-clicking it shows a round handle at every point with the active point highlighted, and the rectangular selection frame with corner handles is no longer displayed.

Check that while point-editing, dragging a round point moves only that point and reshapes the line, and that hovering or dragging where the old corner resize handles were does not resize the element or show a resize cursor.
Confirm that while point-editing, pressing Escape or selecting a different element exits editing automatically and the line returns to a normally selected element.
Ensure that after editing points and leaving edit mode, Undo steps back through the point changes instead of doing nothing or erasing the drawing.

Verify that double-clicking the canvas while exactly one arrow or line is selected no longer places a text box but opens point editing, and that the same applies to a one-finger double-tap on touch devices.
Confirm that double-clicking with nothing selected, or with a non-line shape such as a rectangle selected, still starts text editing as before.
Verify that with a line in point-editing mode, the export dialog preview shows the drawing without the red or white point markers.
Ensure that saving or copying the drawing as an image while point-editing produces a picture containing only the drawing, with no point markers.
Verify that reloading the browser page while a line is in point-editing mode restores the drawing from browser storage and opens in normal mode, not stuck in point editing.
Confirm that opening a previously saved drawing file or a shared link loads without errors and does not resume point editing.
Verify dragging a corner handle resizes the shape from that corner while the opposite corner stays fixed, and dragging a rotation handle rotates the shape.

Verify hovering the corner, side, and rotation handles shows the correct resize and rotate cursors, and that handles still respond when clicked exactly on their edge at different zoom levels, because the hit-testing helpers changed how they receive pointer coordinates.

Verify the exported PNG and SVG images match the on-canvas drawing for line and arrow geometry (endpoints, rotation, and point count), since the shared scene renderer feeds export, clipboard copy, and the export dialog through the same changed point-coordinate calculation.

Verify that entering point-edit mode is recorded as a single undo step: double-click a line to enter edit mode, press undo once, confirm the editor returns to the previous state (edit mode closed, drawing unchanged), and redo re-enters it.

Check that clicking different points without moving them creates no undo steps: click through several points, then press undo and confirm it reverts the last real change instead of stepping through the point clicks.
Verify that moving a point and pressing undo reverts exactly that move, and that undo/redo restores the editor state (in or out of edit mode) together with the drawing.

Verify that selecting a single line or arrow shows a hint about the line editor, and that entering edit mode switches the hint between the point-selected and no-point-selected messages as you click points.

Check the first point: enter edit mode and click the first point of the line - the new logic treats a selected first point as no point selected, so the no-point-selected tip shows instead of a point-selected tip; flag this if the first point should count as selected.
Test a single free-drawn stroke: the new logic treats drawn strokes like lines and arrows, so confirm the hint shown for a selected stroke is the intended message.
Verify that any key names in the hint text render per platform on Mac (Cmd, Option, Delete) and on Windows/Linux (Ctrl, Alt), since hint text is now passed through the shortcut formatter.

Check that ordinary words containing key names as substrings are untouched: a hint containing a word like 'delta' or 'default' should display unchanged, because the formatter now only replaces whole words.
Verify dragging a point of the rotated line or arrow moves only that point while the rest of the shape stays visually fixed, including after pointer release.
Verify removing one point of the selected multi-segment line keeps the remaining segments on canvas at the expected position.
Verify dragging an arrow's endpoint onto its other endpoint (a zero-length collapse) keeps the editor stable, the element selectable, and shows no error.
Verify point dragging on the long freehand stroke stays responsive while the pointer moves.
Verify deleting a selection that includes a line or arrow plus regular shapes removes exactly the selected items from the canvas and leaves nothing stale behind.
Verify that after a deletion, selecting a remaining line and dragging its points still works, confirming element lookups keep resolving.
Verify drawing a multi-segment line by clicking successive points and finishing it places the line at the drawn position with its shape intact.
Verify the finished line's points can be edited immediately by dragging them.
Verify that pressing Delete on an active point of a three-point line removes only that point and the line stays on the canvas and remains editable (before this change the whole line was deleted).
Confirm that deleting points one at a time down to a single remaining point, then pressing Delete once more, removes the whole line and closes point-edit mode.
Check that deleting the first point of a multi-point line removes it and the active point moves to the new first point without the line disappearing.
Ensure that when a line belonging to a group is removed by deleting its last remaining point, one of the other group members becomes selected.
Verify that Escape while point-editing a normal multi-point line exits point-edit mode and the line remains on the canvas and can be selected.
Test Escape after reducing a line to a single point, or after dragging its points so it is too small to see: point-edit mode should close and the degenerate line should be removed from the drawing.
Ensure that pressing Escape while a point is being dragged exits point-edit mode cleanly and the editor is not left in a stuck dragging state.
Verify that deleting two points in point-edit mode and pressing undo twice restores both points step by step, and redo reapplies the deletions.

Check that after Delete removes the final remaining point and the line disappears, one undo brings the line back with its remaining point, even though that removal was not recorded as its own history step.
Confirm that while editing a line's points, holding Alt and clicking at a spot along the line adds a brand-new point exactly at that spot, something the previous release could not do at all.

Verify that dragging the very first point of a line in edit mode moves that point with the cursor while every other point stays exactly where it was, so the shape stretches from that end without jumping, where previously any drag hauled the whole line around.

Check that in point-editing mode pressing one of a line's point handles and dragging it bends and reshapes the line, which was not possible in the previous release because finished lines' points could not be moved; confirm the reshaping follows the mouse.

Verify that after double-clicking a line or arrow so its points become editable with one point highlighted, pressing the Delete key removes only that highlighted point and highlights the neighbouring point, whereas in the previous release the same key press deleted the entire shape, and confirm the new point-by-point deletion is intended.
Check that in line point-editing, pressing a point handle and dragging quickly keeps dragging that same point until the button is released, rather than the grab switching to another point.

Check that in point-editing mode holding Alt and moving the mouse without pressing a button makes a loose preview point trail the cursor, and that once Alt is released and the mouse moves again that preview point disappears instead of being left behind on the line.

Verify that while editing a line's points, moving the mouse over one of the round point handles highlights that handle in a darker red, where before this release the canvas gave no hover feedback because points could not be edited, and confirm the highlighting is intended.

Check that when a line is in point-editing mode every point of the line is drawn as a small circle with a red outline, the one under the cursor filled solid, which never appeared on the canvas before this release, and confirm the handles sit exactly on the line's points.

Verify that in point-editing mode dragging the line's first or last point until it comes within a few pixels of the opposite endpoint and releasing the mouse snaps the two endpoints exactly together, closing the line into a loop, rather than leaving them nearly touching where the drag ended.

Confirm that while editing an arrow's points, clicking directly on the line between two handles adds a new point there and does not start dragging the whole arrow, which clicking a selected arrow used to do before this release, and confirm this is intended.

Confirm that while co-editing, grabbing a point of a line and holding the mouse perfectly still no longer counts as a change and stops sending repeated empty updates to the other participant, where before the drawing was treated as changed and re-sent on every drag event even though nothing had moved.

Check that clicking exactly on one of a line's point handles in edit mode makes that point the active selected one, and when two handles sit on top of each other the one drawn on top is the one picked, whereas before a click could only select the whole line.

Verify that drawing an arrow, clicking it once to select it, and then double-clicking it now opens point-editing mode with a round handle on each point, where the same double-click previously started a text editor on the shape, and confirm the new behavior is intended.

Check that drawing a zigzag line or arrow with at least three points and then dragging one of its middle points moves only that point while the rest of the line stays anchored exactly where it was, and confirm this new way of reshaping lines is intended, given that before this release a finished line could not be reshaped by dragging its points at all.

Confirm that finishing point editing with Escape or the done button after you have deleted a shape's points down to fewer than two removes that shape from the drawing completely, which could not happen before because point editing had no finish path, and confirm this automatic cleanup of leftover shapes is intended.
uncertainty: The new unchanged-points filter compares points from the last index down to index 1 and never compares index 0 (single-point arrays are not compared at all), so a legitimate update that changes only a line's first point could be silently dropped with no version bump, redraw, or collaboration sync; the supplied point-editing flows shift the remaining points whenever the first point moves, so the gap may be unreachable today, but any path that adjusts only the first point is the most likely silent regression.

The evidence does not establish whether the export pipeline clears the point-editing state before rendering, so the export checks above are the way to confirm no editing markers leak into previews, saved images, or clipboard copies.

The line/arrow editing code arrives as whole-file additions with no documented previous behavior to compare against, and the resize hit-testing helpers changed from one coordinates object to two separate pointer arguments; if any caller still passed the old form, handle detection would fail silently with no error, so the resize checks above are the safety net and should be run against the previous release build for comparison.

The exact wording of the new hint messages is not supplied, so expected text cannot be quoted; the new hint branch also fires for free-drawn strokes, not only lines and arrows, so the message shown for a selected drawn stroke may be unintended and needs a product decision.

The previous implementation of the moved bounding-box helper is not part of the supplied evidence, so identical bounds recomputation during point drags cannot be confirmed from the diff alone; compare point-drag behavior on rotated lines and arrows against the build before this change.

Exiting point-edit mode now finishes before the normal finalize cleanup runs, so the mouse cursor or keyboard focus may not reset when Escape closes point-editing; confirm the cursor returns to normal after exiting and flag it if it does not.

Check that in point-editing mode holding Alt and moving the mouse without pressing a button makes a loose preview point trail the cursor, and that once Alt is released and the mouse moves again that preview point disappears instead of being left behind on the line.

Verify that while editing a line's points, moving the mouse over one of the round point handles highlights that handle in a darker red, where before this release the canvas gave no hover feedback because points could not be edited, and confirm the highlighting is intended.

Check that when a line is in point-editing mode every point of the line is drawn as a small circle with a red outline, the one under the cursor filled solid, which never appeared on the canvas before this release, and confirm the handles sit exactly on the line's points.

Verify that in point-editing mode dragging the line's first or last point until it comes within a few pixels of the opposite endpoint and releasing the mouse snaps the two endpoints exactly together, closing the line into a loop, rather than leaving them nearly touching where the drag ended.

Confirm that while editing an arrow's points, clicking directly on the line between two handles adds a new point there and does not start dragging the whole arrow, which clicking a selected arrow used to do before this release, and confirm this is intended.

Confirm that while co-editing, grabbing a point of a line and holding the mouse perfectly still no longer counts as a change and stops sending repeated empty updates to the other participant, where before the drawing was treated as changed and re-sent on every drag event even though nothing had moved.

Check that clicking exactly on one of a line's point handles in edit mode makes that point the active selected one, and when two handles sit on top of each other the one drawn on top is the one picked, whereas before a click could only select the whole line.

Verify that drawing an arrow, clicking it once to select it, and then double-clicking it now opens point-editing mode with a round handle on each point, where the same double-click previously started a text editor on the shape, and confirm the new behavior is intended.

Check that drawing a zigzag line or arrow with at least three points and then dragging one of its middle points moves only that point while the rest of the line stays anchored exactly where it was, and confirm this new way of reshaping lines is intended, given that before this release a finished line could not be reshaped by dragging its points at all.

Confirm that finishing point editing with Escape or the done button after you have deleted a shape's points down to fewer than two removes that shape from the drawing completely, which could not happen before because point editing had no finish path, and confirm this automatic cleanup of leftover shapes is intended.

Verify that while editing the points of a line you rotated earlier, holding Alt and clicking beyond its end adds a new point exactly under the cursor instead of at a position skewed by the rotation, which could not be done before.

Check that when a line you are editing inside a group loses its final remaining point and disappears as a result, the first shape left in that group becomes the selected one; before this release deleting during point editing removed the whole grouped shape at once and only then moved the selection, so confirm the same selection hand-off now happens at the end of the new point-by-point deletion.

Confirm that after double-clicking a line to edit its points, pressing one of its small square point handles and dragging moves just that point while the rest of the line stays put, instead of dragging the whole line the way a plain drag did before.
Check that selecting a line and pressing Enter to start editing its points leaves the line exactly where it was on the canvas, with no jump or shift of the drawing when editing begins.

Confirm that opening a saved drawing containing a line or arrow and then double-clicking that shape puts it into point-editing mode on exactly the shape you clicked, since the canvas now remembers every loaded shape under its own identifier — something it did not do before this release — and confirm that is intended.

Check that while a selected arrow is in point-editing mode the usual outline around the selected shape is no longer drawn and only the red point handles show, while an arrow that is only selected still shows its outline as before, and confirm hiding the outline during point editing is intended.

Confirm that selecting a single line or arrow and pressing Enter now enters point-editing mode showing the red point handles, where pressing Enter on a selected line or arrow previously did nothing, and confirm the new shortcut is intended.

Verify that after rotating a line, entering its point-editing mode draws the round handles on the line's actual corner points in their rotated positions, and that clicking a handle highlights exactly that point rather than a different one.

Check that while editing a line's points, dragging the first or last point until the two ends nearly touch and then releasing snaps them exactly together to close the shape into a loop, where previously the point simply stayed wherever it was dropped.

Check that while you are editing an arrow's points, clicking on an empty area of the canvas closes point-editing mode on its own and shows the arrow back in its ordinary selected state instead of leaving the red handles on a shape that is no longer selected, and confirm this automatic exit is intended.

Confirm that selecting a line or arrow, deleting it, and then double-clicking where it used to be does nothing at all — no editing opens and no error or leftover handles appear — because deleted shapes are now explicitly refused when the editor asks for a shape by its identifier, a check that did not exist before this release, and confirm that is intended.

Verify that on the canvas you draw a line or an arrow, switch to the selection tool and click it so it is the only thing selected, then look at the hint area at the top of the canvas, where before this release no hint appeared for a selected line and now a tip about editing the shape's points is shown, and confirm that this new tip is intended.

Confirm that double-clicking a line on the canvas enters a point-editing mode that did not exist in the previous release, showing a round handle on every point of the line, and confirm this is intended.

Confirm that when you double-click a drawn line to edit its points, click one of its points without moving anything and then press Undo, the first press of Undo now goes straight to undoing the previous real change, whereas before this release simply clicking a point was recorded as its own undo step so the first press appeared to do nothing, and confirm this is intended.

Confirm that if the line you are editing gets deleted while you are in its point-editing mode, for example by the other participant in a shared session, later clicks and drags are harmlessly ignored and the app stays responsive instead of throwing errors or freezing.

Confirm that on a Mac, a keyboard shortcut label that contains the word Delete, for example a Delete key entry in the keyboard shortcuts dialog or in a button tooltip, now reads Delete, whereas before this release the automatic key-name conversion rewrote the Del inside such a word and displayed something like Deleteete, and confirm the fix is intended.

Verify that while you are editing the points of a line in a shared session, an edit the other participant makes to that very line does not break your editing session, so you can still grab its point handles afterwards and they move the line at its newest position rather than an out-of-date copy of it.

Check that pressing and holding to drag a point of a multi-point line or arrow keeps the line following the cursor smoothly for the entire drag instead of getting stuck after the first small move, because the shape is now looked up again by its identifier after every tiny update — a lookup that did not exist before this release — and confirm that is intended.

Check that on a Mac, when the hint area at the top of the canvas shows a tip naming a key, for example the tip that appears when a drawn line is selected, key names in that tip are now written in Mac wording such as Cmd or Delete, whereas before this release the tip text was displayed exactly as stored with no key-name conversion, and confirm this conversion is intended.

Verify that pressing Escape while you are editing the points of a line now closes point editing and returns you to the normal cursor with the line left on the canvas, where previously the app stayed in point editing mode when Escape was pressed, and confirm the new exit behaviour is intended.

Confirm that deleting a shape and pressing Ctrl+Z still brings it back exactly as it was, and that in a shared session a deletion still disappears for the other participant, now that the way the drawing keeps its full list of elements has been reorganized.

Check that reopening the app on a drawing saved earlier in the browser starts in normal selection mode with no point-editing handles showing, the same clean start loading always gave before this release, and confirm the new default keeps it that way.

Verify that after you double-click a drawn line so its point editor opens and you then press Undo, the point editor now closes and the canvas returns to the normal selection mode, whereas before this release Undo left the point editor open and appeared to change nothing, and confirm this is intended.

Verify that refreshing the page while a line is in point-editing mode brings the drawing back in normal selection mode instead of reopening with the point handles still active, since this editing state is now left out of the copy saved in the browser, and confirm that is intended.

Verify that starting a completely fresh session shows a blank canvas and that opening a saved file afterwards makes the whole drawing appear at once, since the drawing is now always supplied as one complete batch after an empty start instead of being attached when the session is created as before, and confirm nothing is lost on load.

report.summary: This release adds grid options to the drawing canvas and changes how elements are moved and resized.
keyChanges: A grid was added to the editor canvas: it can be toggled on and off, is off by default on a fresh editor, and draws faint grid lines at a fixed spacing of 20 canvas units.

Saved scene files now store the grid setting alongside the background color, so a drawing saved with the grid on reopens with the grid on, while drawings saved before this change or scenes without the setting open with the grid off.
Because the grid is drawn by the shared canvas renderer used for image output, PNG exports and clipboard copies of a drawing include the grid lines when the grid is on.
Clearing the canvas and importing scenes rebuild the editor state from defaults, so both reset the grid to off.
The shortcuts dialog was also modified as part of this work; its exact new content is not shown in the evidence, so it needs a smoke check that it opens and lists shortcuts correctly.

Text resizing now has a third font-size attempt: when two measurement passes still miss the target box, the font is scaled about 1% smaller and the resize proceeds, whereas previously a single text element's resize was silently skipped and a multi-selection resize containing text could be aborted entirely.

The shared resize-and-rotate routine no longer reads modifier keys from the pointer event itself; the editor now passes discrete-angle, equal-sides, and center-point flags derived from the same key checks, so Shift-based angle snapping, proportional resizing, and center-point resizing should behave exactly as before.

Moving a selected group and sizing a newly drawn shape were extracted into dedicated drag helpers used during canvas pointer drags, so selection dragging and drawing with Shift or the center-point modifier now flow through new code paths and need regression checks.

A new grid mode can be toggled from a new item in the right-click menu on empty canvas and with Ctrl/Cmd plus the apostrophe/quote key; right-clicking an element keeps the previous menu without this item.

With grid on, newly drawn shapes and straight lines start on grid points, and dragging, resizing, and Alt-duplicate copies land on grid points while keeping the position where the user grabbed the selection; free-draw strokes and the marquee selection rectangle stay un-snapped.

With grid on, plain arrow keys now move selected elements by one full grid step and Shift+arrows by the fine amount, inverting the previous plain-small/Shift-larger pattern; with grid off, the previous nudge distances remain.

With grid off, all new grid math falls back to raw cursor coordinates, so existing draw, drag, resize, and duplicate behavior should be unchanged; any snapping or position jump with grid off is a regression.

The new menu label is fetched from translations, and that lookup throws an error when a label is missing, so a language lacking the grid label could prevent the empty-canvas context menu from opening.
qaChecks: Verify a fresh editor shows no grid lines until the grid is toggled on.
Check that toggling the grid on draws faint grid lines at a consistent 20-unit spacing and toggling it off removes them completely.
Confirm the grid stays aligned with the drawing while scrolling and while zooming in and out, with no drifting or doubled lines.
Ensure drawing, selecting, resizing, and moving shapes still work normally with the grid on.
Verify a drawing saved with the grid on reopens with the grid on, and one saved with the grid off reopens with it off.
Check that a drawing saved before this change opens without errors and the grid stays off.
Confirm clearing the canvas resets the grid to off.
Ensure importing a scene that has no grid setting loads without errors and leaves the grid off.
Verify an exported PNG includes the grid lines when the grid is on and has none when the grid is off.
Confirm copying the drawing to the clipboard as a PNG keeps the grid when it is on.
Verify the shortcuts dialog opens and its shortcut list renders completely with no missing entries or errors.
Verify rotating a selected shape while holding Shift snaps the angle to fixed steps, and rotating without Shift follows the pointer freely.

Verify dragging the endpoint of a two-point line or arrow with Shift locks the segment to straight or 45-degree directions, and without Shift the endpoint follows the pointer freely, testing both the start and end handles.
Verify resizing a single shape with Shift keeps its sides equal in length, and resizing with the center-point modifier key grows it symmetrically from its center.

Verify resizing a text element with a corner handle applies the resize and grows the font proportionally with the box, including a text item with a long word or many lines and a very small drag, and confirm the resize now goes through instead of being silently ignored.
Verify selecting the text element together with a rectangle and dragging a corner handle scales every selected element, including the text, in one gesture.
Verify after resizing, the text still fits inside its box with a proportionate font size, allowing that the fallback may settle on a font about 1% smaller than an exact fit.

Verify drawing a rectangle, ellipse, or diamond while holding Shift produces equal sides even when dragging upward or to the left, with the shape staying anchored at the corner where the drag started.
Verify drawing a line or arrow while holding Shift locks it to perfect angles, and that drawing with the center-point modifier key expands the shape symmetrically around the first click point.
Verify dragging a multi-element selection moves the whole group together, preserving the elements' relative positions and following the pointer.

Verify right-clicking empty canvas shows a new grid-mode toggle item and clicking it toggles snapping: with it on a shape drawn between grid positions lands on a grid point, with it off the shape stays at the cursor.
Confirm Ctrl/Cmd plus the apostrophe/quote key (US layout) toggles the same grid state as the menu item.
Verify right-clicking an existing element still shows the previous menu without the grid toggle item.
Ensure that with a non-English interface language, right-clicking empty canvas still opens the menu and shows the grid item translated or in English fallback instead of failing to open.

Verify with grid on that starting a rectangle, ellipse, or diamond at an off-grid cursor position snaps the element's origin to the nearest grid point, and that arrows and lines start and continue on grid points.
Verify with grid on that the free-draw tool still follows the exact cursor path and its strokes are not snapped.
Ensure with grid off that shapes, arrows, and lines start exactly at the cursor position with no snapping, matching pre-change behavior.
Confirm the drag-selection rectangle still tracks the cursor freely with grid on rather than snapping.
Verify with grid on that dragging a selected element, a multi-selection, and a Shift-added element lands the selection on grid points while the grabbed point keeps its offset under the cursor.
Verify with grid on that resizing from a corner or edge handle snaps the element's edges to grid points.
Confirm with grid on that Alt-dragging a selection creates the duplicate on a grid position.
Ensure with grid off that dragging, resizing, and Alt-duplicating place elements exactly as before, with no snapping and no jump on the first move.
Verify with grid on that pressing a plain arrow key moves the selected element exactly one grid step and Shift+arrow moves it by the small fine amount.
Ensure with grid off that plain arrows and Shift+arrows keep the same small and larger step distances as before the change.

Confirm that with the grid mode turned on, dragging an existing selected shape moves it in whole grid steps so it ends up aligned to the grid, whereas before this release it could be dropped at any pixel position.

Confirm that drawing a new rectangle by dragging up and to the left from the point where you pressed down still extends the shape up and to the left with its top-left corner staying under the pointer, as it did before this release.

Check that with the grid mode turned on, selecting the rectangle tool and dragging from a point between two grid lines makes the shape's first corner snap to the nearest grid intersection instead of starting exactly under the pointer as before this release.

Verify: with the grid switched on, draw a shape with a strong red colour and drag and resize it a few times — before this release no grid existed — and confirm the shape keeps its true red on every redraw while the grid stays faint grey underneath it.

Verify: turn the grid on, place a shape, then pan sideways and zoom in and out — before this release you saw only background and shapes — and confirm faint grid lines now cover the canvas, follow the panning, and stay locked to the shapes at every zoom level.

Confirm that selecting two or more shapes and dragging them across the canvas moves the whole group together with the pointer while every shape keeps its position relative to the others, as it did before this release.
Confirm that holding Alt while dragging a corner handle of a selected shape still resizes it equally in all directions from its center, as it did before this release.
Verify that with the grid mode switched off, clicking and dragging still places every element exactly under the pointer with no snapping to invisible lines, matching the previous release.

Confirm that resizing a text element by dragging its corner handle now changes the letter size even at sizes where the text previously stayed frozen at its original size, and that the slightly smaller fitted lettering now produced in those cases is intended.

Confirm that with the grid mode turned on, tapping an arrow key nudges the selected shape by one full grid spacing instead of the previous single-pixel step, and that Shift with an arrow key now nudges one pixel instead of the previous five.

Check that with the grid mode turned on, grabbing a selected shape by a point inside it and dragging does not make the shape jump when the drag starts, keeping the grabbed point under the cursor while it moves in whole grid steps, whereas dragging previously followed the pointer exactly.

Check: click on the drawing canvas, press the control key and apostrophe together — or command and apostrophe on a Mac — which did nothing before this release, and confirm the grid appears, then press the same keys again and confirm it disappears.
Verify that choosing the grid entry from the right-click menu a second time switches the grid back off, so shapes and dragging stop snapping and behave exactly as they did before this release.

Confirm: open the shortcuts overview and look in the view section — previously there was no grid row there — and confirm a grid toggle row now appears showing command with apostrophe on a Mac and control with apostrophe on other systems.

Verify that right-clicking an empty spot on the drawing canvas now shows a new menu entry for toggling the grid mode, which the right-click menu never offered before this release, and that choosing it switches the grid on.
uncertainty: SVG export goes through a separate image path that does not receive the grid setting, so the grid may not appear in exported SVGs even when it is on; confirm the intended behavior for SVG exports.

The discrete-angle, equal-sides, and center-point flags are now derived by the editor before resizing is invoked; the evidence does not prove these derived values match the previous direct Shift handling, so if any snapping or center-resize gesture behaves differently, this mapping is the most likely cause.

The evidence cannot confirm the new grid menu label exists in every translation file, and the lookup throws an error when a label is missing; if any language lacks it, right-clicking empty canvas in that language could fail to open the context menu, so the non-English menu check above is the guard.
