Verify: draw a shape, move it, delete it, and pan and zoom the canvas with the grid switched off, exactly as you did before this release — the only edit here is a blank line, so nothing should change — and confirm the canvas looks and behaves identically to the previous release.

Confirm: open a drawing file saved with the previous release and then start a brand-new drawing — this change only adds an internal description and should alter nothing — and confirm both load without errors and behave exactly as before, with the grid off.

triggers.check: Confirm that with the grid mode turned on, dragging an existing selected shape moves it in whole grid steps so it ends up aligned to the grid, whereas before this release it could be dropped at any pixel position.

Confirm that drawing a new rectangle by dragging up and to the left from the point where you pressed down still extends the shape up and to the left with its top-left corner staying under the pointer, as it did before this release.

Check that with the grid mode turned on, selecting the rectangle tool and dragging from a point between two grid lines makes the shape's first corner snap to the nearest grid intersection instead of starting exactly under the pointer as before this release.

Verify: with the grid switched on, draw a shape with a strong red colour and drag and resize it a few times — before this release no grid existed — and confirm the shape keeps its true red on every redraw while the grid stays faint grey underneath it.

Verify: turn the grid on, place a shape, then pan sideways and zoom in and out — before this release you saw only background and shapes — and confirm faint grid lines now cover the canvas, follow the panning, and stay locked to the shapes at every zoom level.

Confirm that selecting two or more shapes and dragging them across the canvas moves the whole group together with the pointer while every shape keeps its position relative to the others, as it did before this release.
Confirm that holding Alt while dragging a corner handle of a selected shape still resizes it equally in all directions from its center, as it did before this release.
Verify that with the grid mode switched off, clicking and dragging still places every element exactly under the pointer with no snapping to invisible lines, matching the previous release.

Confirm that resizing a text element by dragging its corner handle now changes the letter size even at sizes where the text previously stayed frozen at its original size, and that the slightly smaller fitted lettering now produced in those cases is intended.

Confirm that with the grid mode turned on, tapping an arrow key nudges the selected shape by one full grid spacing instead of the previous single-pixel step, and that Shift with an arrow key now nudges one pixel instead of the previous five.

Check that with the grid mode turned on, grabbing a selected shape by a point inside it and dragging does not make the shape jump when the drag starts, keeping the grabbed point under the cursor while it moves in whole grid steps, whereas dragging previously followed the pointer exactly.

Check: click on the drawing canvas, press the control key and apostrophe together — or command and apostrophe on a Mac — which did nothing before this release, and confirm the grid appears, then press the same keys again and confirm it disappears.
Verify that choosing the grid entry from the right-click menu a second time switches the grid back off, so shapes and dragging stop snapping and behave exactly as they did before this release.

Confirm: open the shortcuts overview and look in the view section — previously there was no grid row there — and confirm a grid toggle row now appears showing command with apostrophe on a Mac and control with apostrophe on other systems.

Verify that right-clicking an empty spot on the drawing canvas now shows a new menu entry for toggling the grid mode, which the right-click menu never offered before this release, and that choosing it switches the grid on.
Confirm that holding Shift while dragging the end of a two-point line or arrow still snaps the dragged end to horizontal, vertical, or 45-degree directions, as it did before this release.
Confirm that holding Shift while rotating a selected shape by its rotation handle still snaps the rotation to 15-degree steps, as it did before this release.

Confirm that holding Shift while turning the rotation handle of a selected shape snaps the rotation to fixed angle steps, and that releasing Shift returns to the smooth free rotation there was before.

Check: turn the grid on, set the zoom to one hundred percent, and confirm the grid squares are twenty pixels wide — before this release there was no grid at all — and that the spacing scales with zoom.

Verify that pressing Control together with the apostrophe key switches the grid mode on and pressing it again switches it off, Command instead of Control on a Mac, a combination that did nothing in the previous release.

Confirm: open a brand-new empty drawing and also open a drawing saved with the previous release — previously neither had any grid notion — and confirm both now open with the grid switched off and the old file still loads fine.

Verify: save a drawing to a file while the grid is switched on, then reopen that same file — previously it reopened with the grid off because the saved file did not remember the setting — and confirm it now reopens with the grid still showing.

Verify: draw a shape, move it, delete it, and pan and zoom the canvas with the grid switched off, exactly as you did before this release — the only edit here is a blank line, so nothing should change — and confirm the canvas looks and behaves identically to the previous release.

Confirm: open a drawing file saved with the previous release and then start a brand-new drawing — this change only adds an internal description and should alter nothing — and confirm both load without errors and behave exactly as before, with the grid off.

report.summary: The release is essentially an under-the-hood reorganization of how live collaboration and drawing loading are wired together, keeping intended behavior the same apart from a few small interface changes, so testing should focus on re-verifying collaboration and loading flows rather than new features.
keyChanges: Live-collaboration plumbing — scene broadcasting, joining a room, merging other users' edits, the collaboration dialog, and its encryption and link parsing — was reorganized into the app's collaboration area, and the broadcast step no longer records the last broadcast or received scene version as it did before, making concurrent-edit merging the top regression risk.

Scene restore now tolerates completely missing data, so the editor can start with nothing to load (empty saved state, a server record without elements or settings, or no initial data) and must show a clean empty canvas instead of failing.

Shared scenes are now loaded through a backend importer that decrypts with an AES-128 key, preserves your locally stored editor settings, uses a fresh random 12-byte initialization value for every encrypted collaboration message, and on a failed fetch or decryption shows a translated import-failed or decryption-failed alert while continuing with an empty canvas.

Collaboration room links are recognized only when the URL hash exactly matches the room pattern (two alphanumeric, underscore or hyphen parts separated by one comma after the room marker), so malformed links must not start or join a session; the collaboration dialog moved with this code and must keep all behavior, including returning keyboard focus to its opening button when closed.

The showcase app now always wraps the editor in a collaboration component; loading drawings from share links, restoring the saved browser draft, and supplying the user's name moved into that wrapper via a deferred initial-data promise, and the editor component itself no longer reads those URLs or shows the scene-override confirmation.

Live collaboration wiring changed: scene changes are now broadcast through the editor's change callback instead of an internal version check, pointer positions are sent through a callback on every move (the old code suppressed broadcasts during multi-touch and for invalid off-screen coordinates), and the connection is no longer torn down by the editor's unload handler.

Default editor state dropped the user-name and collaboration-active fields (the list of collaborators remains and can now be applied through scene updates, and action results may also change collaborating state), while the embeddable API gained a ready promise, a way to read the current drawing, history clearing, scroll-center control, richer scene updates covering elements, app state, collaborators and history recording, and a scene reset with an optional loading-state reset.
Common handlers (keyboard, copy, cut, paste, gestures, wheel panning, scene updates) now batch their state changes into a single render through a new helper.

The showcase app's data handling — importing shareable links, loading scenes, saving to browser storage, and storing encrypted collaboration rooms in Firebase — was relocated from the shared editor package into the app-specific layer; the features are unchanged in intent, but all of their wiring is new and needs end-to-end regression testing.

Scene loading from links now runs in the app wrapper: a share link opened over a non-empty drawing asks for confirmation before replacing it and clears the link from the address bar once confirmed or declined, an empty canvas loads without asking, and a prompt triggered while the tab is in the background waits until the tab is focused.
Rejoining the same collaboration room link within 15 seconds of leaving it now bypasses the confirmation prompt and reloads the room directly.

Every drawing change is saved to browser storage through a 300 millisecond debounced saver that also flushes when the window loses focus, and during live sessions each change is broadcast to other participants; changing the URL hash of a fully loaded editor now reloads that scene.

The old username-saving hook and the shared package's backend-import, socket-server, and Firebase helpers were removed in favor of app-local equivalents, so display-name persistence and room save/load must still work through the new paths.

The collaboration entry point is redesigned: the old room dialog (with room create/destroy and username editing) in the canvas actions row and the mobile canvas menu is replaced by a new collaboration button with a users icon, a visible collaborator count badge when at least one other person is present, a highlighted style during an active session, and an analytics event fired on click.

Collaboration internals were moved out of the core editor component, including the periodic full-scene sync broadcast, the save of the collaboration room to storage when the tab is closed or the portal is closed, the collaborator-list update from socket events, the rule that re-opening the same collaboration link within 15 seconds reloads without prompting, and the batching wrapper used by many input handlers. End-to-end collaboration behaviour should be unchanged, but the wiring was re-routed and must be re-verified.
The mouse-location broadcast sent to other collaborators no longer includes the sender's selected elements, so remote pointers may behave differently when the sender has elements selected.

When the editor is torn down, the hash-change and before-unload listeners are no longer removed during cleanup, which risks stale page-close handlers if the editor is remounted in the same page session.

The menu components' collaboration inputs changed shape (a single optional button click handler plus an is-collaborating flag instead of room-create/destroy and username handlers); if a collaborator count is exactly 0 the badge is hidden, at 1 or more it shows the number.

Starting, joining, and leaving a live collaboration session (share-link generation, connecting to the room, applying remote drawing updates, and cleanup on exit) was removed from the core editor and now lives in the dedicated collaboration wrapper, so the whole collaboration flow needs end-to-end retesting.

The tab-close safeguard that force-saved unsynced collaboration changes, asked the user to confirm leaving, and set a flag to force a full scene reload on the next visit was removed from the core editor along with its stored flag key.

Saved and exported editor state no longer contains the collaborator name or an is-collaborating marker (the name was previously also kept in browser storage), and Clear Canvas no longer carries that field while still preserving background color, grid, embed, and watermark settings and committing the clear to undo history.

The embeddable editor's public surface changed for integrators: the imperative API now always exposes history clearing, scroll-centering, scene-element getters, and a readiness promise, and component props gained optional width/height, promise-or-null initial data, a renamed ref, and collaboration callbacks (a collaboration button handler, a collaborating flag, and pointer updates) replacing the old username callback.

A debounced helper's flush now skips the callback when the helper was never called, where it previously ran it with no data, and timing constants such as the 300 ms double-tap and 500 ms touch-menu delays moved files with unchanged values.

The collaboration code was moved into the app's collaboration layer, and the connection sender no longer gathers drawing elements itself: callers now pass the exact elements to sync, including the full-scene send that greets each newly joined participant, and a full-scene send while collaborating now also saves the drawing to the room's storage.

Same-element conflict handling changed its data source: incoming remote updates for an element you are actively dragging, resizing, or text-editing are now skipped based on a snapshot of editor state captured when your last local change was broadcast, not the app's live state, so the protection depends on that snapshot being current.

Leaving a session is now handled by the session coordinator: closing or refreshing the tab in an active session with unsaved changes saves the drawing and raises the browser's leave confirmation, and unloading disconnects you so other participants stop seeing your cursor and name.

Participant tracking rebuilds the collaborator list from the server's participant list on every change, so departed participants disappear cleanly, and a user's saved name is restored from local storage when a session starts.

Collaboration internals were relocated into the app-specific folder (live connection layer, room dialog, encrypted scene storage, collaboration-link generation) and the storage accessor was simplified; no behavior change is intended, so existing live-session, save-on-leave, and link flows must still work unchanged.

Live pointer updates now report the sender's selected elements from the editor's live app state, falling back to an empty selection when that state is unavailable; other participants must still see which elements are selected, and pointer updates must not fail when nothing is selected.

The embeddable editor component's public properties changed: integrators now hand the editor's imperative API reference through a new dedicated property instead of the old forwarding property, and the username-change callback was replaced by collaboration properties for a collaboration button, a collaborating flag, and live pointer updates, with the collaboration button callback defaulting to no action when not supplied.
The package also newly exports scene-comparison helpers for integrators.

Starting a live session now creates a shareable room link in the page address and deliberately clears the undo history first, so elements deleted before the session starts are not persisted to the shared room for joiners to see.

Syncing is rebuilt: a joiner loads the room's drawing on entry (with a timeout fallback if the initial scene message never arrives), remote edits are merged with local ones without being echoed back to other users, and the local undo history is cleared whenever a collaborator's change arrives, so undo/redo cannot restore elements after a remote update.
Your cursor position is shared with other collaborators only while a single pointer is active; during two-finger (multi-touch) gestures pointer updates pause and must resume cleanly afterwards.

The collaboration dialog now shows a start-session state and, once live, the room link with a copy button (a failed copy raises an error dialog), a link field that selects its whole text on click or tap, and a name field whose value is remembered between visits; closing the dialog returns keyboard focus to the collaboration button.
Stopping a session saves the room's content, restores the plain app address with no room link, and disconnects the collaborator.
qaChecks: Verify that a user joining an existing room immediately sees the full current drawing, and that changes drawn by either user appear in the other window within moments.
Test simultaneous edits: have both users drag or resize the same element at the same time and confirm neither window loses the element and both scenes end up consistent.
Confirm a room link whose hash has been altered (extra characters, an unsupported character, or a missing part) does not silently start or join a session and instead opens as a normal local drawing.
Ensure reloading or reopening the same room link after leaving restores the previously saved room content, confirming rooms saved before this change still decrypt and load.
Verify the editor opens with an empty canvas, a sensible default scroll position, and no error when there is nothing to load at startup.
Ensure opening a local .excalidraw file (via the open dialog or by dropping it on the canvas) still loads its drawing and view settings exactly as before.
Confirm the load-scene action in the save/export menu still opens a saved JSON drawing without errors.
Validate that an existing shared-scene link loads the drawing content and keeps your locally stored editor settings instead of overwriting them with the shared record.
Check that a broken or expired link shows an import-failed alert in the selected interface language and leaves an empty, usable canvas rather than crashing.
Confirm a shared record that lacks elements or settings still opens without an error.
Verify the dialog shows the start-session state when no session is active and the share-link, copy, username and stop-session controls during a session, on both desktop and mobile.
Ensure the copy control places the room link on the clipboard and that focusing the link input selects its text.
Confirm closing the dialog (close button or Enter in the username field) closes it and returns keyboard focus to the toolbar button that opened it.
Check the collaboration toolbar button shows the count of other participants during a session.

Verify each participant's named cursor follows their mouse across the whole window, including dragging the pointer against and past the window edges where coordinates can become invalid; the remote cursor should not freeze, vanish, or jump.
Test a two-finger pinch-zoom on a touch device while collaborating: the other participant should not see flickering or duplicated remote cursors.

Confirm edits (draw a rectangle, move it) made by one participant appear on the other participant's canvas within about a second without reloading, since syncing now runs through the editor's change callback.

Ensure closing or reloading one participant's tab ends their session cleanly (cursor disappears for the other side), the remaining participants still sync, and a display name entered for collaboration persists after reload.
Confirm a ?id= link and a #json= link each load that drawing into the canvas, and that when a non-empty local draft exists the same override prompt appears before it is replaced.
Verify that after drawing something and fully reloading the page the draft reappears and the canvas is not stuck blank or loading, since initial data now arrives through a deferred promise.
Ensure drag-and-dropping a .excalidraw file still loads its contents into the current scene.

Verify the API is available immediately on mount, that reading the current drawing returns the drawn shapes, and that updating only the background color changes the background without clearing or replacing existing shapes (the old version required the drawing to be supplied alongside).

Test updating the collaborator list from the API and confirm each collaborator's name and cursor appear for the other side, then repeat with history recording enabled and confirm one undo step removes the change.
Ensure the scene-reset API call clears all shapes, keeps the current appearance, and leaves the loading indicator untouched unless the loading-reset option is passed.
Verify copy, cut, and paste of selected shapes still work and keyboard undo/redo steps exactly one change per press, since handlers now batch state updates into single renders.
Confirm middle-mouse or space-drag panning, mouse-wheel scrolling, and touch gestures still pan and zoom the canvas smoothly.
Ensure resizing the browser window keeps the canvas filling the viewport (sizes now default to window dimensions), and clear-canvas and background-color changes still apply.

Verify opening a share link while the canvas holds a saved drawing shows a browser confirmation prompt; confirming replaces the canvas with the linked drawing and removes the link from the address bar, while declining keeps your existing drawing.
Verify opening a share link with an empty canvas loads the linked drawing immediately without any prompt.
Verify opening a share link while the tab is in the background and then switching to that tab still shows the prompt and loads the linked drawing.

Verify a legacy share link, which carries the scene id in the page address instead of the URL hash, still loads its drawing; the old shared importer for this format was removed, so this is the input most likely to break.
Verify leaving a collaboration room and reopening the same room link within 15 seconds joins the room directly, without the confirmation prompt.
Verify reopening the same room link more than 15 seconds after leaving still asks before replacing your current drawing.
Verify two people in the same room see each other's drawing changes appear live as they are made.
Verify a person who joins after others have been drawing for a while receives the complete up-to-date scene, not just recent changes.
Verify closing the browser tab during a session saves the room, so reopening the same room link afterwards still shows the stored scene.

Verify drawing a few shapes, waiting about a second, and reloading the page restores the drawing; also verify switching to another window and back right after drawing does not lose the newest strokes.
Verify pasting a different scene or room link into the address bar of an already-open, fully loaded editor switches the canvas to that scene without restarting the page.
Verify setting your display name and reloading the page keeps the same name, since the previous saving path was removed.
Verify the collaboration button appears in the desktop toolbar where the old room dialog used to be, and in the mobile canvas menu, with a users icon and the collaboration dialog label.
Check that with one collaborator present the button shows the collaborator count badge, and with an empty session (0 collaborators) the badge is hidden.
Confirm the button is visually highlighted while a collaboration session is active and returns to normal styling after leaving the session.
Ensure clicking the button opens the collaboration flow (it now delegates to a click handler instead of managing rooms and usernames directly) and does not silently do nothing.
Verify that drawing changes made in one session still appear in the other session, including periodic full-scene sync (draw something, wait, and confirm the other side catches up).
Confirm the collaborator list updates correctly when a user joins and leaves, so participant pointers and the user list stay accurate.
Ensure closing the browser tab during an active session still saves the room as before, with no duplicated save on page close.

Test a collaborator moving their pointer on the canvas while they have elements selected (the broadcast no longer carries their selection) and verify their pointer still appears and tracks correctly on your canvas.
Confirm pointer broadcast still works when nothing is selected, so basic presence display is not regressed.
Verify keyboard shortcuts, copy and cut, paste from the clipboard, and paste of spreadsheet data still work after the input-handler batching was re-wired.
Check mouse-wheel zoom and panning the canvas by wheel or space-drag still respond smoothly without visual glitches.
Confirm touch gestures (pinch zoom, gesture start/change/end), window resize, text editing via double-click, and the canvas context menu still behave as before.

Test reopening the exact same collaboration link within 15 seconds of closing it and verify the room loads; previously this reloaded without a prompt, so flag any unexpected reload prompt or stuck loading state as a change in behaviour.

Verify that starting a shared session puts a collaboration link in the address bar and that opening it in the second browser joins the same room within a few seconds, shows the sharer's current drawing centered in view with elements deleted before sharing absent, and clears the loading state.

Ensure concurrent edits sync in both directions (add a shape in one session, move or delete it in the other), that each participant's pointer is visible while drawing, and that a participant who leaves stops appearing on the other canvases.

Ensure that closing or reloading a tab immediately after making an edit does not silently drop that change from the shared drawing for the remaining participants, since the old confirm-before-leave protection no longer runs from the core editor.

Confirm that navigating to a different collaboration link within the same tab loads that other room's drawing instead of keeping the previous scene, because address-bar hash changes are no longer handled inside the core editor.
Ensure that drawing a few elements, waiting about a second for the automatic save, and reloading the page restores the drawing along with view settings such as background color.

Check that opening the app without editing anything and then reloading or closing the tab causes no error and leaves a previously saved drawing intact, because a forced save with no pending edit now skips instead of running with no data.
Verify whether a collaborator name asked for or displayed anywhere still persists after a reload, since name storage was removed from the editor's saved state and it may now start blank.
Confirm that clearing the canvas removes all elements, that Undo brings them back, and that settings such as background color, grid, export options, and watermark choice survive the clear.

Verify that the editor still mounts filling the window and is fully interactive, since explicit size settings are now optional and the ref-based API (readiness promise, history clearing, scene-element access) changed shape for external embedders.
Verify that when the second browser joins via the collaboration link, it loads the complete current drawing and the first browser's drawing is unchanged.

Test the same element edited by both users at once: with user A holding a drag, resize, or text edit on one element, have user B move that same element, then have A finish; confirm A's in-progress gesture is not interrupted and, once both finish, exactly one version of the element remains with the later edit applied and no duplicate or lost element.
Confirm that while one user is actively dragging an element, the other user's change to a different element still arrives for both users with neither change lost.

Check that closing or refreshing the tab while the session has changes not yet saved shows the browser's leave-site confirmation, and choosing to stay keeps the session connected with the drawing intact.
Verify that after leaving the session (confirming the leave or closing the tab), the latest drawing is persisted, so opening the same collaboration link in a fresh browser loads the saved drawing.
Confirm that after both users stay connected through a periodic full-scene refresh, their drawings remain identical with no missing or duplicated elements.
Ensure that when one participant leaves or closes their tab, their cursor and name disappear from the remaining participants' canvases and the connection ends cleanly.
Ensure a participant who rejoins the same collaboration link receives the current drawing and their previously used name is restored on the canvas.
Verify that drawing, moving, and deleting elements in one window appears in the other window within a few seconds.

Verify that selecting one or more elements (including right after joining the room) highlights the same elements for the other participant, and that with nothing selected both windows still show live pointers without errors.
Verify that after making edits, leaving the page saves them and reloading the collaboration link restores the latest drawing, including for a participant joining the same link later.
Verify the embedded editor renders and basic drawing works when only default properties are supplied (no collaboration properties passed).
Verify the editor's imperative API reference is delivered to the host through the new dedicated property once the editor mounts, and that a reference attached in the standard way also arrives.

Verify the host receives live pointer updates as the pointer moves in the embedded editor, and that the handler supplied for the collaboration button is invoked when a collaboration session is started from the embedded editor.

Verify that an integration still passing the old properties (the old API-forwarding property and the username-change callback) no longer receives the editor API or username updates, confirming the migration to the new properties.
Verify basic drawing, selecting, moving, resizing, and undo still work on the main page after the reorganization.
Verify the collaboration dialog still opens from the editor and shows the session link with a working copy action during an active session.
Verify that the second user, opening the shared room link, sees the first user's current drawing immediately without the first user redrawing anything.
Check that a shape drawn, moved, and then deleted by one user appears as drawn, moved, and deleted on the other user's canvas, with no element later reverting or appearing twice.

Test that when one user undoes their most recently drawn shape, that shape also disappears on the other user's canvas; broadcasting is gated on the scene version increasing, so an undo is the input most likely to be skipped.

Verify cursor presence: with a single mouse or pen pointer the other user sees your cursor move, and after a two-finger pinch-zoom gesture pointer sharing resumes normally with no stuck or ghost cursor.
Ensure that after deleting some shapes and then starting a session, a user joining the room link never sees the deleted shapes, even after refreshing their page.

Confirm that starting a session replaces the page address with a shareable room link while the visible drawing stays unchanged, and that undo or redo afterwards does not resurrect pre-session deletions.
Confirm that stopping the session restores the plain app address without the room link and that refreshing afterwards does not rejoin the room or show other collaborators.
Check that pressing start again while already in a session does not open a second connection or duplicate your own presence.

Verify the copy control puts the full room link on the clipboard so pasting it in a new browser opens the same shared drawing, and that if copying is blocked an error dialog appears and the link field text becomes selected.
Check that clicking or tapping the link field selects the entire link text in one action.
Confirm a name typed into the name field is remembered after closing and reopening the dialog and after a page reload, and that pressing Enter in the field closes the dialog.
Ensure that after closing the dialog, keyboard focus returns to the collaboration button so keyboard users are not stranded.
Verify that refreshing the page during a session reconnects using the room link in the address bar and the shared drawing reloads with all collaborators' content.

Check that with a heavily throttled network, a joiner whose initial scene message is delayed still ends up seeing the room's drawing through the fallback instead of an empty canvas or endless loading.

Verify that when a collaborator is still on the previous release and moves their mouse over the canvas, their named cursor appears on your screen, whereas before this release cursors sent by that older version were not displayed.
Verify that pressing the Enter key while typing your name in the name field closes the dialog, and that typing into the room link field does not change the link because it is read-only.

Confirm that while you are holding the pointer down dragging or resizing a shape and a collaborator's update to that same shape arrives, the incoming copy is skipped so your drag is not snapped out of your hand — the decision now reads the live interaction snapshot that updates on every pointer move instead of the last rendered screen state, which could lag a moment behind.
Verify that when the browser refuses to copy the room link, an error popup appears describing the problem instead of nothing happening as before.
Verify that when you open the collaboration dialog with the keyboard, focus moves into the dialog onto its controls so tabbing continues from there rather than staying behind on the toolbar.

Confirm that while you are in a shared room with changes not yet saved to the cloud, closing or reloading the tab makes the browser ask for confirmation and, if you choose to stay, the drawing is uploaded to the cloud at once — before this release the tab simply closed and nothing was saved.
Verify that when you open a room link, the canvas scrolls so the shared drawing is centered on your screen instead of leaving you in a blank area with the drawing off-screen as before.

Verify that after you press start session, pressing Ctrl+Z does not bring back anything you drew or deleted beforehand, since the undo history is now wiped when the room is created; confirm that wiping is intended.
Verify that if you draw something during a live session and close the tab right away, a person opening that room link afterwards still sees the drawing, since the last-second change used to be lost.

Confirm that opening a shared-room link in a fresh browser tab and then immediately reloading that tab — without drawing anything — now brings up the browser's leave-confirmation prompt, where before this release the tab reloaded silently.

Confirm that when a participant closes their tab their cursor and name disappear from your canvas immediately, and if that same person rejoins they appear as a plain cursor with no name until they move, instead of keeping stale details from their earlier visit — before this release stale participant details could persist.

Confirm that the automatic whole-drawing re-send happens on a long interval rather than on every stroke, and that a small edit made immediately after it still reaches the other participants — before this release the change counter was advanced during every send, so confirm the new arrangement does not swallow the next edit.

Verify that when two people edit the drawing at the same time, for example each dragging the same rectangle, both screens settle on one final result instead of the shape flickering back and forth as each side echoed the other's change.

Confirm that when you open the collaboration dialog the name you saved in an earlier session is already filled in, and on a device where no name was ever saved the field starts empty rather than erroring or showing leftover text — before this release the saved name was not reliably restored on load.

Confirm that after two people have edited a shared room, reopening the same room link later in a fresh browser shows the latest combined drawing rather than an older copy — before this release the cloud copy could lag behind what was on screen.
uncertainty: Navigation steps and exact labels for the collaboration entry points were not supplied, so testers must locate them in the editor toolbar and mobile menu; the clearest proven old-versus-new difference is missing scene data at startup (previously it would fail, now it must open empty), while for the collaboration relocation no single input was proven to change, so the simultaneous-edit check targets the removed scene-version bookkeeping in broadcasting as the suspected regression risk.

Pointer updates are now sent for cases the old code suppressed (multi-touch and invalid off-screen coordinates), and how the collaboration layer filters them is not established by the evidence; treat a remote cursor that flickers during pinch-zoom or misbehaves when the pointer leaves the window as the most likely regression in this group.

The shared editor package lost its scene-loading, backend-import, and socket-server helpers while the main editor component still referenced them in this group's evidence; the compensating changes belong to other groups, so whether the embeddable editor used by integrating developers still initializes and loads scenes is not settled here.

The collaboration save-on-close, force-reload-within-15-seconds, and full-scene sync logic was removed from the core editor component and presumably re-homed in the collaboration layer; the diff only shows the removal, so if any piece was dropped rather than moved, those behaviours would silently regress and the checks above are the safety net. Also, if the editor component is embedded and remounted in one page session, stale before-unload handlers could now survive teardown, causing duplicate save prompts on tab close; this was not directly testable from the supplied evidence.

The collaboration leave-page safeguard (confirm prompt, last-moment save, and the force-full-reload flag) was removed from the core editor; whether the relocated collaboration code reintroduces that protection is outside this batch's evidence and should be confirmed with the collaboration change group before release.

The skip of remote updates for an element under active local editing now relies on an editor-state snapshot that is refreshed only when the local user's changes are broadcast; the evidence does not show how fresh that snapshot is mid-gesture, so simultaneous edits of one element could behave differently than before (a needed remote update skipped, or applied mid-drag) — the concurrent same-element check is the place to watch.

The embeddable component's removed properties (the old API-forwarding property and the username-change callback) were replaced without a visible compatibility path; whether existing published integrations rely on them could not be confirmed from the supplied evidence.

Every changed function in this group ships only new code in the diff with no removed lines, so the previous behavior could not be compared line by line; the highest-risk boundaries (undo propagation under the version-gated broadcast, single- versus multi-pointer cursor sharing, and undo history being cleared on remote updates) are read from the new logic and should be treated as prime regression suspects rather than proven changes.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied; from the drawing editor, open the live-collaboration dialog from the editor's canvas-action toolbar on desktop (or the mobile menu on small screens), start a session, and open the shared room link in a second browser window.
testAreas.access: Diagram creators acting as live collaborators; no account requirements were supplied.
testAreas.setup: Two browser windows or devices, with a drawing containing several shapes in the first one.
checks: Verify that a user joining an existing room immediately sees the full current drawing, and that changes drawn by either user appear in the other window within moments.
Test simultaneous edits: have both users drag or resize the same element at the same time and confirm neither window loses the element and both scenes end up consistent.
Confirm a room link whose hash has been altered (extra characters, an unsupported character, or a missing part) does not silently start or join a session and instead opens as a normal local drawing.
Ensure reloading or reopening the same room link after leaving restores the previously saved room content, confirming rooms saved before this change still decrypt and load.

testAreas.area: Scene loading and app startup with missing data
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied; open the editor normally (fresh browser profile or cleared storage), and use the file-open or drag-and-drop path for local drawings.
testAreas.access: Diagram creators; anyone opening the editor.
testAreas.setup: A browser profile with no saved drawing, plus one valid .excalidraw file saved earlier.
checks: Verify the editor opens with an empty canvas, a sensible default scroll position, and no error when there is nothing to load at startup.
Ensure opening a local .excalidraw file (via the open dialog or by dropping it on the canvas) still loads its drawing and view settings exactly as before.
Confirm the load-scene action in the save/export menu still opens a saved JSON drawing without errors.

testAreas.area: Shared scene links and backend import

checks: Validate that an existing shared-scene link loads the drawing content and keeps your locally stored editor settings instead of overwriting them with the shared record.
Check that a broken or expired link shows an import-failed alert in the selected interface language and leaves an empty, usable canvas rather than crashing.
Confirm a shared record that lacks elements or settings still opens without an error.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied; from the editor toolbar on desktop (or the mobile menu on small screens), open the live-collaboration dialog.
testAreas.access: Diagram creators and live collaborators.
testAreas.setup: One active collaboration session to see the share-link state.
checks: Verify the dialog shows the start-session state when no session is active and the share-link, copy, username and stop-session controls during a session, on both desktop and mobile.
Ensure the copy control places the room link on the clipboard and that focusing the link input selects its text.
Confirm closing the dialog (close button or Enter in the username field) closes it and returns keyboard focus to the toolbar button that opened it.
Check the collaboration toolbar button shows the count of other participants during a session.

testAreas.howToReach: No navigation details were supplied; open the Excalidraw editor in the browser, start or join a live-collaboration session from the app's collaboration/share entry point, and open the same session in a second browser.
testAreas.access: Any user who can open the editor; both session participants.
testAreas.setup: Two browsers (one touch device for the pinch check), a small drawing, and a shared session link.
checks: Verify each participant's named cursor follows their mouse across the whole window, including dragging the pointer against and past the window edges where coordinates can become invalid; the remote cursor should not freeze, vanish, or jump.
Test a two-finger pinch-zoom on a touch device while collaborating: the other participant should not see flickering or duplicated remote cursors.

Confirm edits (draw a rectangle, move it) made by one participant appear on the other participant's canvas within about a second without reloading, since syncing now runs through the editor's change callback.

Ensure closing or reloading one participant's tab ends their session cleanly (cursor disappears for the other side), the remaining participants still sync, and a display name entered for collaboration persists after reload.

testAreas.area: Opening drawings: share links, saved drafts, and imported files
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation details were supplied; open the editor's web address directly with a drawing link (?id=... or #json=...), or open the editor normally and use its open/import entry point.
testAreas.access: Any user.
testAreas.setup: One saved share link, one .excalidraw file, and an existing local draft in browser storage.
checks: Confirm a ?id= link and a #json= link each load that drawing into the canvas, and that when a non-empty local draft exists the same override prompt appears before it is replaced.
Verify that after drawing something and fully reloading the page the draft reappears and the canvas is not stuck blank or loading, since initial data now arrives through a deferred promise.
Ensure drag-and-dropping a .excalidraw file still loads its contents into the current scene.

testAreas.howToReach: No navigation details were supplied; embed the Excalidraw React component in a scratch page per the integration docs and call the exposed API from a ref.
testAreas.access: Integrating developer.
testAreas.setup: A minimal host page that mounts the editor component and exposes its API.
checks: Verify the API is available immediately on mount, that reading the current drawing returns the drawn shapes, and that updating only the background color changes the background without clearing or replacing existing shapes (the old version required the drawing to be supplied alongside).

Test updating the collaborator list from the API and confirm each collaborator's name and cursor appear for the other side, then repeat with history recording enabled and confirm one undo step removes the change.
Ensure the scene-reset API call clears all shapes, keeps the current appearance, and leaves the loading indicator untouched unless the loading-reset option is passed.

testAreas.howToReach: No navigation details were supplied; open the editor in the browser and use the canvas as usual.
testAreas.access: Any user.
testAreas.setup: A few drawn shapes.
checks: Verify copy, cut, and paste of selected shapes still work and keyboard undo/redo steps exactly one change per press, since handlers now batch state updates into single renders.
Confirm middle-mouse or space-drag panning, mouse-wheel scrolling, and touch gestures still pan and zoom the canvas smoothly.
Ensure resizing the browser window keeps the canvas filling the viewport (sizes now default to window dimensions), and clear-canvas and background-color changes still apply.

testAreas.area: Opening shared scene links (current and legacy link formats)
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; open the Excalidraw editor in a browser, then open a scene link (a URL carrying the scene id, in either the current hash-based format or the legacy page-address format) in the same tab.

Verify opening a share link with an empty canvas loads the linked drawing immediately without any prompt.
Verify opening a share link while the tab is in the background and then switching to that tab still shows the prompt and loads the linked drawing.

Verify a legacy share link, which carries the scene id in the page address instead of the URL hash, still loads its drawing; the old shared importer for this format was removed, so this is the input most likely to break.

testAreas.area: Rejoining a collaboration room right after leaving it
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; open a collaboration room link in the editor, leave the room, and reopen the same link.
testAreas.access: Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: A collaboration room link and a non-empty local drawing that would be replaced by joining.
checks: Verify leaving a collaboration room and reopening the same room link within 15 seconds joins the room directly, without the confirmation prompt.
Verify reopening the same room link more than 15 seconds after leaving still asks before replacing your current drawing.

testAreas.area: Live collaboration syncing and encrypted room storage
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; create a collaboration link from the app's share feature and open it in two browsers.
testAreas.access: Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: Two browsers or people and one collaboration room link created from the share feature.
checks: Verify two people in the same room see each other's drawing changes appear live as they are made.
Verify a person who joins after others have been drawing for a while receives the complete up-to-date scene, not just recent changes.
Verify closing the browser tab during a session saves the room, so reopening the same room link afterwards still shows the stored scene.

testAreas.area: Local autosave of drawings and reloading links in an open editor
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; open the editor, draw on the canvas, then use the browser address bar and page reload.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor
testAreas.setup: A browser session with site data storage allowed.
checks: Verify drawing a few shapes, waiting about a second, and reloading the page restores the drawing; also verify switching to another window and back right after drawing does not lose the newest strokes.
Verify pasting a different scene or room link into the address bar of an already-open, fully loaded editor switches the canvas to that scene without restarting the page.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; open the editor, set your display name in the collaboration controls, and reload the page.
testAreas.access: Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: A browser session where a display name can be set.
checks: Verify setting your display name and reloading the page keeps the same name, since the previous saving path was removed.

testAreas.area: Collaboration button in the editor toolbar and mobile menu
testAreas.howToReach: Open the Excalidraw editor (navigation details were not supplied in the release context) and look at the canvas actions row in the top-left menu; on mobile, open the canvas actions menu in the bottom bar.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor
testAreas.setup: A second browser session joined to the same collaboration session, so the collaborator count is at least 1.
checks: Verify the collaboration button appears in the desktop toolbar where the old room dialog used to be, and in the mobile canvas menu, with a users icon and the collaboration dialog label.
Check that with one collaborator present the button shows the collaborator count badge, and with an empty session (0 collaborators) the badge is hidden.
Confirm the button is visually highlighted while a collaboration session is active and returns to normal styling after leaving the session.
Ensure clicking the button opens the collaboration flow (it now delegates to a click handler instead of managing rooms and usernames directly) and does not silently do nothing.

testAreas.area: Live collaboration sync and room save
testAreas.howToReach: Open the Excalidraw editor, start or join a collaboration session, and edit the drawing (navigation details were not supplied).
testAreas.access: Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: Two browser sessions in the same encrypted collaboration link, each with the drawing loaded.
checks: Verify that drawing changes made in one session still appear in the other session, including periodic full-scene sync (draw something, wait, and confirm the other side catches up).
Confirm the collaborator list updates correctly when a user joins and leaves, so participant pointers and the user list stay accurate.
Ensure closing the browser tab during an active session still saves the room as before, with no duplicated save on page close.

testAreas.area: Remote collaborator pointers while elements are selected
testAreas.howToReach: Join the same collaboration session in two browser sessions and move the mouse over the canvas in one while watching the other.
testAreas.access: Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: Two sessions in one collaboration room; in the sending session select one or more elements before moving the pointer.
checks: Test a collaborator moving their pointer on the canvas while they have elements selected (the broadcast no longer carries their selection) and verify their pointer still appears and tracks correctly on your canvas.
Confirm pointer broadcast still works when nothing is selected, so basic presence display is not regressed.

testAreas.howToReach: Open the Excalidraw editor and interact with the canvas with keyboard, mouse, wheel, touch gestures, and clipboard.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor
testAreas.setup: A drawing with a few shapes and a text element.
checks: Verify keyboard shortcuts, copy and cut, paste from the clipboard, and paste of spreadsheet data still work after the input-handler batching was re-wired.
Check mouse-wheel zoom and panning the canvas by wheel or space-drag still respond smoothly without visual glitches.
Confirm touch gestures (pinch zoom, gesture start/change/end), window resize, text editing via double-click, and the canvas context menu still behave as before.

testAreas.howToReach: Open a collaboration link, leave or close the tab, and reopen the same link within 15 seconds.
testAreas.access: Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: A valid collaboration link and a drawing already shared in it.
checks: Test reopening the exact same collaboration link within 15 seconds of closing it and verify the room loads; previously this reloaded without a prompt, so flag any unexpected reload prompt or stuck loading state as a change in behaviour.

testAreas.area: Live collaboration session (share link, joining, syncing, leaving)
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not supplied for this area: open the Excalidraw showcase app, draw some content, and start a live collaboration session from its share entry point so a collaboration link appears in the address bar; then open that link in a second browser or private window.
testAreas.access: Diagram creators and live collaborators; anyone who has the collaboration link.
testAreas.setup: Two independent browser sessions (or two browsers) sharing one collaboration link, a drawing with several shapes, and one element deleted before sharing.
checks: Verify that starting a shared session puts a collaboration link in the address bar and that opening it in the second browser joins the same room within a few seconds, shows the sharer's current drawing centered in view with elements deleted before sharing absent, and clears the loading state.

Ensure concurrent edits sync in both directions (add a shape in one session, move or delete it in the other), that each participant's pointer is visible while drawing, and that a participant who leaves stops appearing on the other canvases.

Ensure that closing or reloading a tab immediately after making an edit does not silently drop that change from the shared drawing for the remaining participants, since the old confirm-before-leave protection no longer runs from the core editor.

Confirm that navigating to a different collaboration link within the same tab loads that other room's drawing instead of keeping the previous scene, because address-bar hash changes are no longer handled inside the core editor.

testAreas.area: Drawing autosave and restore in browser storage
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not supplied for this area: open the Excalidraw showcase app, draw on the canvas, and reload the page.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator or editor.
testAreas.setup: A browser profile with a previously saved drawing for the restore case, and a clean session for the no-edit case.
checks: Ensure that drawing a few elements, waiting about a second for the automatic save, and reloading the page restores the drawing along with view settings such as background color.

Check that opening the app without editing anything and then reloading or closing the tab causes no error and leaves a previously saved drawing intact, because a forced save with no pending edit now skips instead of running with no data.
Verify whether a collaborator name asked for or displayed anywhere still persists after a reload, since name storage was removed from the editor's saved state and it may now start blank.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not supplied for this area: with a drawing open in the editor, run the clear-canvas action from the editor's actions.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator or editor.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with several shapes and a customized background color or grid setting.
checks: Confirm that clearing the canvas removes all elements, that Undo brings them back, and that settings such as background color, grid, export options, and watermark choice survive the clear.

testAreas.area: Embeddable editor mounting and public API
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not supplied for this area: load the Excalidraw showcase app, which mounts the embeddable editor component.
testAreas.access: Integrating developers embedding the editor component.
testAreas.setup: The showcase app running normally.
checks: Verify that the editor still mounts filling the window and is fully interactive, since explicit size settings are now optional and the ref-based API (readiness promise, history clearing, scene-element access) changed shape for external embedders.

testAreas.area: Live session scene sync between two users
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; test through the live-collaboration flow by creating a shared session and opening its collaboration link in two separate browsers.
testAreas.access: Any user of the editor acting as a live collaborator; no special role or account indicated.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with several distinct elements, one collaboration link shared between two browser sessions.
checks: Verify that when the second browser joins via the collaboration link, it loads the complete current drawing and the first browser's drawing is unchanged.

Test the same element edited by both users at once: with user A holding a drag, resize, or text edit on one element, have user B move that same element, then have A finish; confirm A's in-progress gesture is not interrupted and, once both finish, exactly one version of the element remains with the later edit applied and no duplicate or lost element.
Confirm that while one user is actively dragging an element, the other user's change to a different element still arrives for both users with neither change lost.

testAreas.area: Session saving and recovery on leave or reload
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; use the same live-collaboration session reached via a collaboration link as in the first area.
testAreas.access: Any user of the editor acting as a live collaborator; no special role or account indicated.
testAreas.setup: An active two-user session with at least one change made after joining.
checks: Check that closing or refreshing the tab while the session has changes not yet saved shows the browser's leave-site confirmation, and choosing to stay keeps the session connected with the drawing intact.
Verify that after leaving the session (confirming the leave or closing the tab), the latest drawing is persisted, so opening the same collaboration link in a fresh browser loads the saved drawing.
Confirm that after both users stay connected through a periodic full-scene refresh, their drawings remain identical with no missing or duplicated elements.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; use a live-collaboration session reached via a collaboration link with three browsers.
testAreas.access: Any user of the editor acting as a live collaborator; no special role or account indicated.
testAreas.setup: Three browser sessions joined to the same collaboration room.
checks: Ensure that when one participant leaves or closes their tab, their cursor and name disappear from the remaining participants' canvases and the connection ends cleanly.
Ensure a participant who rejoins the same collaboration link receives the current drawing and their previously used name is restored on the canvas.

testAreas.howToReach: Exact navigation steps were not supplied; open the Excalidraw app, start a live collaboration session to create a collaboration link, then open that link in a second browser window.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor and live collaborator
testAreas.setup: Two browser windows (or two devices) with a drawing containing several elements, and a freshly created collaboration link.
checks: Verify that drawing, moving, and deleting elements in one window appears in the other window within a few seconds.

Verify that selecting one or more elements (including right after joining the room) highlights the same elements for the other participant, and that with nothing selected both windows still show live pointers without errors.
Verify that after making edits, leaving the page saves them and reloading the collaboration link restores the latest drawing, including for a participant joining the same link later.

testAreas.howToReach: Exact navigation steps were not supplied; render the package's Excalidraw component in a host page or the existing integration example.
testAreas.access: Integrating developer
testAreas.setup: A minimal host application that renders the Excalidraw component from the package.
checks: Verify the embedded editor renders and basic drawing works when only default properties are supplied (no collaboration properties passed).
Verify the editor's imperative API reference is delivered to the host through the new dedicated property once the editor mounts, and that a reference attached in the standard way also arrives.

Verify the host receives live pointer updates as the pointer moves in the embedded editor, and that the handler supplied for the collaboration button is invoked when a collaboration session is started from the embedded editor.

Verify that an integration still passing the old properties (the old API-forwarding property and the username-change callback) no longer receives the editor API or username updates, confirming the migration to the new properties.

testAreas.howToReach: Exact navigation steps were not supplied; open the Excalidraw app's main drawing page.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor
testAreas.setup: A blank drawing.
checks: Verify basic drawing, selecting, moving, resizing, and undo still work on the main page after the reorganization.
Verify the collaboration dialog still opens from the editor and shows the session link with a working copy action during an active session.

testAreas.area: Live collaboration sync between two users
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; this is the live collaboration feature of the Excalidraw web editor, reached through the editor's share/collaboration entry point and a shared room link.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor and Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: Two browsers (or one browser plus a touch device), a drawing with several shapes, and the room link shared from the first user's collaboration dialog.
checks: Verify that the second user, opening the shared room link, sees the first user's current drawing immediately without the first user redrawing anything.
Check that a shape drawn, moved, and then deleted by one user appears as drawn, moved, and deleted on the other user's canvas, with no element later reverting or appearing twice.

Test that when one user undoes their most recently drawn shape, that shape also disappears on the other user's canvas; broadcasting is gated on the scene version increasing, so an undo is the input most likely to be skipped.

Verify cursor presence: with a single mouse or pen pointer the other user sees your cursor move, and after a two-finger pinch-zoom gesture pointer sharing resumes normally with no stuck or ghost cursor.

testAreas.area: Session start, stop, and deleted-content privacy
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; these are the start-session and stop-session controls inside the collaboration dialog of the Excalidraw web editor.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor (session owner)
testAreas.setup: A drawing with several shapes, at least one of which is deleted before the session starts, plus a second browser to join the room link.
checks: Ensure that after deleting some shapes and then starting a session, a user joining the room link never sees the deleted shapes, even after refreshing their page.

Confirm that starting a session replaces the page address with a shareable room link while the visible drawing stays unchanged, and that undo or redo afterwards does not resurrect pre-session deletions.
Confirm that stopping the session restores the plain app address without the room link and that refreshing afterwards does not rejoin the room or show other collaborators.
Check that pressing start again while already in a session does not open a second connection or duplicate your own presence.

testAreas.area: Room dialog, link copying, and user name

testAreas.setup: An active collaboration session so the dialog shows the link field, copy control, and name field.
checks: Verify the copy control puts the full room link on the clipboard so pasting it in a new browser opens the same shared drawing, and that if copying is blocked an error dialog appears and the link field text becomes selected.
Check that clicking or tapping the link field selects the entire link text in one action.
Confirm a name typed into the name field is remembered after closing and reopening the dialog and after a page reload, and that pressing Enter in the field closes the dialog.
Ensure that after closing the dialog, keyboard focus returns to the collaboration button so keyboard users are not stranded.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not found in the supplied context; open a saved room link directly in the Excalidraw web editor.
testAreas.access: Live collaborator
testAreas.setup: An active session with drawing content and a browser network-throttling tool.
checks: Verify that refreshing the page during a session reconnects using the room link in the address bar and the shared drawing reloads with all collaborators' content.

Check that with a heavily throttled network, a joiner whose initial scene message is delayed still ends up seeing the room's drawing through the fallback instead of an empty canvas or endless loading.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Verify that when a collaborator is still on the previous release and moves their mouse over the canvas, their named cursor appears on your screen, whereas before this release cursors sent by that older version were not displayed.
Verify that pressing the Enter key while typing your name in the name field closes the dialog, and that typing into the room link field does not change the link because it is read-only.

Confirm that while you are holding the pointer down dragging or resizing a shape and a collaborator's update to that same shape arrives, the incoming copy is skipped so your drag is not snapped out of your hand — the decision now reads the live interaction snapshot that updates on every pointer move instead of the last rendered screen state, which could lag a moment behind.
Verify that when the browser refuses to copy the room link, an error popup appears describing the problem instead of nothing happening as before.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Verify that when you open the collaboration dialog with the keyboard, focus moves into the dialog onto its controls so tabbing continues from there rather than staying behind on the toolbar.

Confirm that while you are in a shared room with changes not yet saved to the cloud, closing or reloading the tab makes the browser ask for confirmation and, if you choose to stay, the drawing is uploaded to the cloud at once — before this release the tab simply closed and nothing was saved.
Verify that when you open a room link, the canvas scrolls so the shared drawing is centered on your screen instead of leaving you in a blank area with the drawing off-screen as before.

Verify that after you press start session, pressing Ctrl+Z does not bring back anything you drew or deleted beforehand, since the undo history is now wiped when the room is created; confirm that wiping is intended.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Verify that if you draw something during a live session and close the tab right away, a person opening that room link afterwards still sees the drawing, since the last-second change used to be lost.

Confirm that opening a shared-room link in a fresh browser tab and then immediately reloading that tab — without drawing anything — now brings up the browser's leave-confirmation prompt, where before this release the tab reloaded silently.

Confirm that when a participant closes their tab their cursor and name disappear from your canvas immediately, and if that same person rejoins they appear as a plain cursor with no name until they move, instead of keeping stale details from their earlier visit — before this release stale participant details could persist.

Confirm that the automatic whole-drawing re-send happens on a long interval rather than on every stroke, and that a small edit made immediately after it still reaches the other participants — before this release the change counter was advanced during every send, so confirm the new arrangement does not swallow the next edit.

testAreas.howToReach: Use the screen or action named in each check.
testAreas.access: Same access as the rest of this report.
testAreas.setup: Use the exact input named in each check.
checks: Verify that when two people edit the drawing at the same time, for example each dragging the same rectangle, both screens settle on one final result instead of the shape flickering back and forth as each side echoed the other's change.

Confirm that when you open the collaboration dialog the name you saved in an earlier session is already filled in, and on a device where no name was ever saved the field starts empty rather than erroring or showing leftover text — before this release the saved name was not reliably restored on load.

Confirm that after two people have edited a shared room, reopening the same room link later in a fresh browser shows the latest combined drawing rather than an older copy — before this release the cloud copy could lag behind what was on screen.

moreChecks: Confirm that when you close the collaboration dialog to stop sharing, all other participants' cursors and names vanish from your canvas at once and reopening the dialog shows no active room link, whereas before this release the old link and stray cursors could remain.

Verify that in Firefox on a plain non-secure address, clicking the copy button next to the room link still copies the link and selects it in the field, whereas before this release copying failed on that setup.

Verify that on a touch screen during a live session, pinch-zooming the canvas with two fingers no longer makes your cursor jump around on the other participant's screen, whereas before this release cursor positions were sent throughout the gesture.

Confirm that on a page embedding the drawing canvas without any collaboration settings, clicking the Live collaboration button now does nothing, whereas before this release it started a live session inside the component itself - verify that this silent no-op is intended.

Check that in a live collaboration session every element you draw still appears on the other participants' canvases exactly as before, since the helpers that prepare elements for sharing are now loaded through the drawing component's main package entry point, which also newly re-exports them to embedding apps that previously could not get them from there - confirm nothing about syncing changed.

Verify that clicking once anywhere in the room link field selects the entire link so you can copy it immediately, while a second click places the cursor normally, whereas before this release the first click merely placed the cursor where you clicked.

Check that when you press the stop-session button after drawing, the drawing as it looked at that moment is saved with the room and still appears if the same room link is opened afterwards, whereas before this release the final state was not saved on stop.

Confirm that when a second person opens your shared-room link they receive the complete current drawing including shapes drawn before they joined, and that your own next edit afterwards is still sent to the room exactly once — before this release that welcome send also advanced the internal change counter, which it no longer does.

Verify that after you close the collaboration dialog, keyboard focus lands on the collaboration button in the toolbar rather than being lost, since before this release focus was left behind when the dialog closed.

Verify that clicking the collaboration button while a session is already running opens the dialog showing the share link and the stop-session option without ending or restarting the session, and confirm that opening it a second time is intended.

report.summary: This release makes the drawing editor account for where its canvas sits on the page, so opening views, pointers, text, and remote cursors now line up correctly whenever the editor is not at the page's top-left.
keyChanges: Both coordinate conversions between the screen pointer and the drawing now subtract the canvas's left and top page offset, so every pointer-driven interaction (drawing, selecting, dragging, resizing, pasting at the cursor, placing the context menu) resolves to a different scene position once the offset is non-zero; with a zero offset all results are identical to before.

The text editing box that appears while typing on the canvas now receives the full app state and includes the offset in both its position and its zoom transform: at 100% zoom nothing changes, while at other zoom levels on an offset canvas the box should stay exactly over the drawn text instead of drifting by the offset.

Adding text centered inside a shape via double-click or a text-tool click uses the offset-aware conversion for its snap position, and remote collaborator cursors are drawn through the same conversion, so both shift correctly on offset canvases.
Internal-only edits in this group (type-only imports and a new private reference field) have no observable behavior; the offset handling above is the only QA-visible change.

Opening a drawing now centers the view on its content: reloading the editor with a saved drawing or opening a shareable link recalculates the scroll position from the drawing's bounds instead of restoring the stored scroll position, so content far from the canvas origin now opens visible rather than possibly off-screen; the previous scroll-to-content option was removed from the internal restore step and centering now happens in the load flow itself.

Dropping a saved .excalidraw file onto the canvas now opens the drawing centered in the current view, and the editor keeps the current window size and canvas position whenever loaded state is applied, so a file saved on a differently sized screen no longer resizes the canvas.

The editor now measures its own top-left position on the page at startup, on embedded width/height changes, and after every state update, and positions the canvas accordingly; in the standalone editor the measured offsets are effectively zero so layout should look unchanged, while in an embedded page with margins drawing should now land exactly under the cursor, and the default state no longer supplies these offsets itself.

Opening a drawing via the load button or dropping a .json/.excalidraw file onto the canvas now computes the view scroll from the loaded elements and the current editor window, so the imported drawing should appear centered in view instead of using the previous generic scroll-to-content behavior.

Loading a scene from a shared or backend link no longer auto-scrolls to the drawing; the view now uses the scroll position saved inside that scene, which means a shared scene saved with an off-screen scroll position may load showing empty canvas until the user pans.

The underlying file-reading and validation logic was restructured but the rules are unchanged: files without the excalidraw format still show the same invalid-file error, so invalid-file handling is not expected to behave differently.

The editor's shared state now carries two numeric values recording the drawing canvas's top and left position, and both are configured to be stripped when state is stored in the browser or written into an exported drawing file, so saved data keeps its previous shape and drawings saved by older versions remain loadable.

The Node-based image export utility previously passed only the default state, which no longer contains the two position values, so it now explicitly supplies zero for each to keep the rendered sample image unshifted and identically framed.
