Verify changing the embedded width and height settings keeps the canvas aligned and pointer drawing accurate afterwards.
Verify the canvas settles into the correct position after the first load with no visible jump or misalignment.
Verify that after Undo, Redo, and Clear canvas, the canvas keeps its current size and position, and in the embedded editor keeps the embedded size instead of resizing to the full window.

Verify opening a shared link whose saved scroll position places the drawing far from the origin still shows the drawing on the canvas, or at minimum that the user can pan to reach it and the canvas is never left permanently blank.
Verify opening a valid shared link loads the saved elements and settings (background color, name) exactly as saved, since the view now follows the scene's stored scroll instead of auto-centering.

Verify opening the saved file centers the view on the imported drawing even when the current canvas was scrolled far away, and that the drawing's saved settings still apply apart from the view position.
Verify opening a file saved with an off-screen scroll position still shows the drawing in view, because the computed center should override the file's stored scroll.
Verify dropping the valid file onto the canvas loads its elements and the view is centered on the dropped drawing rather than staying wherever the canvas was.
Verify dropping the non-Excalidraw file still shows the invalid-file error message and leaves the editor usable, with no loading state stuck on screen.
Verify a drawing saved with a previous version still opens with every element at its original position and nothing shifts while panning, zooming, or editing.

Ensure that saving a new drawing, reloading the page, and reopening it reproduces the same drawing at the same scroll position, because the new position values must not be kept in or restored from browser storage.
Confirm that saving a drawing to a file and reopening that file reproduces the exact layout and canvas position shown before the save.
Verify the generated PNG shows all three sample elements fully inside the image on a white background, with none clipped, missing, or shifted toward a corner compared to earlier output.

Check that dropping a saved drawing file onto the canvas places the view centered on the drawing for your current window, which used to scroll to the content instead, and confirm the new centering is intended.

Confirm that opening a drawing through a shared link now shows the shapes centered on screen even if the drawing was saved while scrolled away from them, because the view is recalculated when the drawing opens, whereas before this release the saved scroll position was used as-is and could show blank space.

Verify that on a page where the drawing area does not start at the very top-left of the window, for example with a banner above it or the page scrolled down, shapes appear exactly where you click and draw rather than shifted down or to the right, because the drawing area's position within the page is now measured directly.

Verify that when the app opens the drawing area still fills the whole window exactly as before, with no new gap, overlap or shift at the top or left edge, now that its size and position are set on the drawing frame itself at display time.

Check that when the drawing canvas sits inset from the window edge, for example below a header on a test page, and zoom is set to 200 percent, clicking and dragging to draw a rectangle keeps the growing shape exactly under the pointer, where before this release the shape appeared below and to the right of where you clicked.

Verify that in a live shared session, with the drawing canvas inset from the window edge so it is not at the top-left corner, the collaborator cursor dot on your screen lands exactly on the shape the other person is pointing at, where before this release it appeared shifted up and to the left by the size of the surrounding header and margin.

Confirm that with the drawing canvas inset from the window edge and zoom set to 200 percent, double-clicking an existing text element opens the typing box directly on top of that text, where before this release the box was pulled up and to the left toward the page corner so the text you were editing sat outside it.

Verify that double-clicking an existing text element while the drawing canvas is inset below a header and zoomed to 200 percent reopens the typing box exactly over that text, where before this release the box opened shifted away from the text by the page offset so it looked like a different spot was being edited.

Confirm that exporting a drawing to PNG through the server-side script still produces a correctly positioned image (no shifted, misplaced or blank content), now that the export explicitly starts from zero offsets.

Check that after the browser window has been resized since the last visit, reopening the app shows the drawing area at the current window size rather than the size remembered from the earlier session, because size and position are now kept from the live window whenever a saved drawing is applied.

Verify that opening a shared scene link whose saved view was scrolled away from the drawing now opens at that saved position instead of jumping to center the drawing, which is what happened before this release, and confirm that is intended.

Check that opening a shared drawing link on a page where the drawing area sits below a banner or header opens the drawing centered within the visible drawing area, because the drawing now finishes loading only after its position has been measured, whereas before this release the view could come out shifted by the header's height.

Confirm that a drawing saved while the view was scrolled away from the shapes still ends up centered on the shapes once fully loaded, because the automatic centering now happens later in the opening sequence rather than during the loading step, and nothing should open on a blank area.

Verify that when the drawing canvas is inset below a page header, selecting the text tool and clicking on an empty spot puts the typing box right where you clicked so the text appears under the pointer as you type, where before this release the typed text showed up above and to the left of the click point by the height of the header.

Confirm that with the drawing canvas inset below a page header, clicking the text tool right at the center of a rectangle snaps the typing box to the exact middle of that rectangle on screen, where before this release the box snapped to a point above and to the left of the middle, off the shape's center.
uncertainty: No affected page, screen, or navigation in the supplied context produces a non-zero canvas offset, so the visible differences may only reproduce in an embedded editor or a page with content above the canvas; if the shipped canvas always sits at zero offset this group's behavior change is invisible there, and the remaining review groups complete the same offset change.

The canvas position is re-measured only at startup and when the embedded width and height settings change; if the host page scrolls or the container moves without a size change, alignment and pointer accuracy may go stale, so confirm this case in the embedded scenario before release.

Shared-link scenes previously auto-scrolled to the drawing on import and now keep the scene's saved scroll position; if a shared scene was saved with content outside the visible viewport, the link could open on an apparently blank canvas, which is the most likely user-visible regression to confirm or rule out.

No application areas or navigation were supplied for these changes, so testing guidance relies on the described capabilities only, and how a restored session obtains the new position values is handled elsewhere in this release and was not established by this group's evidence.

report.summary: The release adds arrows that attach to and follow shapes while rebuilding how clicks select items, so basic selection and arrow-to-shape connections are the main areas to retest in the drawing editor.
keyChanges: Arrows can now attach to shapes (rectangles, diamonds, ellipses, and now also text elements): while drawing or dragging an arrow endpoint near a shape it is highlighted as a binding target, and once attached the endpoint follows the shape as it moves or is resized.
Only arrows bind - plain lines and freehand strokes do not - and detaching one end of an arrow that touches the same shape at both ends leaves the other end attached.

Click, hover, and right-click detection on the canvas was rebuilt on new geometry math that respects element rotation, so picking should now match the visually rotated shape instead of its straight bounding box.

Moving or resizing a shape updates the arrows attached to it, including adjusting the attachment gap when the shape is scaled and avoiding double movement when a shape and its arrow are moved together in one selection.
Bindings are maintained across common scene operations: deleting, duplicating, and pasting elements repairs or carries over arrow attachments.

Click detection now measures the exact distance to each shape with an about 10-pixel tolerance at the current zoom: clicks about 5 pixels outside a text label's bounds and in the thin band alongside a filled shape's edges now register, which previously did not.

Arrow-to-shape binding now uses a rebuilt border test whose connection zone scales with the shape between a 15-pixel minimum and an 80-pixel maximum (diamonds measured against their drawn edges), and the canvas now draws faint gray binding hints, a halo around a bindable shape and circles at arrow tips, while arrows are drawn with binding enabled.

Selection borders and resize/rotation handles were extracted into shared drawing routines; the rotation handle is now a solid filled circle and the point handles on line and arrow vertices are filled circles centered exactly on each point.
Exported images and copy-to-clipboard PNG/SVG render through the reworked scene renderer and should look unchanged, because selection and handle rendering is disabled during export.
Element picking now receives its hit test as a callback instead of raw coordinates; picking still returns the frontmost element at a point, so overlapping-shape selection order should be unchanged.

Twenty-seven new math routines for points, lines, directions, and transforms (vector arithmetic including scalar forms, geometric products, norms and normalization, line intersections and distances, rotation, translation, and transform composition) were introduced as the foundation for the editor's geometry calculations, with a dedicated unit test suite covering them.

Pointer hit-testing against rectangles, ellipses, diamonds, and lines/arrows is now computed through this library, so element selection, hover targeting, double-click handling, and right-click context-menu targeting all depend on its numerical results.

Arrow-to-shape binding is also computed through it: which shapes are eligible under the cursor, the binding suggestion shown at the cursor, attachment focus points and gaps, and endpoint updates when shapes change.
Dragging, resizing, and rotating elements push connected-arrow endpoint updates through these calculations, and completing a newly drawn element at pointer release flows through them as well.

New arrow binding: while the arrow (or line) tool is active, hovering over a shape highlights it as a bindable target, and finishing a multi-point arrow now connects it to the hovered shape; holding Ctrl/Cmd while finishing intentionally skips binding, and releasing the keys or the window losing focus re-enables binding.
Finishing a line/arrow by switching tools mid-draw now also completes the binding, a new code path in the editor update cycle.
Pasting or dropping elements (including dragging from the Library) that contain an arrow connected to a shape now repairs the connection on the copies instead of leaving it dangling.
Submitting empty text (which deletes the text element) now cleans up arrows that were bound to that text, so they no longer point at a deleted element.

Click detection for double-click, right-click context menu, hover cursor, and text-at-position was switched to a new hit-testing routine, and the underlying segment/curve intersection math was renamed and adjusted, so element selection under the pointer may resolve slightly differently for overlapping elements.

All arrow and line connection behavior, including highlighting candidate shapes while drawing or dragging an endpoint, attaching ends on release, re-anchoring arrows when a connected shape moves or is resized, and detaching ends, was moved into a new dedicated module; no behavior change is intended, but the whole connection workflow now runs through relocated code and needs regression coverage.
The moved code preserves the rule that a straight arrow with only two points cannot bind both of its ends to the same shape, while a line with three or more points can bind both ends to one shape.

When an arrow end is detached, the shape's list of attached arrows is cleaned up through a new scene lookup that skips already-deleted elements, so deleted shapes no longer interfere with unbind cleanup.

Resizing a connected shape recalculates each attached arrow's gap so it stays at least 1 and never exceeds the shape's binding border, and releasing a moved shape over a loose arrow end can attach that end.

A diamond's left-corner coordinate is now taken as 0 directly instead of via the top coordinate, which is also 0, so diamond rendering on canvas, in PNG/SVG exports, and in library previews should be visually unchanged.
Arrows and lines now stay attached to shapes: moving, resizing (single or multi-select), and rotating a shape updates the endpoints of arrows connected to it, which previously stayed behind.

Finishing a drawn arrow or line on a shape now connects it there, starting one on a shape records that connection, and eligible shapes near the cursor show a connection highlight while drawing or dragging that clears on release.

Deletion now cleans up connections: deleting or cutting a shape detaches arrows that pointed to it, undo/redo keeps those connections consistent, and deleting an arrow's first or last point in point-editing mode clears that end's connection.

Duplication preserves connections across the Duplicate action, copy-paste, drag-and-drop or library paste, and Alt-drag, where roles are intentionally reversed so each copy attaches to its own shapes.

In arrow/line point-editing mode, dragging an endpoint suggests a shape binding that is applied on the next click off a point, Alt-click remembers the hovered shape for the new point, and releasing Alt now fully clears the uncommitted preview point; scrollbar dragging was only reorganized with unchanged behavior.

Drawing an arrow or line that ends on or very near a shape now attaches it when the arrow is finished: this applies to simple arrows and to multi-point arrows with more than one point that do not close into a loop, so dragging the shape afterwards moves the arrow's endpoint, while a line closed back onto itself stays unattached.
Duplicating a selection that contains a shape and its attached arrow now rewires the duplicate so the duplicated arrow points at the duplicated shape instead of the original.
Undo and redo now repair attachments when a history step removes or restores bound shapes, so arrows no longer keep dangling references to shapes that are absent at that step.

Saved and imported drawings now preserve arrow attachment data on arrows and a per-shape list of attached arrows (previously dropped when loading); new arrows are created with empty attachment fields, and the new binding-related editor state is stripped from browser saves and exported files.

The math deciding which drawing element is under the pointer was rewritten on a new geometric engine; clicking shapes, the border tolerance of roughly 10 screen pixels at the current zoom, and the rule that filled shapes can be grabbed from inside while transparent shapes are only grabbed at their border must behave exactly as before.

Where an arrow tip attaches to a rectangle, diamond, text item, or ellipse is now computed by the new engine; arrows must still snap when drawn near a shape (snap zone between 15 and 80 pixels depending on shape size, tighter for diamonds) and must follow shapes when they are dragged or resized.

The new code adds explicit handling of degenerate positions: an adjacent arrow point exactly level with an ellipse's center is nudged by 0.0001 to keep the calculation valid, and a binding line that is tangent to a shape or catches only one corner returns no intersection, making the arrow tip fall back to a point inside the shape instead of its offset boundary position.

Diamond geometry is now built from its four corner tips with small circular offsets at each corner, replacing the previous diamond-point math, so diamond hit-testing and arrow attachment should still align with rectangles of the same size.
qaChecks: Verify that an arrow drawn from a rectangle to an ellipse attaches at both ends, and that dragging the ellipse afterward carries the arrow's attached end with it.
Verify that dragging an arrow endpoint away from its shape detaches it, and that moving the endpoint from one shape to another releases the first shape and attaches to the second.
Check that an arrow with both ends attached to the same shape keeps its remaining attachment after one end is dragged away.
Confirm that resizing a shape with an attached arrow (drag a corner handle larger and smaller) keeps the arrow attached with a sensible gap rather than detaching or cutting through the shape.
Verify that while dragging an arrow endpoint near a shape, that shape is highlighted as a binding target and the highlight disappears when the pointer moves away.
Check that when an arrow's start end is already attached to a shape, hovering the free end over that same shape shows no suggestion highlight, while hovering a different shape does.
Confirm that while creating a multi-point arrow by clicking to place each point, hovering over a shape highlights it as a binding target.
Verify that a plain line ending on a rectangle does not attach to it, while an arrow drawn the same way does.
Confirm that an arrow can attach to a text element and keeps following it when the text is moved or resized, for example by changing its font size through the resize handles.

Verify that clicking a point inside a 45-degree-rotated rectangle but outside its straight bounding box selects it, and that clicking the opposite bounding-box corner that lies outside the rotated shape does not select it.
Check that clicking directly on a diamond's slanted edge and on an ellipse's curved edge selects them where they visually appear.

Confirm that right-clicking an element opens the element menu with options like Copy, Paste, Copy as PNG, and Copy as SVG, while right-clicking empty canvas shows the canvas menu including Paste and Toggle grid mode.
Test resizing a straight line, an arrow, and a freehand stroke by dragging a handle past the opposite side: each shape should mirror correctly and keep positive dimensions.
Verify that deleting a shape an arrow is attached to leaves the arrow on the canvas without errors, and that undoing the delete restores the drawing with the arrow attached again.
Confirm that duplicating (or copy-pasting) a shape together with its attached arrow produces a second pair attached to each other while the originals remain attached to each other.
Check clicking each shape type and a text label selects it, clicking one of two overlapping shapes selects the frontmost one, and double-clicking a text label still opens it for editing.
Test clicking about 5 pixels just outside a text label's bounding box: the text should now be selected, where previously the click did nothing.

Test clicking about 8 pixels to the right of a filled rectangle's right edge but well below its bottom-right corner: the shape should now be selected, where previously only clicks within 10 pixels of its bounding box registered.
Check clicking the center of an unfilled rectangle: the result should match the previous build, which required clicking near its border.

Verify while drawing an arrow and hovering within a shape's connection zone, a faint gray halo appears around that shape and a gray circle appears at the arrow's tip, and releasing the pointer attaches the arrow end to the shape.
Test the connection-zone size: a small shape should start hinting about 15 pixels out from its edge and a very large shape at most about 80 pixels.
Check hovering near a diamond and an ellipse while drawing an arrow: their gray highlights should follow the diamond outline and the ellipse curve rather than the rectangular bounding box.
Verify after binding, moving and resizing the bound shape keeps the arrow attached with the endpoint following smoothly, for rectangles, diamonds, and ellipses.
Verify each vertex handle is drawn as a small filled circle sitting exactly on the point and that clicking and dragging a point still moves it.
Check the active point being edited is still visually distinguished from the other points.
Verify a single selected element shows its dashed border, the resize handles, and a rotation handle drawn as a solid filled circle centered above the element.
Verify multiple selected elements show a combined dashed border with corner handles and no rotation handle when not rotating, and that resizing and rotating still work.
Verify an image produced by the export dialog matches the on-canvas drawing with no selection borders, resize handles, or gray binding hints included.
Test copy to clipboard as PNG and as SVG and paste into another application: the pasted image should match the drawing.
Verify clicking each shape type (rectangle, ellipse, diamond, line/arrow, text) selects exactly that element, including on rotated shapes and near their edges.
Check that hovering and right-clicking where two shapes overlap targets the topmost element under the cursor and the context menu acts on that element.
Confirm double-clicking a text element opens it for editing instead of selecting a shape behind it.
Test clicking exactly on a rotated shape's border and just outside it; selection should switch cleanly at the boundary without errors or mis-selection.
Verify drawing an arrow that starts or ends on or near a shape attaches to it, and that a binding suggestion appears at the cursor while hovering bindable shapes.
Confirm dragging a bound shape keeps the arrow's endpoint attached with a consistent gap.
Test binding an arrow to a rotated shape and then resizing it; the arrow endpoint should follow the shape without detaching.
Check that dragging a line/arrow endpoint in line-editing mode and dropping it onto another shape re-binds the arrow to that shape.
Verify dragging a group selection containing a bound shape and its arrow keeps the arrow attached at the same relative position.
Confirm resizing a single shape and then resizing a multi-element selection updates connected arrow endpoints correctly.
Confirm finishing a newly drawn shape or line at pointer release commits the element and it can immediately be selected at its final position.

Verify that with the arrow tool selected, hovering near a shape highlights it as a binding target and that finishing the arrow on the shape connects the arrow to it (dragging the shape afterwards moves the arrow endpoint with it).
Test finishing an arrow while holding Ctrl (or Cmd) directly on a shape: the arrow should not bind, and after releasing the key the next arrow drawn onto a shape should bind again.

Test drawing a multi-point arrow and, without releasing to finish, switching to a different tool (for example the selection tool): the arrow should be finalized and bind to the shape under its last point.

Test clicking shapes with the line and freehand draw tools as well: binding suggestions should appear for arrow-like tools and the highlight should disappear when a non-linear tool (such as rectangle or selection) is selected.
Verify that pasting a bound arrow plus its shapes produces a copy where the arrow is still connected to the copied shapes, and moving a copied shape keeps the copied arrow attached.
Verify dragging a Library item containing a bound arrow and shape onto the canvas places the elements with the connection intact.
Verify that submitting an empty text editor (which deletes the text) removes the text and that any arrow bound to it is cleaned up rather than left pointing at a deleted element.
Verify that editing existing text still preserves normal behavior: submitting non-empty text keeps the element selected and undo history records the change.
Verify double-clicking a line or arrow enters point-editing mode and double-clicking text opens the text editor, including when elements overlap.
Verify right-clicking on an element opens the element context menu (with Copy, Paste, Copy As PNG, Copy As SVG) and right-clicking empty canvas opens the canvas-only menu including Toggle Grid Mode.
Verify clicking inside a freehand drawn curve still selects it, and the pointer cursor over text still shows the text cursor.

Verify that while editing an arrow's points and dragging the final uncommitted point toward a shape, the shape is highlighted as a binding suggestion, and the highlight clears when the cursor moves away.
Verify dragging arrow points still moves the correct point and the editing session can be exited without leaving stray state on the canvas.

Verify that drawing an arrow from inside one shape to the other attaches its start to the first shape and its end to the second on release, and that both connections survive small moves of each shape.

Verify that while an arrow is being drawn and the cursor nears a bindable shape (rectangle, ellipse, diamond, or text), that shape highlights as a connection suggestion and releasing there attaches the arrow end.

Verify that a straight arrow with only two points whose start is already attached to a shape cannot attach its other end to the same shape, while a line with three or more points can have both ends on one shape.
Verify that dragging a connected shape keeps its arrows attached with endpoints following the shape's edge.
Verify that resizing a connected shape keeps arrows attached with a small visible gap at each connection that never drops below 1 and never pulls an endpoint inside the shape.

Verify that moving a shape and its attached arrow together as one selection moves them as a unit without the arrow jumping or detaching, and that releasing a moved shape over a loose arrow end attaches that end.
Verify that dragging an arrow's endpoint off its shape detaches that end and that moving the shape afterwards no longer moves the arrow.
Verify that dragging the detached endpoint onto another shape re-attaches it there.
Verify that deleting a bound shape leaves its arrows on the canvas with their last endpoints and without errors.
Verify that while dragging a multi-element selection, elements inside the selection are never offered as connection suggestions.
Verify that after the drag all previously existing connections are intact and no unintended new bindings were created.
Verify that a diamond renders correctly on the canvas and looks identical in the exported PNG and SVG images and in a copy-to-clipboard image.
Verify that a diamond saved as a library item shows a correct preview in the library.
Verify dragging a rectangle moves the attached arrow's endpoint along with it so the arrow stays connected for the whole drag; before this change the arrow stayed behind.

Verify resizing a rectangle from a corner handle and from a side handle keeps the attached arrow's endpoint on the shape's edge, and that selecting both rectangles and resizing them together keeps both arrows attached.
Verify rotating a rectangle keeps the attached arrow's endpoint following the rotated edge.
Confirm clicking a shape still selects it and shows its resize handles, since the pointer-down hit-testing was reorganized.

Verify drawing an arrow by pressing on empty space and releasing on top of a rectangle attaches the arrow's end to it, so moving the rectangle afterwards drags the arrow's end (previously the arrow never attached).
Verify starting an arrow directly on a rectangle and releasing on another rectangle connects both ends, so moving either rectangle moves its matching arrow end.
Verify that while dragging a new arrow the hovered eligible shape shows a connection highlight, and the highlight disappears immediately on release.
Test dragging an existing selected arrow so its end lands on a shape, which should attach on release, then dragging the end away, which should detach on release.
Verify deleting or cutting a shape with an attached arrow leaves the arrow in place but detached, and after undo the arrow is connected to the restored shape again and follows it.

Verify duplicating a connected shape-and-arrow set via Duplicate, copy-paste, and drag-and-drop or library paste yields a copy whose arrows attach to the copied shapes while the originals stay attached to the originals.
Verify Alt-drag duplication of a connected set keeps both the dragged copy and the original set correctly attached after release.
Verify clearing all text from an attached text label and submitting removes the label and detaches its arrow without errors.

Verify dragging the arrow's start or end point near a shape shows a connection highlight, and after releasing, a single click on empty canvas applies the binding so the shape then drags that arrow end.

Verify deleting the first point clears the start connection and deleting the last point clears the end connection (confirmed after a click on empty canvas), while deleting the final remaining point removes the whole arrow.

Verify Alt-click adds an uncommitted preview point that follows the cursor, releasing Alt removes it and clears the preview completely, and pressing Alt again produces a fresh preview point; previously a stale preview could linger after releasing Alt.
Verify dragging a start or end point so the arrow forms a closed loop still snaps the loop closed on release.

Verify pressing and dragging the horizontal scrollbar pans the canvas horizontally and the vertical scrollbar pans vertically, with the normal cursor restored on release; this logic was only reorganized, so any difference from before is a regression.
Verify that drawing an arrow whose last point lands on or very near a shape and then finishing it attaches the arrow: dragging the shape afterwards moves the arrow's endpoint with it.

Test a multi-point arrow (several clicks, more than one point) finished near a shape — its end should attach; then draw a line closed back into a loop and confirm it stays unattached when nearby shapes move.

Confirm double-clicking an existing arrow to edit its points and finishing the edit keeps its shape attachments, and that the small round point handles still appear at the arrow's points while editing.

Verify selecting a shape plus its attached arrow and duplicating the selection produces a duplicate arrow attached to the duplicate shape: moving the duplicate shape moves only the duplicate arrow, and the originals keep their own attachment.

Verify undoing and redoing the deletion of a shape that an arrow is attached to: at every step the arrow stays visible and draggable and does not point at a missing shape, and after undoing the deletion the arrow attaches to the restored shape again.
Check multi-step undo and redo on a mixed drawing (shapes, arrows, text) still restores earlier positions and selection as before.
Verify saving a drawing with an arrow attached to a shape and reloading it (via file open and browser restore) keeps the attachment: dragging the shape still moves the arrow's endpoint.
Test opening an older saved drawing file whose arrows carry no attachment data — it should load without errors and those arrows remain editable and draggable.
Ensure a fresh editor session initializes cleanly with default state and the clear canvas action empties the drawing without errors.

Verify dragging each bound shape around the canvas keeps every arrow attached, with tips landing on the shape boundary at the small binding offset, not at the shape center and not floating in empty space, including the rotated rectangle.

Test the horizontal ellipse case: with an arrow bound from a point exactly level with the ellipse center, drag the ellipse up and down and confirm the tip stays on the boundary and never detaches, jumps, or lands at the center.

Verify drawing a new arrow that ends within the snap zone of a rectangle, diamond, and ellipse binds it to the shape, and ending just outside the zone leaves it unbound; the diamond's zone should feel slightly tighter than a same-sized rectangle's.
Confirm the snap zone grows with shape size up to about 80 pixels and never shrinks below about 15 pixels for a small shape.

Verify clicking the middle of each filled shape (rectangle, diamond, ellipse, text) selects it, while clicking the middle of a transparent, unfilled shape does not select it unless the click lands on its border.
Verify clicking just outside a shape's border, within roughly 10 screen pixels at the current zoom, still selects it, and repeat zoomed in to confirm the tolerance scales with zoom.
Verify clicking on empty canvas never selects or drags a nearby element, including transparent lines and arrows.
Verify resizing a bound shape keeps its arrows attached to the new boundary after both enlarging and shrinking it.
Verify multi-selecting a shape together with its bound arrow and resizing the selection keeps the arrow attached with its tip on the resized shape.
Ensure shrinking a bound shape to a very small size never detaches the arrow; the tip may sit slightly inside the boundary as a fallback but must remain visually connected.

Confirm the pretend-infinity basis element used when building transforms is exactly the same value as the triple-product basis element, since before this release neither existed and every transform depends on them matching.

Confirm that when one element is selected by you and by a collaborator at once, the dashed border still shows two staggered colour patterns and the rest of the drawing is not shifted or left with a stray dash pattern afterwards.

Verify that hovering an arrow endpoint near a diamond shows a faint band shaped like the diamond and near an ellipse shows a band shaped like the ellipse, each following the shape's own outline, where before this release no highlight appeared.
Confirm that multiplying a value by the plain number 2 doubles every part of it, including its hidden weight part, unlike adding a plain number which touches only the weight.

Verify that dragging a corner handle to enlarge a rectangle that has an arrow attached keeps the arrow endpoint glued to the growing edge the whole time, where before this release the arrow stayed put while the rectangle grew, and confirm the endpoint following the resize is intended.

Check that hovering an arrow endpoint just outside the far left tip of a very wide, flat ellipse gives a steady binding zone at the tip, since the closest point on the curve is now found by a clamped search instead of the looser inline iteration used before.

Check that clicking with the selection tool on the middle of a long straight line, far from either endpoint, still selects the line, since the helper that measured the pointer's distance from the middle of a segment was removed in this release.

Confirm that with a single element selected the rotation handle above it is now a solid filled circle instead of the outlined ellipse drawn before, and that the corner handles around a multi-selection still look like outlined squares.

Verify that clicking just beyond a closed filled loop's box corner but within the ten-pixel margin selects the loop, while clicking inside a thin unfilled zigzag's box but far from every stroke still selects nothing, and confirm both outcomes are intended.
Verify that drawing an arrow so it starts on one rectangle and ends on another now leaves it attached so both ends follow the shapes when you drag them around, which the previous release never did.

Confirm that after you connect an arrow to a very wide, flat ellipse from steeply above and then drag the ellipse around, the arrow stays attached at a point on the upper part of the ellipse instead of sliding to a corner, because before this release arrows never attached to shapes at all.

Verify that while adding extra points to a line or arrow you are drawing, with the newest point not yet committed, moving the pointer near a rectangle now highlights that rectangle as a snapping target, which the previous release never showed.

Check that while dragging a new arrow whose starting end already sits near one shape and whose moving end approaches another shape, a translucent circle appears at each endpoint sized to the nearby shape's binding zone, where before this release no circles appeared.

Check that with another element already selected, dragging an arrow endpoint near a shape makes a faint highlight appear around that shape while the selected element's dashed border and resize handles still render normally, where before this release no highlight appeared.

Confirm that hovering an arrow endpoint over a shape draws a soft band around the whole shape while hovering near its edge draws a circle at the arrow tip, and that strokes drawn afterwards keep their normal colour and width, where before this release nothing was drawn for either.
uncertainty: The binding and hit-testing code is entirely new with no previous implementation in the diff, so there is no baseline for how close the pointer must be to a rotated shape's edge or to a shape's border to select it or trigger a binding suggestion; judge these cases by whether the on-screen result matches what is visually drawn.

The acceptance zone of the new near-border check for unfilled shapes, especially whether clicks deep inside now select them, depends on helper logic not included in this diff; because the whole hit-test engine was replaced, compare border and center clicks on unfilled shapes against the previous build and report any difference before sign-off.

The evidence shows all changed math routines as newly added files with no removed code, so no specific input that a previous geometry implementation handled differently could be identified from the diff; the checks above are broad regression probes rather than targeted at a proven changed input.

The segment intersection and point-on-segment math was replaced with renamed routines where the point-on-segment check is described as a bounding-box approximation, so edge-case hit detection exactly on element borders or collinear points may differ subtly from the previous behavior; no single concrete failing input was identifiable from the evidence, so border-touching clicks on overlapping shapes are worth extra attention.

The previous implementation of the relocated connection logic was not included in this group's evidence, so old and new behavior could not be diffed and no specific input was identified that the two versions treat differently (the diamond corner change is numerically identical because the value it previously borrowed was already 0); treat any connection behavior that differs from the previous release as a regression and report it.

No affected areas or navigation details were supplied, so all locations are described in business terms and testers must locate the tools themselves; which shape types qualify for connections is also undocumented, so an unexpected refused connection should be raised as a question rather than assumed to be a defect.

This group only wires binding support into resizing and rendering internally; whether an attached arrow follows a bound shape while the shape is resized or rotated is not proven by this group's evidence and should be checked manually alongside the other groups of this release.

The diffs present the new geometry code as additions and the previous implementation's exact outputs are not available, so borderline clicks and arrow attachment points cannot be compared to a documented baseline; judge parity against a pre-change build when deciding whether selection or attachment positions moved slightly.

testAreas.area: Selection and pointer accuracy after the hit-testing rework

Confirm that right-clicking an element opens the element menu with options like Copy, Paste, Copy as PNG, and Copy as SVG, while right-clicking empty canvas shows the canvas menu including Paste and Toggle grid mode.

testAreas.area: Bindings across delete, duplicate, and paste

testAreas.howToReach: Open the Excalidraw editor drawing canvas where shapes are drawn and selected; the context supplies no routes, menu labels, or entry points, so use the normal editor entry.

Test clicking about 8 pixels to the right of a filled rectangle's right edge but well below its bottom-right corner: the shape should now be selected, where previously only clicks within 10 pixels of its bounding box registered.
Check clicking the center of an unfilled rectangle: the result should match the previous build, which required clicking near its border.

Check hovering near a diamond and an ellipse while drawing an arrow: their gray highlights should follow the diamond outline and the ellipse curve rather than the rectangular bounding box.
Verify after binding, moving and resizing the bound shape keeps the arrow attached with the endpoint following smoothly, for rectangles, diamonds, and ellipses.

Verify multiple selected elements show a combined dashed border with corner handles and no rotation handle when not rotating, and that resizing and rotating still work.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied in the application context; this is the main Excalidraw editor canvas where arrows are drawn between shapes.

testAreas.setup: An empty canvas with the shape and line/arrow tools available.
checks: Confirm finishing a newly drawn shape or line at pointer release commits the element and it can immediately be selected at its final position.

testAreas.area: Element selection, context menu, and double-click hit detection

Verify that while an arrow is being drawn and the cursor nears a bindable shape (rectangle, ellipse, diamond, or text), that shape highlights as a connection suggestion and releasing there attaches the arrow end.

Verify that moving a shape and its attached arrow together as one selection moves them as a unit without the arrow jumping or detaching, and that releasing a moved shape over a loose arrow end attaches that end.

testAreas.area: Editing arrow endpoints and detaching connections

Verify that dragging the detached endpoint onto another shape re-attaches it there.
Verify that deleting a bound shape leaves its arrows on the canvas with their last endpoints and without errors.

testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied; on the editor canvas, select several elements and drag them together.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor; no special permissions indicated.

checks: Verify that while dragging a multi-element selection, elements inside the selection are never offered as connection suggestions.
Verify that after the drag all previously existing connections are intact and no unintended new bindings were created.

testAreas.area: Diamond rendering in canvas, image export, and library previews

testAreas.area: Moving, resizing, and rotating shapes with attached arrows

Verify starting an arrow directly on a rectangle and releasing on another rectangle connects both ends, so moving either rectangle moves its matching arrow end.

checks: Confirm the pretend-infinity basis element used when building transforms is exactly the same value as the triple-product basis element, since before this release neither existed and every transform depends on them matching.

Confirm that when one element is selected by you and by a collaborator at once, the dashed border still shows two staggered colour patterns and the rest of the drawing is not shifted or left with a stray dash pattern afterwards.

Verify that hovering an arrow endpoint near a diamond shows a faint band shaped like the diamond and near an ellipse shows a band shaped like the ellipse, each following the shape's own outline, where before this release no highlight appeared.
Confirm that multiplying a value by the plain number 2 doubles every part of it, including its hidden weight part, unlike adding a plain number which touches only the weight.

checks: Verify that dragging a corner handle to enlarge a rectangle that has an arrow attached keeps the arrow endpoint glued to the growing edge the whole time, where before this release the arrow stayed put while the rectangle grew, and confirm the endpoint following the resize is intended.

Check that hovering an arrow endpoint just outside the far left tip of a very wide, flat ellipse gives a steady binding zone at the tip, since the closest point on the curve is now found by a clamped search instead of the looser inline iteration used before.

Check that clicking with the selection tool on the middle of a long straight line, far from either endpoint, still selects the line, since the helper that measured the pointer's distance from the middle of a segment was removed in this release.

Confirm that with a single element selected the rotation handle above it is now a solid filled circle instead of the outlined ellipse drawn before, and that the corner handles around a multi-selection still look like outlined squares.

checks: Verify that clicking just beyond a closed filled loop's box corner but within the ten-pixel margin selects the loop, while clicking inside a thin unfilled zigzag's box but far from every stroke still selects nothing, and confirm both outcomes are intended.
Verify that drawing an arrow so it starts on one rectangle and ends on another now leaves it attached so both ends follow the shapes when you drag them around, which the previous release never did.

Confirm that after you connect an arrow to a very wide, flat ellipse from steeply above and then drag the ellipse around, the arrow stays attached at a point on the upper part of the ellipse instead of sliding to a corner, because before this release arrows never attached to shapes at all.

Verify that while adding extra points to a line or arrow you are drawing, with the newest point not yet committed, moving the pointer near a rectangle now highlights that rectangle as a snapping target, which the previous release never showed.

checks: Check that while dragging a new arrow whose starting end already sits near one shape and whose moving end approaches another shape, a translucent circle appears at each endpoint sized to the nearby shape's binding zone, where before this release no circles appeared.

Check that with another element already selected, dragging an arrow endpoint near a shape makes a faint highlight appear around that shape while the selected element's dashed border and resize handles still render normally, where before this release no highlight appeared.

Confirm that hovering an arrow endpoint over a shape draws a soft band around the whole shape while hovering near its edge draws a circle at the arrow tip, and that strokes drawn afterwards keep their normal colour and width, where before this release nothing was drawn for either.

moreChecks: Check that copying a drawing in which an arrow is attached to a rectangle and pasting it onto the canvas produces a pasted arrow that is attached to the pasted rectangle, whereas before this release the pasted arrow came in loose and unattached.

Verify that after tilting a diamond slightly, hovering an arrow endpoint near it shows the faint binding band tilted to match the diamond rather than drawn upright, where before this release no band was drawn.

Confirm that while you are drawing an arrow with several clicked points and have not finished it, picking a different drawing tool such as the rectangle tool now makes the arrow's last point snap to a nearby shape, which did not happen before this release.

Check that a leftover selection element still produces only a console warning and no selection when clicked, while lines and ellipses are still hit tested normally, and confirm the new unified routing did not change those outcomes.
Confirm that meeting the horizontal axis line with the vertical axis line produces the origin point, even if it arrives carrying a negative weight that has to be cleaned up later.
Confirm that adding a plain number like 2 to a point leaves the point's visible position at 3 across and 4 up unchanged, changing only its hidden weight part.
Check that subtracting the point 1 across, 1 up from the point 3 across, 4 up gives a raw offset of 2 across and 3 up, and confirm that is the intended meaning of point minus point.

Verify that ending an arrow five pixels from a rectangle's edge and then repeating it five pixels from a diamond's slanted edge stores and keeps a small attachment gap in both cases, where before this release no gap between an arrow and a shape was measured at all.

Verify that double-clicking an attached arrow to edit its points and dragging one of its middle points around leaves both of its ends attached to their shapes when you finish; before this release arrows never stayed attached because attachment did not exist.
Verify that with the arrow tool selected, simply hovering the pointer over a rectangle now highlights it as a possible attachment target, which did not happen in the previous release.
Verify that measuring a point 3 across and 4 up against a horizontal line sitting 2 units lower returns roughly 6, the signed gap between them.
Check that joining the origin point with the point 3 across and 4 up produces a line-like value whose two direction parts are 4 and minus 3, and confirm that sign pattern is intended.
Verify that when every component of a value is smaller than one millionth, the printed form is just the single digit 0 rather than a row of near-zero numbers.
Verify that conjugation flips the sign of the six middle parts of a value while leaving the very first and very last parts unflipped, and confirm keeping the last part positive is intended.
Confirm that taking the dual of a value lists its eight parts in exactly reverse order, so a line's numbers reappear mirrored and the plain-number and triple-product parts swap places.

Verify that hovering an arrow endpoint a few pixels beyond a rectangle's top-right corner measures to the top edge when the endpoint sits above the corner's diagonal and to the right edge when it sits below it, where before this release no such distance was computed.

Check that a tiny rectangle offers a binding zone of at least fifteen pixels, a very large rectangle's zone stops growing at eighty pixels, and a large diamond's zone is proportionally smaller than the rectangle's to match its slanted sides, where before this release no binding zone existed.
Check that building a base unit element while asking for slot number 8 fails loudly with an error instead of quietly returning an all-zero value, and confirm failing loudly is intended.

Check that while dragging an arrow's endpoint to a spot about ten pixels outside a rectangle's edge the rectangle counts as a binding target, and that moving the endpoint to the rectangle's centre stops it from counting, because before this release neither position produced any binding reaction.

Confirm that clicking about five pixels above a text element now selects the text, and that clicking the middle of a heavily rotated arrow selects the arrow, where before this release the click above the text selected nothing and the rotated arrow's midsection could be missed.
Check that after tilting an ellipse slightly, hovering an arrow endpoint near it shows the faint binding band tilted with the ellipse and no stray rotation left behind on later strokes.
Confirm that normalizing a value whose corner-area part is negative flips the entire value so that part turns positive, and that values already at length zero or one are handed back untouched.

Check that hovering an arrow endpoint just outside a diamond's slanted upper edge, close to where a straight box edge would be far away, puts the diamond in its binding zone, because the distance is now measured to the slanted side instead of to a straight box edge as before.

Verify that when an attachment highlight is showing, switching to the free-draw pencil tool leaves the highlight in place while switching to the rectangle tool clears it, because the pencil is meant to count as a line-type tool; before this release no tool switch affected anything since highlights did not exist.

Confirm that hovering an arrow endpoint just outside the curved top of a wide ellipse opens the binding zone along the curve, and that a point just inside the curve does not open it, since the distance is now measured to the curved outline with inside counting as negative, where before this release nothing was measured.
Check that taking a direction between two identical points returns an all-zero direction instead of not-a-number values, since the ideal length is zero there.

Check that waving the pointer in and out over shapes with the arrow tool so attachment highlights flash on and off keeps the side toolbar responding normally with the current settings shown as before this release.
Check that the small handles shown when editing a line's points and the rotation handle above a selection are now solid filled dots rather than hollow outlined circles as before.
Check that the measured gap between the origin point and the point 3 across and 4 up comes out as exactly 5.

Verify that clicking a spot where a small shape overlaps a larger one still selects the topmost shape as before, and that the endpoint lookup for binding picks the bindable shape under the endpoint using the same front-to-back order, and confirm both are intended.
Verify that the direction-flavored measure of a direction of 3 across and 4 up reads 5, mirroring the ordinary length measure but for directions.
Check that shifting the vertical axis line 2 units only lowers its distance coefficient by 2 while the original line stays unchanged, and confirm the direction of the shift is intended.

Verify that after double-clicking a line to edit its points, each vertex shows a solid filled dot centred exactly on the point, rather than the hollow circle that sat slightly offset from the point before, and that the point being edited still shows tinted.
Verify that building a direction from moving 3 across and 4 up produces a length-one direction split as 0.6 across and 0.8 up, and confirm that normalizing is intended.
Verify that when a single plain number is supplied instead of a full eight-part value, the operation still returns a valid result with no not-a-number parts.
Check that combining a point with itself through the scalar-only product yields minus 1 rather than plus 1, and confirm this flipped sign is intended.
Confirm that pulling a direction out of the point 3 across and 4 up keeps exactly those two amounts while dropping the weight part, so the result is a pure direction.

Confirm that clicking just inside the edge of a selected shape and clicking far inside its centre both still select it, and that a click within the ten-pixel margin outside also selects it, and that this widening is intended.
Check that a raw offset of 3 across and 5 down is stored with the vertical amount 5 in the first slot and the horizontal amount 3 in the second, and confirm this swapped order is intended.
Confirm that mirroring the point at minus 3 across and minus 4 up lands it at 3 across and 4 up with its weight forced to exactly one, even if the input carried a different weight.

Confirm that offering a binding on the left side of an ellipse and then on the right side yields a positive attachment gap both times, because the line's sign is now read and flipped in the distance, where before this release no such measurement existed.

Verify that offering a binding near each of the four corners of a rectangle always measures the gap to the nearer of the two edges meeting at that corner, since a diagonal through the shape's centre now decides which edge is compared, where before this release no measurement existed.

Verify that hovering an arrow endpoint deep inside a large rectangle does not mark it as a binding border, while hovering just outside its edge within the gap band does, because only strictly outside points now pass, where before this release neither position signalled anything.
Verify that combining a rotation with a translation applies the translation first and the rotation second, and confirm this reversed order is intended.

Verify that after an attachment highlight appears on a shape while the arrow tool is active, switching to the rectangle tool makes the highlight disappear at once; before this release no highlights existed to clear.
Verify that holding down Ctrl or Cmd while drawing an arrow that ends on a rectangle leaves the arrow unattached, whereas before this release it attached no matter which keys were held.

Confirm that pressing and releasing Ctrl or Cmd and then drawing an arrow onto a rectangle attaches it again, since releasing the keys turns attachment back on; before this release there was nothing to re-enable because attachment was always active.
Verify that turning a vertical line into a direction yields a horizontal direction along the line's normal, and confirm that is the intended meaning of perpendicular to a line.
Check that the perpendicular of a rightward unit direction points straight down, and confirm that this downward rather than upward choice is intended.
Confirm that the distance between two parallel horizontal lines 2 units apart reads 2, while two crossing lines read as 0 apart.
Check that building a move of 4 units along a line uses exactly half that distance, 2, times the line's perpendicular direction, and confirm this halving is intended.

Confirm that drawing an arrow onto a rectangle attaches it and that the attached end keeps meeting the rectangle's edge cleanly when you drag the rectangle around afterwards; this attachment geometry is new in this release.

Check that drawing an arrow attached to a piece of text and then emptying that text and pressing Escape leaves the arrow cleanly detached instead of keeping a stale link; before this release arrows could not attach to text at all so nothing was left behind.

Check that double-clicking an attached arrow to enter point editing and pressing Escape straight away keeps both ends attached to their shapes, something the previous release could not do since arrows did not attach.

Confirm that double-clicking a piece of text that lies on top of another shape still opens that text for editing as it did before this release, since the way the app decides which element sits under the pointer was rebuilt.

Confirm that if you hold Ctrl or Cmd to pause attachment, switch to another window and come back, the next arrow you draw onto a rectangle attaches again without pressing anything else; before this release attachment was simply always on.

Confirm that right-clicking directly on the outline of an unfilled shape still opens the shape's own menu with copy, paste, copy-as-image and delete, rather than the empty-canvas menu, because pointer hit-testing was reworked in this release.
Check that with a group of shapes selected, double-clicking one member of the group still drills into the group and selects just that one element for editing as before this release.

report.summary: This release adds text that lives inside shapes, so those labels now behave as part of the shape when selected, edited, moved, resized, copied, and exported.
keyChanges: Text can now be attached to shapes: while typing, lines wrap to the shape's width, the shape's height grows line by line as text is added and shrinks back when text is removed, and the text stays vertically centered; standalone text keeps the old no-wrap behavior.

Finishing text editing now wraps the typed text to the shape's width and links or unlinks it to the shape: clearing the text and clicking away removes the text element and unbinds it, submission is skipped if the text element no longer exists, and while typing only standalone text re-measures its box per keystroke while bound text updates dimensions on submit.

New text elements (including pasted text and chart labels) now also store the original un-wrapped text and their container link, so changing font family, font size, or text alignment, or pasting styles, re-measures the text box from the original text (within the shape width for bound text) instead of the previously stored text.
Text measurement gained a width-limited wrapping mode and an approximate line-height calculation, which now also drive how bound text is drawn on the canvas and in exports.
When starting text editing, text elements are excluded from the container lookup, so double-clicking a shape that already has text edits that existing text.

Creating text by double-clicking at the center of a shape, or clicking its center with the text tool, now attaches the text to that shape: a shape smaller than one line of text is enlarged to fit, and dragging or deleting the shape takes the text with it, while double-clicking away from a shape's center still creates free-standing text as before.

Clicking directly on attached text now selects the containing shape rather than the text, and a selection box drawn around a shape returns only the shape, with the attached text excluded from selection.

Double-clicking a selected shape that already has attached text reopens that existing text for editing at the shape's center instead of adding a second text, and after submitting with the keyboard the shape is selected rather than the text.
Duplicating a shape with attached text (duplicate command, copy/paste, or alt+drag copy) now keeps the copy's text attached to the duplicated shape.

The on-canvas text editor is now positioned using raw viewport coordinates, free-standing text recalculates its size live while typing and on submit, and text attached to a shape only updates its size when editing finishes.

Resizing a container with bound text now rewraps the text to the new width, grows the container taller when the text no longer fits, keeps the text vertically centered, and keeps the bottom edge anchored when resizing from a top handle.

Rotating, dragging, duplicating, and flipping a container were reworked around a new bound-text lookup, so confirm the text stays attached, centered, and positioned correctly through each of these actions.

Font-size scaling during resize now measures bound text at its container width, so scaling a multi-selection or a single text element keeps wrapped multi-line text inside its container; the text-type check in multi-element resize became null-safe with no intended behavior change.
Minimum sizes for adding bound text now include padding, so starting to type in a small shape expands it to at least one character's width and one line's height.
Text wrapping on commit and the character-width cache used for wrap decisions were reworked, so edited text wraps at the container width and clearing all text releases it from the shape.
Copying or cutting now includes text attached to a selected shape, where previously the attached text was left behind on the canvas; this applies to keyboard copy and cut and the app's Copy action.

Clicking inside a shape now drags it when the shape has attached text even if its background is transparent, and transparency now also covers semi-transparent and fully transparent custom fills such as #ffffff00, which previously counted as filled and were draggable from inside.

Text attached to a shape now wraps to the shape's width while editing, and the shape automatically grows to enclose the text (text size plus roughly 30px of padding) whenever the text would overflow it; committed text edits now also record the original text and recalculate the text box size only when the edit requires it, and the center/middle re-centering logic now applies only to standalone text.

Text measuring moved to the text-element code and now accepts a width cap; all text-sizing paths (new text, font family, font size, and alignment changes, paste styles, handle-resizing of text, and pasted spreadsheet chart labels) go through it, with no visible change expected for plain standalone text.

Selecting exactly one rectangle, diamond, ellipse, or image now shows a hint-bar tip about binding text to that element; these selections previously showed no tip, while the tips for lines, arrows, and standalone text behave as before.

Arrows can no longer attach to text that lives inside a shape; the connection now targets the containing shape, while standalone text outside any shape remains attachable. The same rule now governs connection cleanup when elements with text are deleted and restored by undo and redo.
Text inside shapes is now measured through a new per-character width cache and canvas measurement; committing typed text and resizing or flipping a shape re-wraps its text through this new path.
The connection-cleanup rule is exercised by the automated history and collaboration test suites, which is coverage evidence rather than user-facing impact.
Dragging a shape with attached text now carries the text along, including when dragging groups and when drag-duplicating with the duplicate modifier held, where the text previously stayed behind.

Pasting or inserting copied, dropped, or library elements now reattaches duplicated attached text to the correct pasted shape, and after the insert only free-standing text items remain selected, where previously every pasted element stayed selected.

Clicking a shape that already has attached text with the text tool now opens the existing attached text for editing centered on the shape, and pressing Enter with a shape selected now creates text bound to that shape instead of a floating text.
Exporting the selection to PNG or SVG and adding the current selection to the library now include text attached to selected shapes, which was previously left out.
Opening, importing, or reloading scenes, including collaboration data and library items, now preserves each text element's link to its shape and its original text instead of dropping them.

Multi-line text attached to a shape (bound text) is now drawn with line height estimated from its font instead of dividing the text's total height by its line count, so lines no longer stretch to fill the shape, while standalone text keeps the old height-based spacing in this shared canvas renderer that produces both the editing view and every image output.

Because one renderer draws everything, the new bound-text spacing reaches the on-screen canvas, the PNG/SVG export dialog preview, copy-as-PNG and copy-as-SVG clipboard actions, saving a drawing back into its image file, publish-library preview generation, and the embeddable package export helpers, which have automated test coverage.
Selection handling now treats bound text as part of its shape: a selection box covering the shape selects the shape with its attached text, and bound text alone is not captured as a separate element.

The remaining edits are supporting wiring — new element fields recording the owning shape and the text as originally typed, a dedicated bound-text type, and new imports in the text editor and renderer — with no runtime behavior beyond enabling the changes above.

Commands that act on the current selection — add to library, copy as PNG, copy as SVG, and group — now include the text bound inside a selected shape, so labels that were previously left out of a copied image, a saved library item, or a new group now travel with their container.
Deleting a selected shape now also deletes the text bound inside it; previously the label could survive after its container was deleted.

Duplicating now copies the bound label into the duplicate and re-attaches it to the copied shape, and the duplicated label is no longer left individually selected, so dragging right after duplicating moves the copy as one unit.
Select all (Ctrl/Cmd+A) no longer selects bound labels individually; the container is selected and the label follows it for later delete, duplicate, and move operations.
Grouping now counts bound labels: selecting a single labeled shape can enable the Group command, and grouping labeled shapes puts their labels inside the group.

Verify a standalone text element containing tab characters keeps a bounding box that still fits the rendered text after a font size change (no clipping or visible gap).
Verify with the text editor still open, changing font size from the properties panel re-synchronizes line spacing and shape height instead of leaving stale spacing.
Verify double-clicking a shape that already has text opens the existing text for editing in place rather than creating a second overlapping text element.

Verify pasted plain text creates normal editable text elements that can be restyled like newly typed text.

Check double-clicking a selected shape that already has attached text: the existing text opens for editing with no second text created, and after pressing Enter or Escape the shape itself ends up selected.

Confirm the on-canvas text editor appears exactly over the text being edited, including after zooming or scrolling the canvas.
Ensure clearing all text and submitting removes the attached text but leaves the shape on the canvas.
