Ensure deleting a selected shape also deletes its attached text, and undo restores both the shape and its text.
Verify dragging a corner handle to make the container much narrower rewraps the text to the new width and the container grows taller instead of clipping the text.
Verify resizing from the top edge or a top corner moves the container's top up so the bottom edge stays anchored while the text rewraps.
Verify resizing the container wider rewraps the text into fewer lines and the text stays vertically centered inside the shape.
Verify very small width adjustments do not rewrap the text erratically, while narrowing by about one character's width or more does rewrap it.

Verify dragging a corner handle to scale the selection down and up changes the standalone text's font size proportionally while the bound text keeps fitting inside its container, wrapped at the container's width.
Verify after scaling, the bound text stays vertically centered in its container with the baseline aligned (no text floating above or sinking below the container).
Verify selecting only a container with bound text and resizing it by a corner handle scales the font size so the text still fits the container.
Verify typing a single very long word wider than the container breaks it across lines instead of letting it overflow the shape.
Verify clicking away after editing wraps the text at the container width with no stray extra lines or clipped edges.
Verify deleting all text and clicking away removes the empty text from the shape so the shape no longer holds an empty text element.
Verify rotating the container with the rotation handle keeps the text attached, centered, and rotated with the shape.
Verify dragging the container moves its text with it, and duplicating the container creates a copy with its own text that stays inside the copy when the original is moved.
Verify flipping a container with bound text keeps the text inside the shape and correctly positioned afterwards.
Verify double-clicking the small shape to add text expands it to at least the minimum character width and line height so the text editor and resulting text are not clipped.
Verify adding text to a normally sized shape does not unexpectedly change its size.
Verify that selecting the shape with attached text, copying it, and pasting elsewhere produces a duplicate that includes the attached text (previously the text was left behind).
Verify that cutting the shape with attached text and pasting places both the shape and its attached text.
Ensure that copying a multi-element selection that includes a shape with attached text brings that text along in the pasted result.
Verify that clicking inside the transparent shape that has attached text and dragging now moves the whole shape together with its text.

Check that clicking inside the shape with the fully transparent custom fill (#ffffff00) and no attached text no longer grabs it from its empty interior, while the shape remains selectable via its border (such fills now count as transparent).
Ensure the opaque-filled shape can still be dragged by clicking inside it as before.
Verify that attached text longer than the shape's width wraps inside the shape while editing instead of spilling outside it.
Test typing a very long line into a shape's attached text: the shape should grow automatically so the text stays fully enclosed with roughly 30px of padding on the tight sides.
Confirm that a standalone centered, middle-aligned text still recenters in place when edited, since that offset logic now applies only to standalone text.
Verify that changing font family, font size, and text alignment on a text element keeps the text fully visible inside its box and correctly positioned.
Ensure resizing a text element with the corner handles still scales its font size correctly.
Test pasting spreadsheet content and choosing a chart: axis labels should be sized and positioned correctly.
Ensure multi-line text containing empty lines is measured and placed correctly, since the text-measuring code moved and its old version padded empty lines with a single space.
Verify dragging an arrow endpoint onto text that sits inside a shape attaches the arrow to the shape itself, and that moving or resizing the shape keeps the connection.
Verify an arrow still attaches to a standalone text element that is not inside any shape, and to plain shapes as before.
Verify deleting a shape that contains text while an arrow is attached removes the connection cleanly, and Undo and Redo restore the shape, its text, and the connection intact.
Verify typing multi-word text into a shape wraps the lines within the shape's inner width with even padding on both sides.
Verify resizing a text-filled shape narrower and then wider with side and corner handles re-wraps the text so it stays inside the shape without overflowing or leaving large gaps.

Verify a single long word wider than the shape breaks across lines character by character and the editor stays responsive, and flipping the shape horizontally and vertically keeps its text positioned and readable.

Verify selecting exactly one rectangle, diamond, ellipse, or image shows the new tip about binding text to the element on both desktop and the mobile menu, and the tip area never goes blank or errors.
Verify selecting one line or arrow still shows the line-editor tips, both when entering point-edit mode with no point selected and with a point selected.
Verify selecting a standalone text element still shows its text-editing tip rather than the new bind-text tip.
Verify dragging a shape with attached text moves the text together with the shape, and a connected arrow stays attached to it.
Test drag-duplicating (hold the duplicate modifier while dragging) a shape with attached text: the duplicate carries its own attached copy of the text and the original keeps its text.
Verify dragging a group containing a shape with attached text moves the text with the group at the same offset as the shape, not left behind or shifted twice.
Verify copying a shape with attached text and pasting it: the pasted copy carries the text attached to the pasted shape and the original shape keeps its own text.

Confirm pasting plain shapes or images now leaves them unselected after the paste, where previously all pasted content stayed selected, and that the pasted content can still be clicked and moved normally afterwards.

Test clicking with the text tool on a shape that already has attached text, aiming away from the shape's center: the existing attached text opens for editing at the shape's center instead of a new floating text being created at the click point.
Verify selecting a shape, pressing Enter, typing, pressing Escape, and then moving the shape: the typed text moves together with the shape instead of remaining behind as a separate floating text.

Validate that with export limited to the selection the live preview includes the attached text and the exported PNG or SVG file contains it, where previously the attached text was missing from the output.
Verify saving a scene containing a shape with attached text and reopening the saved file: the text is still attached to the shape and positioned correctly.
Verify selecting a shape with attached text, adding it to the library, and inserting it back into a scene: the inserted item includes its attached text.
Ensure rejoining or reloading a live collaboration session keeps attached text bound to its shape.

Verify that multi-line text attached to a shape much taller than the text keeps line spacing based on its font size instead of stretching the lines apart to fill the shape, including text with blank or trailing empty lines.
Check bound text with a large font size and each available font family for even, non-overlapping line spacing inside its shape.
Confirm a standalone multi-line text element still distributes its lines across the text element's own height exactly as before.
Verify that a selection box dragged over only the shape selects the shape together with its bound text.
Verify the dialog's live preview shows the same bound-text line spacing as the editor canvas.
Ensure an exported PNG at two different export scales matches the preview's bound-text spacing, with standalone text unchanged.
Verify that a drawing with a shape containing multi-line bound text, copied as PNG and pasted into another application, shows line spacing matching the canvas.
Confirm that copy-as-SVG still produces a valid SVG whose bound-text spacing matches the canvas.
Verify that saving the drawing to its active file and reopening it preserves the bound-text line spacing and that the scene stored inside the image loads correctly.
Test the library publishing flow for an item containing a shape with bound text and confirm the generated preview image's spacing matches the canvas.
Verify that selecting only the labeled rectangle and pressing Delete removes both the rectangle and its label, and that Undo restores both.
Ensure deleting a mixed selection of labeled shapes and plain shapes removes every label together with its container while the standalone (unbound) text element remains untouched.
Confirm deleting a selected group that contains a labeled shape also removes the label, and Undo brings the whole group back.

Confirm duplicating a labeled shape produces a copy that contains its own label, the original keeps its label, and dragging the duplicate immediately afterwards moves shape and label together without the label drifting or jumping back to the original.
Verify duplicating a selection of plain shapes without bound text still copies every shape as before, since duplication now runs an extra label-rebinding pass on every duplication.
Test duplicating a selected group of labeled elements: each copy keeps its own label inside it.
Verify that Copy as PNG with a labeled shape selected, followed by pasting the result, produces an image that includes the label text.
Confirm that Copy as SVG with the same selection renders the label inside the shape at the correct position when pasted into an external viewer.
Ensure that adding a labeled shape to the library stores its label with it, so inserting that library item later puts the text back inside the shape.
Verify that with only one labeled shape selected the Group command is now available, and grouping ties the shape and its label so moving them keeps the label inside.

Check that grouping a labeled shape with a plain shape includes the label in the group, so selecting and moving the group carries the label, and that ungrouping afterwards leaves the label correctly bound to its shape.
Verify that after Ctrl/Cmd+A, dragging the selection moves every shape together with its label and no label is left behind or offset.
Confirm that after Ctrl/Cmd+A, Delete removes all shapes and their labels, and Ctrl/Cmd+D duplicates all of them with labels intact.

Verify that typing one very long unbroken word, such as a long web address, as the label of a narrow shape and clicking away breaks the word across several lines to fit the shape's width instead of running past its edges; text could not be attached to shapes before this release, so confirm the breaking is intended.

Confirm that pressing Enter repeatedly while editing text inside a shape grows the shape taller line by line, and deleting those lines shrinks it back toward its original height with the text kept vertically centered, rather than the text overflowing a fixed-size shape as happened before.

Confirm that dragging the right edge of a rectangle with text attached inside it to make it narrower rewraps the label to the new width, grows the rectangle taller when the text needs more lines, and keeps the label centered; text could not be attached to shapes before this release, so confirm this reflow behavior is intended.

Verify that when you finish typing text inside a shape by clicking outside, the text stays inside the shape broken into lines that fit its width, instead of being saved as one long line that could stick out past the shape's border as before.

Verify that when text inside a shape is re-measured after a change, any line longer than the shape's width now counts as multiple wrapped lines so the text box grows taller rather than wider, instead of being measured without a width limit as before.

Verify that double-clicking inside the centre of a small empty rectangle now creates a text bound inside it and enlarges the rectangle to fit the minimum text size, whereas before it inserted an unbound text element at the click position.
Check that copying a shape that has a label and pasting it produces a pasted label attached to the pasted shape, where before the pasted label ended up detached from its shape.

Confirm that shapes and strokes you draw from scratch with each toolbar tool still come out with the same default styling and normal selecting, moving, and resizing behavior they had before this release.
Verify that dragging a resize handle to make a shape with text inside narrower re-wraps the text so fewer characters fit on each line, where previously resizing could not change any text.

Confirm that the editor which opens when you double-click a shape wraps long text at the shape's edges and grows downward as you type, instead of extending on a single unwrapped line past the shape as editors did before.

Check that when you double-click a rectangle and type a label whose sentence is wider than the rectangle, the text now breaks onto a new line at the rectangle's edge instead of continuing on one line past the shape as it did before this release, and confirm the wrapping is intended.

Confirm that dragging the middle-left handle of a plain rectangle to the right, past the rectangle's right edge, now stops the resize at zero width instead of flipping the rectangle through to the other side of its right edge as happened before this release, and check that blocking that flip-through is intended.

Check that with a shape's text editor open, picking a larger font size in the toolbar makes the shape grow tall enough to hold the bigger text instead of leaving the text overflowing an unchanged shape as before.

Verify that duplicating a labelled shape, for example with Ctrl+D or by Alt-dragging it, now produces exactly one label bound to the duplicated shape with only the shape left selected, whereas before the duplicate label could end up selected on its own instead of together with its shape.

Verify that after typing a long sentence into a double-clicked rectangle and clicking away, reopening that text shows the sentence exactly as you originally typed it rather than only the line-broken copy that used to be saved.
uncertainty: The evidence does not show whether text elements restored from previously saved files receive the new saved pre-wrapped text value that re-measuring now relies on; the restyling check on an older saved file covers this, and any error or wrong sizing there should be reported.

No affected pages, menus, or routes were supplied for these canvas-level changes, so navigation is described only in general terms; drawings saved before this change contain only free-standing text, so spot-check that text already overlapping shapes in older files is still selected and edited independently of the shapes.

The before/after evidence for the container-resize path was only partially supplied, so exercise container resizing with bound text through corner handles, edge handles, and the flip action to catch any mismatch in how the text rewraps or repositions.

The text-measuring routine moved into the text-element code and now accepts a width cap, but its new implementation was not supplied for review; whether its previous handling of empty lines (padding them with a single space when measuring) is preserved could not be confirmed, so multi-line text with blank lines is covered by the spot-check above. No behavioral difference is proven for plain standalone text.

The new tip's wording comes from translation files not covered by this change, and the translation lookup fails hard on a missing phrase, so check the new tip in at least one non-default language to confirm it renders instead of erroring when a shape is selected.

No documentation confirms whether the narrowed post-paste selection (only free-standing text stays selected, while pasted shapes, groups, and images are no longer selected) is intended for all content types; this is the most likely unintended UX change, so confirm with the team that users can still immediately act on pasted shapes.

Bound-text line spacing is now an estimate derived from the font rather than the text's measured height, so the spacing drawn on canvas or in exports may differ slightly from what you see while editing the text; check multi-line bound text in each available font family for consistency between the editing view and the drawn canvas and exports.

Group is now offered when the only selection is a single shape containing text, because its bound label counts as a second selected element; the supplied context does not confirm whether this is intended or whether Group should still require two or more separately selected shapes.

Check that double-clicking a very narrow shape, one narrower than a single character of the current font, to start typing inside it now widens the shape to at least one character's width plus padding so the text fits; text could not be placed inside shapes before this release, so confirm the shape widening is intended.

Confirm that double-clicking directly on a label inside a shape still opens that existing label for editing rather than creating a brand-new separate text element, since ordinary clicks now skip labels and the text editor lookup must still find them.

Check that double-clicking a very flat shape, one shorter than a line of text, to start typing inside it now stretches the shape to at least one line of text in height so the text fits; text could not be placed inside shapes before this release, so confirm the shape growing is intended.

Verify that after wrapping text inside a shape, closing the text editor and double-clicking the shape again to type more produces line breaks consistent with the earlier ones because the remembered character widths are reused, where previously nothing about the text was stored between edits.

Check that grouping a shape with a typed-in text label together with another shape now makes the label part of the new group along with its shape, where before the group was created with the shapes only and the label stayed outside it.

Check that drawing a selection box fully around a labelled shape now selects just the shape rather than the shape and its label as two separate items, which is how it worked before.

Confirm that with a single shape that has a text label typed into it selected, the Group option is now offered in the selection panel and right-click menu, where before it appeared only once at least two separately selected elements were present.

Check that selecting a shape with a text label typed into it and choosing Add to library now saves the label together with the shape, where before the saved library item contained the shape only and the label was lost.

Verify that Copy as SVG with a shape that has a typed-in text label selected now includes the label when the SVG is pasted into another program, where before the copied SVG left the label out.

report.summary: The release adds the ability to attach web links to canvas elements in the editor, including a link icon, popup, and keyboard shortcut, with underlying data changes that make element creation and scene loading the main areas to re-test.
keyChanges: Selecting exactly one element now shows a new link action in the selected-shape panel and in the mobile menu; with two or more elements selected the action stays hidden.
The Help dialog now lists the link tool with its Ctrl or Cmd+K shortcut.

Tooltip display was reorganized around a shared positioning routine that clamps tooltips inside the viewport with a small margin and can place them above or below a control; all editor tooltips (toolbar, panels, library, zoom, export options, footer) and the element-link URL tooltip now use it, so behavior near screen edges changed and the link URL tooltip appears above the element's link icon.

The link icon's position and size (zoom-scaled and rotated with the element) now come from one shared calculation used for drawing, click detection, and tooltip placement; hovering a linked element shows its URL after a short delay, moving the pointer away hides it, and clicking the icon opens the link, so exports or clipboard copies containing linked elements should be spot-checked.

Drawing elements can now carry a link: the canvas draws a fixed-size (about 14 px) external-link icon at the top-right corner of each linked element while it is not selected, the icon follows the shape's rotation and zoom, and unlinked shapes show nothing.

Link icons are excluded from all export paths: the image export dialog, PNG/SVG copies, clipboard copies, and saved-image reshares render in export mode where the icon is skipped, so exported and pasted images show shapes only.
The right-click menu on an element gains a new link menu item (shown when the selection qualifies), and opening any context menu now closes the link popup if it is visible.

The new link popup state starts hidden, hides automatically when the tool switches away from selection, resets with clear canvas or scene reset, and is stripped from saved files, exports, and browser storage so it never persists between sessions.

Restored drawing elements now carry a link property (null when a shape has none), so hyperlink data attached to shapes survives opening files, drag-and-drop, paste, library items, and collaboration loads, while scenes saved before this change load unchanged.

A link keyboard shortcut (Ctrl/Cmd+K) is registered and the K key added, so the shortcuts list and context-menu hints can now show it; K was previously unmapped, so no existing shortcut should be displaced.

Canvas scene rendering gained internal support for link markers (an external-link image, handle coordinates, and a canvas cache), and a 300 ms hyperlink tooltip delay constant was added; a whitespace-only cleanup in the rounded-diamond path drawing has no expected visual effect.
The remaining edits are additive groundwork with no standalone behavior change: a new edit icon, the link action re-export, and a hyperlink-popup app-state field.

A new link action opens a link editor popup for a selected element from a new panel button, the right-click context menu, or the Ctrl/Cmd+K shortcut, and triggering it again while the editor is already open does nothing.

The context-menu entry appears only when exactly one element is selected; its wording reflects whether that element already has a link (edit) or not (create), and the panel button shows as active only when the single selected element has a link.

Every newly created element now stores a link field that defaults to none, which is the persistence for this feature; creation itself is otherwise unchanged, so shapes, freehand strokes, lines and arrows, text, images, and spreadsheet-pasted charts should behave exactly as before.

Once a link is saved, a popup over the element stays visible while the pointer is over the element, the gap up to the popup, or the popup itself, and hides about half a second after the pointer leaves them; the shared bounding-box hit test it uses only became reusable with no logic change, so selection behavior should be unaffected.

Selecting a single canvas element can show a hyperlink popover with a 'Type or paste your link here' input; Enter or Escape saves the entry and switches the popover to a view showing the saved link with Edit and Remove (trash) buttons.

Saved addresses are normalized: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and any address without '://' that does not start with '/' or '[' gets 'https://' prefixed, so 'example.com' is saved as 'https://example.com', while an empty or whitespace-only entry is saved as an empty link and keeps the edit input showing.

Pressing and releasing on the small chain icon at an element's top-right corner opens the saved URL in a new tab for external addresses and in the same tab for addresses starting with '/' or containing the app's own address; the popover's link text follows the same rule, and Ctrl/Cmd+K is blocked while the link input has focus.

The popover is centered above the element's top edge, disappears during drag, resize, or rotation, and auto-hides after a brief delay once the pointer leaves the element, the vertical gap between element and popover, or the popover itself; the Remove button, shown only when a link exists, deletes the link and closes the popover.

Elements with an attached web link are now interactive on the drawing canvas: hovering the element's link icon shows a hand cursor and a tooltip with the link, and a click that both presses and releases on the icon opens the URL, with same-site or slash-prefixed links opening in the current tab and external links opening in a new tab.

Pressing on a link icon no longer starts selecting or dragging that element, and selecting exactly one linked element, whether by clicking it or by dragging a selection box that ends containing exactly one linked element, now shows a small link popup on the canvas that is only rendered while exactly one element is selected.

The editor now remembers where the last press and release happened so it can tell a real link click from a drag, and closing the context menu by pressing the canvas no longer keeps the link popup suppressed.

Canvas hover cursor logic was restructured around the link check; cursors for the text tool, view mode, scrollbars and normal element dragging are preserved, and multi-point line editing now shows a move cursor over the line's points where the cursor previously did not update.
The base data definition behind every drawing element (shapes, lines, arrows, text, images, frames) now declares a link slot that holds either a text value or an empty (null) value.

This is a compile-time declaration only: no executable code was added or removed, the dependency graph shows no dependent code, and no screen, route, or menu was supplied for this area, so no confirmed user-facing change exists in this group.
qaChecks: Verify that selecting exactly one element shows a link action in the selected-shape panel and in the mobile menu on a small screen, and that selecting two or more elements hides it.

Verify that after attaching a URL to a single element using the new link action or Ctrl or Cmd+K, hovering the element shows a tooltip with the link URL above the link icon at the element's top-right after a brief pause, and that the tooltip hides as soon as the pointer moves away.
Verify that at different zoom levels and with the element rotated, the link icon stays attached at the element's top-right, the tooltip follows it, and clicking the icon still opens the link.
Verify the Help dialog shows a new shortcut row for the link tool with Ctrl or Cmd+K and opens without errors, including in a non-English language if available.
Verify that hovering familiar controls such as the zoom reset control and the export dialog's embed-scene option still shows each tooltip with its usual text near the control.

Verify that hovering a control near the viewport's left or right edge keeps the tooltip fully inside the window with a small margin instead of cutting it off, and that near the bottom edge the tooltip flips above the control when there is no room below.

Verify that exporting a drawing with a linked, unselected element to PNG or SVG and copying it to the clipboard completes and the image renders normally, with any link icon on the linked element in its usual top-right spot.

Verify a rectangle with a link attached through the new link menu shows a small external-link icon at its top-right corner while unselected, and that the icon disappears while the rectangle is selected.
Check that a plain shape with no link shows no icon anywhere, and that a shape whose link is cleared or removed through the link menu loses its icon.
Test the linked shape rotated 45 degrees and zoomed between 50% and 200%: the icon stays at the rotated top-right corner and keeps a constant on-screen size.
Confirm the icon also appears on other linked element types such as text and images, not just rectangles.
Verify exporting a scene that contains one linked shape and one plain shape to PNG and SVG through the image export dialog produces files with no link icon on the linked shape.
Check that Copy as PNG on a selection containing the linked shape pastes into another application as an image without the link icon.
Verify right-clicking a single element shows the new link menu item (between the flip options and duplicate/delete) and that using it attaches or edits the shape's URL.
Check that right-clicking empty canvas offers no link item.
Ensure the link popup can still be shown normally after a context-menu action such as Duplicate has run.
Confirm that opening the context menu while the link popup is visible closes the popup.
Verify switching from the selection tool to another tool, for example the rectangle tool, while the popup is visible hides it.
Ensure Clear canvas or a scene reset closes the popup, and that reloading an existing saved drawing (browser storage or a saved scene file) opens it as before with no link popup showing on load.
Verify a drawing saved before this change opens with all shapes, text, arrows, and images intact and no error.
Check that a scene whose shapes carry link data loads without errors and that, after saving and reopening it, the link data is still attached to the same shapes.
Ensure copying shapes and pasting them onto the canvas still inserts the pasted copies correctly.
Verify the scene renders exactly as before, with no unexpected link icons or handles appearing on shapes.
Confirm drawing, moving, resizing, selecting shapes, and the right-click canvas menu still work and render correctly.
Verify joining an existing session loads the full shared scene with all elements and no error.
Confirm a scene containing linked shapes still loads and that edits sync normally between collaborators.
Verify library items still show their previews and insert into the canvas without errors.
Check that an item created from a linked shape still previews and inserts correctly, and that publishing a library still generates its preview image.
Verify the shortcuts list now shows a link entry with Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) + K and that all previously listed shortcuts are unchanged.
Test pressing Ctrl/Cmd+K with a shape selected: it should trigger the link action without errors and leave nearby shortcuts such as duplicate (Ctrl/Cmd+D) and group (Ctrl/Cmd+G) working.
Verify that with exactly one element selected, pressing Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the link editor popup and pressing it again while the editor is already open leaves the editor open without errors.
Verify that the right-click context menu shows the link entry only when exactly one element is selected and omits it when nothing or two or more elements are selected.
Verify that for an element without a link the link entry offers creating one, and after a link is saved the entry offers editing and the panel link button appears active.
Verify on a touch device that a long-press on an element opens the context menu with the link entry under the same single-selection rule.

Verify that typing a URL in the link editor and confirming, including by closing the popup, stores it on the element so reopening the editor shows the saved URL and the popup switches to its info view.

Verify that moving the pointer from the element through the gap between the element and the popup into the popup keeps the popup visible the whole way, and that it auto-hides about half a second after the pointer leaves both.
Verify that a small tolerance around the element's edges still counts as hovering the element so the popup does not flicker away near the border.
Verify that creating each basic element type (shape, freehand stroke, line or arrow, text, image) still works and each can be selected and moved as before.
Verify that pasting spreadsheet content still offers the chart choice and inserting the chart produces the same chart elements and preview as before.
Verify that a drawing with several element types still saves and reopens with all elements intact now that created elements carry the new link field.

Verify typing example.com into the popover input and pressing Enter saves it as https://example.com and the popover switches to showing the link with Edit and Remove buttons; also paste ' example.com ' with surrounding spaces and confirm it saves the same trimmed https://example.com.
Verify pressing Enter with an empty or whitespace-only input does not crash the editor, leaves the element without a usable link, and the popover keeps showing the empty edit input.
Verify clicking Edit reopens the input pre-filled with the saved link, and while the input has focus Ctrl/Cmd+K triggers no app shortcut while Enter or Escape still saves and leaves editing.
Verify a relative address starting with '/', for example /docs, is saved without an https:// prefix.

Verify pressing and releasing the pointer on the small chain icon at the element's top-right corner opens https://example.com in a new tab while /docs opens in the same tab, and clicking the link text inside the popover follows the same same-tab/new-tab rule.
Verify a URL that merely contains the app's own address, for example inside a query parameter, opens in the same tab because the app treats any address containing its own address as local.
Verify dragging from the nearby corner resize handle across the chain icon does not open the link, since the press and the release must both land on the icon.
Verify at higher and lower zoom levels the chain icon still catches clicks within a few pixels and the adjacent corner handle still resizes the element instead of opening the link.
Verify the popover is centered above the element's top edge and stays anchored there while zooming and panning the canvas.
Verify moving the pointer onto the popover or into the vertical gap between the element and the popover keeps it visible, while moving well away from both hides it automatically after a brief delay.
Verify the popover disappears while dragging, resizing, or rotating the element and reappears once the gesture ends.

Verify the Remove (trash) button appears only after a link is saved, and clicking it deletes the link and closes the popover; reselecting the element then shows no chain icon and an empty link editor.

Verify hovering the link icon of an unselected linked element shows a hand cursor and a tooltip with the link, then a full click that presses and releases on the icon opens an external link in a new browser tab and a same-site or slash-prefixed link in the current tab.
Verify pressing the icon, dragging away, and releasing elsewhere does not open the link.
Verify pressing the link icon does not select the element or start dragging it, and the element stays unselected after release.
Verify that with the linked element already selected, hovering its icon shows the link popup rather than the hover tooltip, and clicking the icon does not open the link.
Confirm clicking a linked element selects it and immediately shows the link popup, while clicking an unlinked element selects it with no popup.
Confirm dragging a selection box that ends containing exactly one linked element shows the popup, and a box containing two or more elements shows none.
Confirm exactly one popup is visible when switching selection between two linked elements, showing the newly selected element's link.
Verify that after opening the context menu and dismissing it by pressing the canvas, hovering a selected linked element shows the link popup again rather than staying hidden.
Check that while the context menu is open, hovering a selected linked element does not raise the link popup over the menu.
Verify moving the pointer from a link icon to the element body and then to empty canvas hides the tooltip, shows the move cursor over the element body, and shows the default cursor over empty canvas.
Check that hovering a linked element covered by an unlinked element on top shows no tooltip while covered, and shows the tooltip once the covering element is moved away and the icon becomes topmost.
Ensure that while editing a multi-point line or arrow, hovering its points shows the move cursor over the points and the default cursor elsewhere, where the cursor previously did not update.
Verify that after drawing a rectangle and a text label, saving the drawing, reopening it, and exporting it still preserves both elements with their position, size, and styling unchanged.

Check that while a link popup is showing above a selected shape, starting to drag or resize that shape hides the popup until you release the mouse, where no such popup existed in earlier releases, and confirm hiding it during dragging is intended.
Verify that after adding a link to an element, hovering the pointer over it shows a small external-link icon on the element, which did not appear before this release.

Confirm that with the selection tool active a shape with a web link shows a small link icon at its top-right corner on the canvas, where the previous release drew nothing, and confirm that icon is intended.

Confirm that resting the pointer on a shape with a link shows a small tooltip with the link's address just above the link icon at the shape's corner, and that shapes without a link show no such tooltip — this tooltip is new in this release, so confirm it is intended.

Confirm that the popup stays open while you move the pointer across the shape or through the gap between the shape and the popup, and only begins closing once you move clearly away from both, where no popup existed before this release, and confirm these keep-open zones are intended.

Verify that a shape given a link shows a small link icon just outside its top-right corner once it is deselected, that the icon stays pinned to that corner after the shape is rotated, and that clicking the icon opens the link — none of this existed before this release, so confirm the placement is intended.

Check that hovering a tooltip-bearing control very close to the left edge of the window keeps the whole tooltip inside the screen, where it previously could hang partly off the left edge and get clipped — confirm the new positioning is intended.

Verify that a quick click on the small link icon just above the top-right corner of a linked shape opens its web address, while clicking the shape anywhere else still selects it exactly as before this release, and confirm the icon click opening the address is intended.

Verify that moving the mouse pointer well away from a selected shape and its popup makes the popup close by itself after a brief pause, which could not happen before this release, and confirm the automatic closing is intended.

Verify that hovering a toolbar button near the right edge of a narrow window keeps the tooltip a few pixels clear of the window edge, where it previously sat flush against that edge — confirm the small gap is intended.

Confirm that selecting a single element shows a new link button in the toolbar, which was not there before this release, and that the button appears highlighted when the selected element already has a link.
Confirm that clicking the new link button in the toolbar opens the link editing popup for the selected element, where before this release no such button or popup existed.

Confirm that the popup sits horizontally centred just above the top edge of the selected shape and stays pinned there when you scroll or zoom the canvas, where earlier releases displayed nothing there, and confirm this placement is intended.

Verify that moving the pointer straight from one linked shape to another shows only the second shape's link tooltip after the usual short delay, with no leftover tooltip from the first shape — no link tooltips appeared before this release, so confirm the behavior is intended.

Check that typing an address without the https part, such as example.com, into the popup's box saves it as https://example.com with any extra spaces removed, where typing in earlier releases saved nothing, and confirm the automatic https prefix is intended.
uncertainty: The new Help-dialog shortcut row depends on the link tool's interface text being present in the translations, and the text lookup raises an error when a label is missing; if a language lacks it, the Help dialog could fail to open, so the non-English Help dialog check above is the guard.

The rule for when the context-menu link item appears is a selection predicate not included in this evidence; record exactly where it shows (single element, multi-selection, canvas) and flag any unexpected placement rather than assuming a fixed rule.

The preserved link value has no confirmed user-visible surface in this change group (the link popup, editor, and on-canvas marker ship in other changes), so the exact effect of Ctrl/Cmd+K and any tooltip timing should be re-confirmed on a build that includes the hyperlink UI; until then the key expectations are that older scenes load unchanged and nothing new renders.

The supplied context contains no affected areas, navigation details, or final label text for the new link button and menu entry, so the exact on-screen wording is unverified and should be recorded during testing.

The supplied context includes no navigation, menu, or shortcut information for this feature, so the command or key that first summons the link popover on a selected element is unconfirmed, and since the evidence contains only added lines there is no documented prior behavior to compare against; confirm the intended trigger in the running app.

Opening a link relies on a click listener attached only while the pointer hovers the link icon after a pointer move, so a direct tap on a touch device may never attach it; verify tapping a link icon on a touch device and record whether the link opens.

No specific failing input could be identified because this change is a type declaration that treats no input differently from the previous version; any visible effect would depend on code outside this group that writes or reads the new link value on elements, and the supplied evidence shows neither such code nor an affected screen.

report.summary: Text attached to shapes can now be aligned vertically to the top, middle, or bottom, and the chosen alignment is kept everywhere in the editor and in exports instead of the text always snapping back to center.
keyChanges: When a shape containing attached text is resized (single element or multi-selection) or flipped, the text's vertical position now follows its vertical alignment: top-aligned text is pinned just inside the top edge and bottom-aligned text just inside the bottom edge, where previously every such operation re-centered the text vertically; default middle-aligned text behaves exactly as before.

While editing attached text inside a shape, the on-canvas editing box is now positioned to match the text's vertical alignment (top, middle, or bottom) instead of always appearing vertically centered in the shape.

Supporting groundwork: the element data model now accepts bottom as a vertical alignment value (previously only top and middle were allowed), a new action for changing vertical text alignment was registered, and chart and element defaults were switched to a shared constant holding the identical middle value, so those defaults are unchanged.

The selection properties panel (desktop panel and mobile menu) now shows the vertical-align control only when every selected element either has text bound to it or is itself text bound to a container, so a mixed selection that includes any plain element hides the control.

Re-editing an existing bound text no longer forces its vertical alignment back to the default when the text is not at the container's center or is not center-aligned, so an alignment the user picked now survives later edits; creating brand-new text is unchanged.

When text is drawn, bottom-aligned bound text is positioned a fixed padding from the bottom of its container instead of the previous baseline-based offset; this affects the live canvas and every export path: the image export dialog preview and PNG/SVG export, copy-as-PNG/SVG, saving a file with the embedded scene image, library publish previews, and the packaged export APIs used by integrating developers.
A new vertical alignment control offering top, middle, and bottom placement is added for text bound to a shape, and choosing an option moves the text inside the shape and is recorded in undo history.

Text bound to a shape is now positioned according to that alignment: top and bottom pin the text to the corresponding edge with a small padding and no longer enlarge an undersized container, while the default middle alignment keeps the previous centered behavior including growing the container when the text is taller than it.

Because changing font size, changing font family, changing horizontal text alignment, and pasting styles all recompute the position of text bound to a shape, those existing actions now respect the chosen vertical alignment instead of always centering the text.

The horizontal text alignment control now reads the alignment from the text bound to a selected shape so it highlights the value actually in use, and the new vertical buttons share one selection group and three newly drawn icons with it.
qaChecks: Verify that resizing a shape by dragging any corner or side handle keeps top-aligned attached text pinned just inside the top edge and bottom-aligned text pinned just inside the bottom edge, where both previously slid back to the vertical middle.
Verify middle-aligned (default) attached text stays vertically centered through the same resize drags.
Verify flipping a shape with top- or bottom-aligned attached text, horizontally and then vertically, leaves the text at its aligned edge instead of re-centering it.
Verify resizing a multi-element selection that includes such shapes keeps the attached text at its aligned edge.

Verify that entering edit mode through each entry point (double-clicking the canvas, clicking into existing text, and keyboard) opens the editing box at the top of the shape for top-aligned text and at the bottom for bottom-aligned text, instead of always centered.
Verify editing middle-aligned (default) text still shows the editor vertically centered, and typing text that overflows the shape still grows the shape's height with the editor following.
Verify that bound text set to vertical alignment bottom renders hugging the bottom inside edge of its shape with a small padding on the editing canvas.

Confirm the same bottom-aligned text appears at the bottom in a PNG and an SVG exported from the image export dialog, in a copy-as-PNG clipboard image, and in a drawing saved to a file with the embedded scene image, matching what the canvas shows.
Ensure text with the default (middle) vertical alignment and standalone text elements still render in exactly the same position as before, since only the bottom-aligned case should have changed.
Verify the vertical-align control appears when selecting the shape with bound text on its own and when selecting that shape together with its bound text, on both desktop and mobile.
Check the control is hidden when the selection includes any element that neither has bound text nor is bound text itself, for example a plain rectangle with no text or a standalone text element.
Validate that choosing bottom (and top or middle if offered) immediately repositions the bound text inside the shape.

report.summary: The release makes the editor treat every incoming file the same way, inspecting the file's contents to decide whether it opens as a drawing or gets imported as a library, and it now handles unsuitable files more gracefully.
keyChanges: Dropped and opened files are now normalized before loading: when the browser supplies no file type, an .excalidraw or .excalidrawlib extension assigns the scene or library type, and supported PNG, JPEG, and GIF images are checked against their actual bytes and re-created with the correct type when the declared type disagrees.

Loading from a file is now dispatched by content: scene files restore the drawing, library files import as library items, and anything else raises the invalid-file error, while a file dropped onto the canvas now retains its file-system handle for later saving to the same file.

Reading file bytes for image identity hashing and for encrypting collaboration and shared-scene data now goes through a compatibility conversion for browsers such as Safari, so those browsers no longer risk random image identities or encryption failures.
Opening a file now goes through the shared scene-or-library loader, and any file that is not a drawing produces the existing invalid-file alert instead of attempting to restore data of unknown shape.

Opening a file through the load-scene flow now normalizes the picked file before parsing: files with no reported type get typed from their .excalidraw or .excalidrawlib extension, and image files get their type corrected from the file's actual bytes, so a scene PNG with a missing or mislabeled type should now load where it previously failed with a file-could-not-be-loaded error.

The internal helper that converts picked file data into raw bytes moved to the shared file-import code so the new type detection can reuse it; PNG scene embed and restore paths — exporting a PNG with the embedded scene, copy as PNG, opening or dropping a scene image, and resaving an image-backed drawing — now run through the relocated copy and should behave exactly as before, including its fallback path for browsers without native file reading.
The embeddable package now publicly exports the loader that accepts either a scene or a library file, for use by integrating developers.
The developer example app gained a 'Load Scene or Library' button that opens a picked file and replaces the canvas scene with its contents.
The remaining edits in this group (module imports and comments) have no runtime effect.

File opening is unified across drag-and-drop, operating-system file launch into the installed app, and share-to-app: all three now go through one loader that detects by content whether a file is a scene (loads onto the canvas) or a library (imports into the library), whereas drag-and-drop previously routed purely by file extension and MIME type and forced everything else through the scene loader.

Because detection moved from extension to content, a library file not named with the .excalidrawlib extension now imports into the library instead of failing with an invalid-file error, and a drawing saved with the .excalidrawlib extension now loads onto the canvas instead of being attempted as a library import.
Dropping a library file no longer opens the library panel automatically as it did before; the items are still imported and appear once the library is opened.

The file handle that lets the editor remember an opened file is now captured once, at the moment the file is dropped or launched, and passed through the loader instead of being attached in several separate places.
For developers embedding the editor, the package now publicly exposes the MIME type constants and the unified scene/library loader function.

uncertainty: The evidence contains no prior version of the file-type normalization and mime-sniffing logic (all of it appears as new code), so the exact previously failing or passing inputs cannot be confirmed; the typeless .excalidraw file and the mismatched-type image above are the probes most likely to expose a regression, and any failure there should be compared against a pre-change build.

The new example button feeds both scene and library files through the same scene-update call, so loading a .excalidrawlib file may not import it as a library; its behaviour for library files is unverified and should be observed during testing.

A file arriving via share-to-app is rebuilt without its original filename, so recognition depends entirely on the file's MIME type; if the sharing app sends a missing or generic type, the import may fail - worth checking that such a shared file still loads or shows a clear error.

report.summary: This release reworks how lines and arrows are selected and edited on the drawing canvas, so their points can now be adjusted directly from a normal selection instead of a separate editing mode.
keyChanges: Selecting a single arrow or line now shows a small circle at each of its points instead of the rectangular selection box, and arrows and lines no longer offer any corner or rotation handles; before this change, a two-point line kept one corner pair plus the rotation handle, and an arrow or line with three or more points showed the full handle set.

Hovering a point of a selected arrow or line now draws a translucent purple highlight circle with no outline at that point, and the selection box is no longer drawn while dragging a single selected arrow or line (it used to stay visible).

Line point handles were recolored from red to purple and selected points from pink-red to light purple, and in line point-editing mode the point circles are now exactly twice their previous size (selection-mode circles keep the old half size).

A new editor state field records which arrow or line is selected and which of its points is hovered; it starts empty, is kept across browser reloads, and is stripped from exported files and collaboration sync, so exports and collaborators should not show the new selection UI.
Freehand drawings and shapes such as rectangles keep their previous selection box and handle behavior.

Selecting a single line or arrow now immediately shows its point handles and lets the pointer drag endpoints and midpoints directly, without the separate line-editing mode previously required; hovering over a point shows a pointer cursor and over the line body a move cursor.

Releasing a dragged point of a selected arrow now re-evaluates its shape connections: dragging an endpoint onto or off a shape binds or unbinds the arrow at release, which previously only happened in the edit mode.

Linear-element selection is now tracked and kept in sync: right-clicking an unselected arrow selects it with handles, box-selecting exactly one line or arrow activates it, selecting several elements hides the handles, and deselecting clears any leftover handles.

While a line or arrow is selected, hit testing changes: selected elements are no longer grabbed anywhere inside their bounding box, so clicks off the actual shape fall through to whatever is underneath, affecting picking, erasing, context menu, and double-click targeting.

The multi-point drawing routine was reparameterized with no intended behavior change, but the whole drawing flow now shares the new selection state, so continuous multi-point line drawing needs a regression pass.
Finishing a multi-point line or arrow now leaves the finished shape selected in point-handle mode instead of deselecting it; pencil (freedraw) strokes are excluded and behave as before.

Select All now explicitly controls point-handle selection: with exactly one line or arrow in the drawing it opens in point-handle mode, and with several elements it clears any lingering point selection (previously the old state was left untouched).
Locking selected elements now exits point-handle selection on a locked line or arrow; unlocking keeps the current selection as before.

Point handles on selected lines and arrows are drawn at half the previous size (10 instead of 20), while the clickable and hover area around each point stays the same at 11 pixels, so click precision should feel unchanged.

Point clicking and dragging was refactored to run from the stored line selection: dragging a point now works as soon as the line is selected (previously it required the dedicated point-edit mode), and alt-click to add a point still applies only in point-edit mode.

Verify that exporting the scene as an image while an arrow is selected produces a picture containing no point handles, highlight circles, or selection boxes.

Check that hovering exactly over one of the arrow's points shows a pointer cursor, hovering over the middle of the line shows a move cursor, and hovering away from the line restores the normal cursor.
Verify that dragging an endpoint of the selected arrow moves only that point and reshapes the arrow live rather than dragging the whole arrow.
Test dragging from the middle of a segment of the selected arrow and confirm the segment follows the pointer as a reshaped point while the rest of the arrow stays in place.
Verify that dragging the free endpoint of the selected arrow onto a rectangle and releasing connects the arrow to that shape and its end follows when the rectangle is dragged afterwards.
Confirm that dragging an attached endpoint of the selected arrow away from its rectangle and releasing disconnects it, so the arrow no longer follows the rectangle when the rectangle is moved.

Verify that clicking a spot inside the selected arrow's bounding area but clearly off its drawn stroke, such as the empty middle of the V, no longer grabs the arrow and instead selects the element underneath or nothing.
Confirm that clicking directly on the arrow's stroke still grabs and drags it, and that clicking inside the bounding box of a selected non-arrow shape still grabs that shape as before.
Ensure that with the arrow selected, running the eraser across the empty bounding area of the overlapping rectangle erases only content actually under the eraser path.
Verify that right-clicking an unselected arrow opens the context menu and that, once the menu is closed, the arrow is selected with its point handles shown.

Check that box-selecting the arrow together with a rectangle hides the arrow's point handles while several elements are selected, and that shift-clicking the rectangle to leave only the arrow selected brings the handles back.
Ensure that deselecting everything by clicking empty canvas or pressing Escape clears any leftover point handles from arrows.

Verify that drawing a multi-point line by clicking successive points, including the variant with Alt held to add points continuously, extends points following the pointer and finalizes on release with no stray leftover point at the end.

Verify that finishing a multi-point arrow (several click-placed segments) leaves the arrow selected with visible point handles, and that immediately pressing on an endpoint and dragging reshapes only that point instead of moving the whole arrow.

Verify that with an arrow merely selected (single click, not in point-edit mode), pressing on an endpoint and dragging moves just that point, while pressing on the arrow body away from the points still drags the whole arrow.
Verify that completing a pencil stroke leaves it selected as a normal shape with no point handles, matching the previous behavior.
Verify that in point-edit mode (entered by double-clicking a line) alt-clicking still adds a new point at the cursor.
Verify that point handles on a selected line or arrow render visibly smaller than before (half the previous size) and that clicking within the old, larger handle area still grabs the point.
Verify that hovering over a point shows the pointer cursor and that moving off the point onto the line restores the move cursor.
Verify that in a drawing containing exactly one line, Select All (Ctrl+A) selects the line in point-handle mode.
Verify that with several elements, Select All selects everything as a normal multi-selection with no point handles, and dragging moves all selected elements together.
Verify that locking the selected arrow exits point-handle mode (handles disappear and points cannot be dragged) while the element itself stays selected.
Verify the locked arrow cannot be moved until unlocked, and unlocking restores normal selection behavior.

Confirm that after dragging a selected arrow's endpoint dot onto the edge of a rectangle and releasing, later dragging the rectangle carries the arrow's end along with it instead of leaving the arrow disconnected.

Check that selecting a single arrow now shows only its point markers where the black rectangle border used to be drawn around it, and that the border also stays hidden while you drag the arrow across the canvas, and confirm both are intended.
Confirm that with an arrow selected, hovering over one of its endpoint dots changes the cursor to a pointer and moving off the dot onto the middle of the line switches it back to the move cursor.

Check that dragging a selection box around a single arrow and releasing shows the arrow's point handles right away, instead of the old behavior where the arrow was selected without handles until you double-clicked it.
Confirm

Verify that moving the pointer over one of the points of a selected arrow makes a soft translucent purple circle appear at that point, where nothing similar appeared before this release, and confirm the hover highlight is intended.

Verify that after selecting an arrow with a single click, pressing and dragging one of its endpoint dots moves that point and reshapes the arrow, instead of the old behavior where a selected arrow could only be moved as a whole.

Confirm that when a single arrow or line is selected, the round rotation handle that used to sit above its outline is no longer shown, and confirm that removing the rotation handle from selected arrows and lines is intended.

Check that when an arrow is selected and its point handles are showing, shift-clicking that same arrow to remove it from the selection makes the point handles disappear too, instead of leaving them on the now-unselected arrow.

Confirm that double-clicking an arrow to edit its points now shows the point markers in purple and noticeably larger than before, with a selected marker turning light purple instead of the previous red, and confirm the new colours and size are intended.

Verify that after selecting an arrow with a single click, moving the mouse over the arrow's line shows the move cursor, whereas before this release that cursor only appeared after double-clicking the arrow to enter its edit mode.

Confirm that the translucent purple circle that appears when you hover over a point of a selected arrow is a plain filled disc without an outline ring, unlike the outlined circles drawn elsewhere, and confirm the missing outline is intended.

Verify that selecting a line no longer shows the two small square resize handles at opposite corners of its outline that could previously be dragged to resize it, and confirm that resizing a line is now meant to happen only by dragging its point markers.
Confirm that right-clicking an arrow that is not selected selects it and immediately shows its point handles, instead of selecting it with no handles as before.

Check that a drawing saved with the previous version opens with nothing selected and no point markers anywhere, just as it did before, and confirm that the new empty default for the arrow-selection slot is intended.
uncertainty: The new selection state is saved to browser storage even though it stores transient details such as the currently hovered point; if a hovered point index gets persisted, reloading could show the purple highlight circle on a line right after startup without any pointer interaction, and whether that is intended is unresolved.

It is not established from the evidence whether dragging the body of a selected arrow still moves the entire arrow as plain selection dragging did before this change, because those clicks now go through the new point-editing path; verify whole-arrow moving explicitly.

Select All decides it is a single-line selection by checking the first element in the drawing rather than the selected one; if the only selectable element is not first in the drawing (for example, a locked line drawn before an unlocked rectangle), the point-handle selection may attach to the wrong element, so one exploratory Select All check with a locked element drawn first is worthwhile.

Verify that after selecting an arrow with a single click, pressing and dragging one of its endpoint dots moves that point and reshapes the arrow, instead of the old behavior where a selected arrow could only be moved as a whole.

Confirm that when a single arrow or line is selected, the round rotation handle that used to sit above its outline is no longer shown, and confirm that removing the rotation handle from selected arrows and lines is intended.

checks: Check that when an arrow is selected and its point handles are showing, shift-clicking that same arrow to remove it from the selection makes the point handles disappear too, instead of leaving them on the now-unselected arrow.

Confirm that double-clicking an arrow to edit its points now shows the point markers in purple and noticeably larger than before, with a selected marker turning light purple instead of the previous red, and confirm the new colours and size are intended.

Verify that after selecting an arrow with a single click, moving the mouse over the arrow's line shows the move cursor, whereas before this release that cursor only appeared after double-clicking the arrow to enter its edit mode.

Confirm that the translucent purple circle that appears when you hover over a point of a selected arrow is a plain filled disc without an outline ring, unlike the outlined circles drawn elsewhere, and confirm the missing outline is intended.

checks: Verify that selecting a line no longer shows the two small square resize handles at opposite corners of its outline that could previously be dragged to resize it, and confirm that resizing a line is now meant to happen only by dragging its point markers.
Confirm that right-clicking an arrow that is not selected selects it and immediately shows its point handles, instead of selecting it with no handles as before.

Check that a drawing saved with the previous version opens with nothing selected and no point markers anywhere, just as it did before, and confirm that the new empty default for the arrow-selection slot is intended.

moreChecks: Verify that with an arrow selected, clicking an empty area inside its invisible bounding box where another shape sits underneath selects that underlying shape instead of grabbing the selected arrow by its bounding box.

Verify that after selecting an arrow with the selection tool and refreshing the browser tab, the arrow is still selected with its point markers showing, whereas before this release the selection was always cleared by a reload, and confirm that remembering the selection is intended.

Check that selecting a single arrow now shows only its point markers where the black rectangle border used to be drawn around it, and that the border also stays hidden while you drag the arrow across the canvas, and confirm both are intended.
Confirm that with an arrow selected, hovering over one of its endpoint dots changes the cursor to a pointer and moving off the dot onto the middle of the line switches it back to the move cursor.

Check that dragging a selection box around a single arrow and releasing shows the arrow's point handles right away, instead of the old behavior where the arrow was selected without handles until you double-clicked it.
